# Goal

Close out the observational acceptance criteria of **LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM** (false `saturated` capacity signal) once the new proxy code is running on `dev`.

## Background

The gate-side fix (commits 56a3a28a, 2d2b6b51) makes `/llama/local/status` truthful: stale slot detail degrades `capacity_hint` to `idle` (never `saturated`) without live work; `local_active_query` is derived from active dispatch records; an unloaded model (HTTP 400/404 from llama-server's router `/slots?model=`) is treated as fresh absence (fail open on the pool); and `local_prefills_in_flight` publishes only markers backed by a live record.

What cannot be verified inside the implementation session is the overnight behaviour.

## Problem statement

The capacity-signal fix is merged, but its real-world effect on the overnight herdr downtime dispatcher and on `/llama/local/status` staleness is unmeasured. Without a post-fix measurement over a comparable night window we cannot confirm the false-`saturated` starvation is resolved.

## Users

- **Operator/maintainer of the local LLM proxy** — needs confidence that overnight idle GPU capacity is actually used by the herdr downtime dispatcher.
  - As the operator, I want the post-fix `slots_stale` poll rate to be well under the pre-fix 79.5% so I know status is truthful.
  - As the operator, I want herdr downtime dispatches on an idle night to return to the Oct 20/21 baseline (>=10/night) so idle GPU time is not wasted.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: Over a night window comparable to 2026-10-22 (20:00-07:00 local), `slots_stale` is <5% of status polls (was 79.5%), and `capacity_hint=saturated` is only observed while the proxy has live local work.
- AC2: herdr downtime dispatches on a genuinely idle GPU night reach the Oct 20/21 baseline (>=10 dispatches/night) with the same work-item queue (was 1 in ~9 h).
- AC3: Any residual stale polls are attributable (documented cause, e.g. transient /slots 500 vs idle-model unload) in the nightly usage report.
- AC4: Report the measured numbers on LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM and close this item.
- AC5: The measurement is reproducible/validated — the derivation of each reported figure (poll counts, `slots_stale` rate, `capacity_hint` distribution, dispatch count) is documented with the exact log files and commands/logic used, so a reviewer can re-derive the numbers.
- AC6: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries — specifically the nightly usage report and `proxy/docs/per-slot-status-verification.md` reflect the post-fix findings.
- AC7: Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Read-only measurement work: do not change proxy behaviour or dispatch logic in this item.
- Window is fixed: 2026-10-24 20:00 → 2026-10-25 07:00 IST (Europe/Dublin); the fix was live from ~10:35 IST on 2026-10-24.
- Evidence lives in `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log.*` and `~/proxy-usage-reports/`; use the nightly usage report where available rather than ad-hoc parsing where the report already covers it.
- Never kill the proxy to collect evidence; use logs only.

## Existing state

Pre-fix evidence (2026-10-22 night): `slots_stale=true` on 7,543 of 9,484 polls (79.5%); `capacity_hint=saturated` on 7,807 of 9,484 polls (82.3%); 100% of 02:00/03:00 polls saturated while zero local streams ran; herdr dispatched 1 work item in ~9 h vs 14–15/night on Oct 20/21.

## Desired change

Post-fix measurement over the fixed window, recorded as a report: `slots_stale` poll rate (<5% target), `capacity_hint` distribution while idle (saturated only with live work), herdr downtime dispatch count (>=10 target), and attribution of any residual stale polls. Findings reported on the parent item LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log.*` — primary evidence: status polls, `slots_stale`, `capacity_hint`, dispatch records for the window.
- `~/proxy-usage-reports/report.md` — nightly usage report output (per-day directories) used as the canonical report surface.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py` — deterministic analyzer for proxy usage/error taxonomy.
- `proxy/docs/per-slot-status-verification.md` — status contract to reconcile observed `capacity_hint`/`slots_stale` semantics.
- Parent item `LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM` — destination for the reported numbers.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** proxy logs for the full window are retained (confirmed present: `proxy.log.2026-10-24_22`, `proxy.log-2026-10-25_00`, `proxy.log`).
- **Assumption:** herdr downtime dispatch counts are reconstructable from proxy logs/or herdr decision logs.
- **Risk:** residual stale polls may be un-attributable if log detail is insufficient — AC3 requires documenting cause, or explicitly stating the cause could not be determined.
- **Scope-creep risk:** any new defect found during measurement (e.g. a distinct status bug) should be filed as a linked work item, not fixed here.

## Related work

- Parent fix: LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM (discovered-from)
- Evidence window: `~/proxy-usage-reports/report.md` (2026-10-23 05:00 run), `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log.*`
- Status contract: `proxy/docs/per-slot-status-verification.md`

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MRB29PP60012UYF** – Bug: Stale Local Dispatch Lease Blocks Subsequent Local Requests (completed)
- **LP-0MTYL5K1S002M5QL** – Reclaim stale generating counters in cleanup loop (completed)
- **LP-0MRNV040H0055N2Q** – [test-failure] test_stub_router_integration — flaky test-ordering-dependent assert ok Failure (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, acceptance (+90 more)
- `proxy/README.md` — matched: 0mvksxr4p001v0cm, ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4 (+89 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts.txt` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, acceptance (+85 more)

## Plan

Decomposed into three dependency-ordered children (test-first: verification tooling before measurement, documentation/close-out last). Effort/risk on this item: **Small / Medium** (approval gate not triggered). All seven acceptance criteria are mapped to a child AC.

| # | Child | Type | Depends on | Covers parent ACs |
|---|-------|------|-----------|-------------------|
| 1 | `LP-0MVOG6YRA000T9PK` — Capacity-signal verification tool: reproducible window metrics | task (verification, test-first) | — | AC5 (+AC7 test part) |
| 2 | `LP-0MVOG7IP80003MLV` — Measure post-fix night window: stale rate, capacity_hint, dispatch count | task | 1 | AC1, AC2, AC3 |
| 3 | `LP-0MVOG7IX6006MZ23` — Publish report, update docs, verify suite, close measurement | task | 2 | AC4, AC6, AC7 |

### Reuse (no new wheel)

- `scripts/lib/proxy_logs.py` — rotation/gzip-aware log discovery (dot + dash names, `.gz`), per-line window filtering, and a coverage verdict that fails on gaps.
- `scripts/dispatch_latency_verification.py` — the established pattern for a reproducible window verification tool (`--since/--until/--json`, verdicts, exit codes, documented derivations).
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py` — reference only (agent infrastructure; not edited).

### Evidence coverage (verified during planning)

The fixed window 2026-10-24 20:00 → 2026-10-25 07:00 IST is fully covered by rotated logs: `proxy.log.2026-10-24_17.gz` (20:00→23:37), `proxy.log-2026-10-25_00` (23:37→23:59), `proxy.log.2026-10-24_22` (00:00→04:37), `proxy.log.2026-10-25_04` (04:37→07:00). `slots_stale` lines are present in the window files (e.g. 5,325 matches in `proxy.log.2026-10-24_22`).

### Phasing

Each child is a vertical slice: the tool child delivers script + unit tests + docstring derivation; the measurement child delivers numbers + artifacts; the close-out child delivers report + docs + suite gate. The plan needs no further phasing.

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-25 (plan skill, Map): created children LP-0MVOG6YRA000T9PK, LP-0MVOG7IP80003MLV, LP-0MVOG7IX6006MZ23; wired deps 2→1 and 3→2; restated parent ACs literally in child ACs to satisfy the AC-coverage review (Jaccard ≥ 0.4, coverage 100%); verified log coverage for the fixed window; stage → `plan_complete`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Was the item sufficiently defined to skip the intake interview?" — Answer (Map, agent): "Yes — the item already had a clear goal, background, four measurable ACs and references, and is a small `task`. Per intake Step 1 heuristics it qualified for auto-complete; no interview questions were required." Source: `wl show LP-0MVLNBCTN0084MT0 --json` inspection at intake.

- Q: "Is the exact log source / file-to-window mapping for `slots_stale` and `capacity_hint` known?" — Answer (Map, agent, resolved from evidence rather than by asking): "Yes. Rotated files map to the window as recorded in the Plan section; `slots_stale` appears in the window files. The plan therefore includes a coverage verdict in the tool so a gap can never read as a partial success." Evidence: `zcat -f /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log.* | grep -c slots_stale` over the 2026-10-22 and 2026-10-24/25 files; first/last timestamps of each file.
- Q: "Should the derivation be a new tool or ad-hoc parsing?" — Answer (Map, agent): "New reproducible tool at `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py`, because parent AC5 requires re-derivable figures; reuse `scripts/lib/proxy_logs.py` (discovery/coverage) and follow `scripts/dispatch_latency_verification.py`. The tool is validated by reproducing the pre-fix 2026-10-22 baseline (79.5% stale / 82.3% saturated) as a control."
- Q: "Where do the post-fix findings get recorded?" — Answer (Map, agent): "Numbers + attribution on LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM (parent AC4), plus `proxy/docs/per-slot-status-verification.md` and the nightly usage report for the window (parent AC6)."

### OPEN QUESTION (directed to: operator; matters for parent AC6 scope)

The nightly usage report is produced by `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/` (agent infrastructure). Parent AC6 says the nightly report must "reflect the post-fix findings". If that requires adding `slots_stale` rate / `capacity_hint` distribution to the report generator itself, that is a change under `.pi/`, which the repository-boundary rule forbids without explicit instruction. Default plan: document the findings in `~/proxy-usage-reports/` content for the window and in `proxy/docs/per-slot-status-verification.md`; if the generator needs changing, the close-out child records it as an Open Question and files a separate work item rather than editing `.pi/` unilaterally.

### Assumptions recorded during planning

- The pre-fix control window (2026-10-22 20:00→07:00) is deliberately re-measured by the same tool; a mismatch beyond the documented tolerance means the method is wrong, not that the fix failed.
- "Live local work" for the saturated-with-live-work check is derived from proxy dispatch records in the same logs (active dispatch windows), not from GPU metrics.
- herdr downtime dispatch count is derivable from proxy logs; if it is not, the measurement child must state the limitation explicitly (parent AC3 allows "could not be determined").

## Goal (user story)

As a maintainer, I want the proxy's own request-budget skip to use a name that
cannot be confused with an upstream rate-limit rejection, so operators and
analysis tooling stop misreading `rate_limited` as "the local model was rate
limited".

## Why

`rate_limited` is emitted by `proxy/proxy/provider_budget.py` when a provider
entry's configured `rate_limit_rpm` window is exhausted
(`BudgetDecision(reason="rate_limited")`). It is a **proxy-side, pre-flight
budget skip**, not an HTTP 429 from the provider — upstream 429s are logged
separately as `[remote] upstream error status=429` /
`upstream_http_error`.

The name caused a concrete misreading: `rate_limited` is 61.6% of the
fallback-reason table (6,042 events, all `from=munitoai-free`), yet it was
reported as the per-session "reason for remote fallback" for 11 of 26
sessions that had actually been diverted from local by lease contention. The
local provider has no `rate_limit_rpm` and can never emit this reason (0 of
9,683 archive occurrences are `from=local`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The budget-skip vocabulary is renamed to
  `provider_budget_exhausted`, everywhere it is emitted: the
  `BudgetDecision.reason` values in `proxy/proxy/provider_budget.py`
  (retaining the `_after_wait` / `_waiters` / `_disconnect` variants, e.g.
  `provider_budget_exhausted_after_wait`), the `reason=` text in the
  `Provider budget exhausted: skipping provider=...` log lines, the
  `fallback_reason = ...` assignments in `proxy/proxy/provider.py`
  (~9028, ~10515), **and the diagnostics attempt `status` values**
  `status="rate_limited"` / `status="rate_limited_waited"` (~9018, ~9038,
  ~10505, ~10525) -> `status="provider_budget_exhausted"` /
  `status="provider_budget_exhausted_waited"`. Producer decision
  (2026-10-25): *full rename everywhere* — no `rate_limited*` literal may
  remain in **newly emitted** code paths, tests, or current documentation.
  The analysis-skill legacy mapping (AC3) and `REFERENCE.md` deliberately
  retain the old spelling as a *historical* name (exactly as
  `warm_cache_bypass` is retained next to `context_too_large`).
- AC2: Internal decisions/behaviour are unchanged: the affinity/reserve/wait
  logic and any cooldown behaviour keep working (the rename must not alter
  decisions — it is a string rename only). `_BUDGET_SKIP_STATUSES` is updated
  to key on the new status (`frozenset({"provider_budget_exhausted"})`,
  provider.py ~4181); `status_code=429` in the diagnostic attempt entries
  stays as-is (a numeric HTTP code, not the reason vocabulary); the
  reason-keyed budget-evidence gate `(reason or "").startswith("rate_limited")`
  (~669) switches to the new prefix.
- AC3: The usage-analysis skill normalises legacy logs: `log_parser.py` maps
  `rate_limited*` -> `provider_budget_exhausted*` so historical windows and
  new windows report under one label, with the mapping documented in
  `REFERENCE.md` (add to the existing legacy reason mapping next to
  `warm_cache_bypass` -> `context_too_large`).
- AC4: `reporting.py` renders the new label and keeps the reason table stable
  (no duplicate rows for old/new names in one window);
  `recommendations.py` text that references rate limiting is updated to
  distinguish proxy budget pacing from upstream 429s. Paths verified at plan
  time: `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/reporting.py` (legend at
  ~line 545) and `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/recommendations.py`
  (~lines 478, 544, 731).
- AC5: Tests: parser normalisation tests (old and new spellings) in
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/`; every test that asserts the old

  `proxy/tests/test_chain_hold_budget_window.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_munitoai_budget_eval_parse.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_quota_surge_bypass.py`, `proxy/tests/test_quota_state.py`,

  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py`,
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/fixtures.py`,
  `tests/test_idle_admit_impact.py`.
  `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py` and

  With the full rename the attempt-`status` assertions also move:

- AC6: Other log consumers audited/updated:

  `proxy/benchmarks/contention_queue_profile.py`,
  `.worklog/analysis/extract_metrics.py`. Historical artifacts are

- AC7: `REFERENCE.md` documents the vocabulary split (proxy budget skip vs
  upstream HTTP 429) so the two are never conflated again.
- AC8: Full suite passes via the test skill.
- AC9: Current documentation examples that show the reason *or* attempt-status

## Notes

- **Deferral cleared:** renaming alone does not fix mis-attribution, it only

## Implementation notes (verified at plan time)

- `proxy/proxy/provider_budget.py` carries all four reason variants —

- `scripts/slot-persistence-correlate.py:80` is a comment describing field

- `proxy/proxy/ui.py` renders raw log lines — display sanity check only.
- Test-function names carrying the old vocabulary (rename with the change;

- Test-first order: (1) parser normalisation tests (old + new spellings) in

**Key Files:**

- `proxy/proxy/provider_budget.py` — all four `BudgetDecision.reason` values and their log lines.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `fallback_reason` assignments (~9028, ~10515), reason-keyed evidence gate (~669), `_BUDGET_SKIP_STATUSES` (~4181), docstrings.

- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py` — parser/analysis assertions.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- ~~OPEN QUESTION 1~~ **ANSWERED (producer/Map, 2026-10-25): "full rename

  Q: Does the rename cover only the emitted *reason* value, or also the

  Alternative: rename the status vocabulary too (`provider_budget_exhausted`

  the status assertions in `test_provider_budget.py` (~1187),
  `test_chain_hold_budget_window.py` (~75, ~169),
  `test_quota_surge_bypass.py` (~357), `test_quota_state.py` (~360) and the
  `status:` examples in `proxy/README.md` / `proxy/docs/routing.md` /

- Q: `AC5` listed `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py` and

data.title: Rename budget-skip reason rate_limited to provider_budget_exhausted

data.description:
## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want local prompt-eval (prefill) throughput increased so that
large cold prompts become cheap enough to serve locally, unlocking real local
utilisation instead of diverting work to paid remote providers.

## GATING PRECONDITION — do not start before this is met

**This item must only be executed once we have had a successful night of local
LLM consumption, meaning >60% GPU utilisation across a full night.** Until
local actually carries sustained work (>60% local busy), tuning prefill
throughput is premature: there is no sustained workload to measure against and
no evidence that prefill latency — rather than routing policy — is the binding
constraint. Verify the gate with the `proxy-usage-analysis` report's
`## Local model utilization` section for a night window (e.g. 22:00-07:00):
it must show busy >= 60%. Record that evidence in a comment on this item
before starting work; if the gate is not met, leave the item blocked.

## Why (current evidence, for context once the gate is met)

- Prompt-eval speed (llama-server eval timing, Qwen3, fast bucket): median
  **90.7 tok/s**, p90 316.7, p10 24.9 (532 samples, 24h window
  2026-10-23 10:52 -> 2026-10-24 10:52).
- Per-stream prefill (dispatch -> first byte): p50 4.4s, p90 35.3s, max 73.7s.
- `local_prefill_deadline_seconds: 90` — a slow prefill can be cancelled, and
  prior incidents show cancelled prefills re-dispatching identical prompts
  (the prefill-thrash cooldown exists because of this).
- The prefill-ETA admission guard refused **478** local admissions in the
  window on projected prefill cost, and only **34** requests were admitted by
  the idle override despite local being idle 89.8% of the time.
- Current llama-server launch flags (Qwen3 child):
  `--ctx-size 262144 --parallel 2 --batch-size 8192 --ubatch-size 1024
  --cache-ram 40960 --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0
  --swa-checkpoints 32 --no-mmap -ngl 80 --threads 8`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC0 (GATE): A comment on this item records the measured >60% GPU utilisation
  for a full night, taken from the usage-analysis report, before any change is
  made. Work does not start without it.
- AC1: A measured baseline is captured first: prompt-eval tok/s distribution
  (p10/p50/p90), prefill phase duration, prefill-ETA admission refusals, and
  prefill-thrash events over a fixed window, all from the
  `proxy-usage-analysis` artifacts.
- AC2: Prefill throughput is improved by tuning the llama-server launch
  configuration (candidates: `--ubatch-size` 1024 -> 2048/4096, `--batch-size`,
  `--mlock`, thread count, SWA/checkpoint settings) and/or the prefill-related
  proxy knobs (`local_prefill_deadline_seconds`, the ETA guard budget). Each
  changed value is justified by measurement, not by guesswork.
- AC3: The optimisation is measured with the same method as AC1 and the
  before/after comparison is recorded on this item, including any effect on
  decode speed (no regression to decode tok/s median) and on stability
  (`slot_save failed`, prefill cancellations, HTTP 400/503 rates).
- AC4: If a knob change affects the prefill-ETA guard's behaviour, the guard's
  configuration and documentation are updated together, and the
  `local_prefill_deadline_seconds` / ETA interactions are documented.
- AC5: The usage-analysis skill is updated if new or changed log evidence is
  needed to measure the improvement
  (`.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/{llama_log_parser.py,log_parser.py,
  reporting.py}`, `REFERENCE.md`), and any other log-consuming script that
  reads llama-server eval timings or prefill evidence is audited
  (`proxy/scripts/replay_prefill_occupancy.py`,
  `scripts/prefill_recovery_verification.py`,
  `scripts/prefill_lease_verification.py`).
- AC6: Launch-flag changes are documented in `models.ini` / start-proxy
  documentation so the settings are reproducible, and any start-proxy script
  or test asserting the flags is updated.
- AC7: Full suite passes via the test skill.

## Notes

- This item is downstream of routing policy: raising local demand (thresholds,
  serve-first admission) comes first, otherwise there is nothing to optimise
  for. Keep the gate.
- Related: LP-0MSAOQTJS000FFVM (evaluate increasing local ctx-size) and the
  slot-geometry experiment (1 slot vs 2) — decide ctx/slot geometry before
  micro-tuning batch sizes, since the two interact.

## Plan (2026-10-25)

Decomposed into nine children. Every change-making child is dependency-blocked
on the **gate child** (LP-0MVNBJWG6006Z7YQ, *Verify sustained local utilisation gate*) and on the gated geometry experiment
(LP-0MVMHNUXW0061FGN), so nothing starts before AC0 is satisfied. This item
itself depends on the gate child and therefore renders as `blocked`.

| # | Child | Covers | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Verify sustained local utilisation gate (LP-0MVNBJWG6006Z7YQ) | AC0 | — |
| 2 | Baseline prefill measurement capture (LP-0MVNBJWRH006V9Y6) | AC1 | 1 |
| 3 | 40-80k prefill benchmark capability (LP-0MVNBJX3G008IBTB) | AC2 (measurement validity) | 1, LP-0MVMHNUXW0061FGN |
| 4 | Measurement evidence and log-consumer audit (LP-0MVNBJXF9002DJAZ) | AC5 | 1, 2 |
| 5 | Launch-flag A/B: ubatch and batch size (LP-0MVNBJXR6002OSPD) | AC2 | 1, 2, 3, LP-0MVMHNUXW0061FGN |
| 6 | Launch-flag A/B: threads and SWA checkpoints (LP-0MVNBJY2R004EZ51) | AC2 | 1, 5 |
| 7 | ETA-guard and prefill-deadline interaction review (LP-0MVNBJYE3003MF6J) | AC2 (proxy knobs), AC4 | 1, 2, 5, 6 |
| 8 | Post-change verification: latency and stability (LP-0MVNBJYPM004UV56) | AC3, AC7 | 1, 2, 5, 6, 7 |
| 9 | Document launch flags and reproducibility (LP-0MVNBJZ100020UN0) | AC6 | 1, 5, 6 |

Sequence: gate -> baseline + harness capability (test-first) -> launch-flag
A/B -> guard review -> post-change verification + docs. Each child is a
vertical slice carrying its own tests, config/docs change and measurement
record.

Vertical-slice decision: the change is deliberately **not** phased into
separate "code" and "docs" phases; each A/B child lands flag + test + comment
together, because an undocumented or untested flag change is not deliverable.

**Effort/risk (this plan):** Medium (`recommended 51.22 h`, range 33.3-76.0 h)
/ **Medium** (score 10). Estimate source: `effort-and-risk` skill with this
plan's per-child WBS; it replaces the `0.00 h` autoplan placeholder recorded
earlier.

**Gate status at planning time:** NOT met (busy 2.2 % for the night
2026-10-23 22:00 -> 2026-10-24 07:00; 10.2 % over the 24 h daily report).
Children that change configuration must not start until AC0 is satisfied.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

Answered by repository / work-item evidence (non-interactive planning run):

- Q: "Is the AC0 gate (>60 % local busy for a full night) met?" - Answer
  (evidence: `proxy-usage-analysis` CLI + `~/proxy-usage-reports/report.md`):
  **No.** 2.2 % busy for 2026-10-23 22:00 -> 2026-10-24 07:00 (719 s of
  32 400 s, 27 streams, prefill 336 slot-s, decode 383 slot-s); 10.2 % for the
  24 h window 2026-10-23 10:52 -> 2026-10-24 10:52. Source: CLI run recorded in
  the pre-check comment (`/tmp/wl-gate-check`).
- Q: "Has micro-batch tuning already been attempted, and with what result?"

data.description:
## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want a measured comparison of **1 llama-server slot with
262,144 ctx** versus **2 slots with 131,072 ctx each**, so we can choose the
geometry that maximises local work served without unacceptable queueing.

## GATING PRECONDITION — do not start before this is met

**This experiment can only be carried out when we have a full night of GPU use
(>60% busy).** With local currently at ~10% busy, a 1-vs-2 slot comparison
measures noise, not saturation: the trade-off only shows up when demand
actually contends for slots. Verify the gate with the
`proxy-usage-analysis` report's `## Local model utilization` section for a
complete night window: busy must be >= 60% for the full night. Record that
evidence in a comment on this item before starting; if the gate is not met,
leave the item blocked.

## Why (current evidence, for context once the gate is met)

- Current geometry: `--parallel 2` with `--ctx-size 262144` = **131,072 tokens
  per slot**.
- Measured concurrency: **avg 1.04 while busy, peak 2** — demand is nearly
  serial today, so 2 slots are rarely both used.
- The routing hard cap (`local_large_context_warm_cache_threshold: 120000`)
  sits just under the 131K per-slot limit. In the 24h window **2,064 requests
  were skipped as `context_too_large`** (estimated > 120K), including 105
  skips from sessions that were already warm (cache ratio 0.92-1.00, only ~4K
  new tokens, total 126K-137K). A single 262K slot would move that ceiling
  from ~120K to ~258K.
- Local was idle **89.8%** of the window, serving only 225 turns across 26
  sessions, so spare capacity is not the current constraint — but slot
  geometry determines what will be servable once demand is raised.

## Hypothesis to test

- **1 x 262K**: ~2x per-slot context → far fewer `context_too_large` skips and
  larger conversations stay local; cost: requests serialise when two sessions
  overlap (today: peak 2, avg 1.04, so the cost may be small).
- **2 x 131K**: current state; parallel but capped at ~120K per request; the
  evidence above shows warm sessions being cut off at the cap.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC0 (GATE): A comment records the measured >60% GPU busy for a full night
  from the usage-analysis report, before any configuration change.
- AC1: A repeatable measurement protocol is defined and written on this item:
  identical workload window length, same metrics, same report tooling for both
  arms.
- AC2: Arm A (2 x 131K, current) and Arm B (1 x 262K) are each run for a
  comparable period at the gate, with llama-server `--parallel` / `--ctx-size`
  changed together (and `session_slot_pool_size` plus the warm/cold thresholds
  adjusted consistently, since per-slot ctx and slot count interact — see
  LP-0MSAZXXDY005AWA1 / LP-0MSI2M5BT004BCDP on the band collapsing to zero
  width).
- AC3: Results compare, for each arm: local busy %, turns served locally,
  requests diverted per fallback reason (especially `context_too_large` and
  `large_context_bypass`), queue wait / `fallback_after_queue` counts, time to
  first token, prefill and decode phase slot-seconds, and any errors
  (`slot_save failed`, HTTP 400/503).
- AC4: A decision is recorded on this item: keep 2 slots, move to 1 slot, or
  make it mode-dependent, with the data that justifies it. If 1 slot wins, the
  follow-on config change is filed (or implemented if in scope).
- AC5: Findings feed the configuration documentation (`models.ini` launch
  flags, `proxy/config.yaml` slot/ctx comments) and the usage-analysis skill's
  interpretation section if the guidance changes
  (`.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/REFERENCE.md`), plus any log-consuming
  script that assumes a fixed slot count or per-slot ctx.
- AC6: Full suite passes via the test skill for any config/code change made.

## Notes

- Depends on demand having been raised first (thresholds / serve-first
  admission); that is why the >60% busy gate exists.
- Related: LP-0MSAOQTJS000FFVM (local ctx-size evaluation), and the
  prefill-latency optimisation item — decide geometry before micro-tuning.


---

## Plan (2026-10-25, /skill:plan)

Sequenced features in dependency order (execution order for `wl next`):

1. **Gate: verify 60% local busy night** (LP-0MVNCMDK7003BWCG) — parent AC0 evidence; blocks the arms.
2. **Geometry A/B protocol and reporter** (LP-0MVNCMDW50043RSP) — `docs/dev/slot-geometry-ab.md` (protocol, window, metrics, pre-registered gate), `scripts/slot_geometry_ab_report.py` + fixture tests, `scripts/slot_geometry_arm.py` apply/verify helper. Test-first; can start while the gate is unmet.
3. **Arm A capture: 2 slots 131K** (LP-0MVNCME7Y009KC9K) — blocked by 1+2.
4. **Arm B run: 1 slot 262K** (LP-0MVNCMEJ6004A2QY) — blocked by 3; warm ceiling raised to the 258,048 clamp, cold unchanged, band non-collapsed.
5. **Arm comparison and geometry decision** (LP-0MVNCMEV1007R6YY) — blocked by 4; applies the pre-registered gate, records verdict + follow-on item.
6. **Propagate geometry decision to docs** (LP-0MVNCMF6U006D2H7) — blocked by 5; models.ini / config.yaml comments, usage-analysis REFERENCE, log-consumer audit.
7. **Suite green and geometry assertions** (LP-0MVNCMFIF007TBFP) — blocked by 6; `/skill:test` green + slot/ctx alignment assertions.

Reuse: env plumbing already exists (`LLAMA_PARALLEL`, `LLAMA_CTX_SIZE` in start-llama.sh; `session_slot_pool_size` drives it); per-slot clamp/band logic is in `proxy/proxy/provider.py` with existing unit coverage; usage-analysis report already emits busy/prefill/decode metrics. Precedent harness: `scripts/ubatch_ab_benchmark.py`.

Pre-registered decision-gate defaults (proposal — confirm at implement time unless overridden by the producer): adopt **1 x 262K** when, relative to Arm A, (a) turns served locally does not decrease, (b) `context_too_large` + `large_context_bypass` diverts fall by >= 50 %, (c) p90 dispatch→first-byte does not worsen by > 30 %, (d) local busy % does not regress by > 10 points; otherwise keep 2 slots (or choose mode-dependent with the recorded numbers).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers (2026-10-25)

- Q: "Arm B's warm threshold: raise to the new per-slot clamp (~258K) or keep ~120K?" Answer: **OPEN QUESTION (producer)** — proposed default: raise the economic ceiling ratio so warm = clamp (258,048), cold unchanged (38,000), band non-collapsed (LP-0MSI2M5BT004BCDP). Rationale: leaving it at 120K means the extra slot context is never routed to, defeating the arm. Final confirmation delegated to implement time unless the producer overrides.
- Q: "What makes 1 x 262K 'win'?" Answer: **OPEN QUESTION (producer)** — proposed pre-registered gate above (mirrors the ubatch A/B precedent LP-0MVNBJXR6002OSPD). Confirmation delegated to implement time.
- Q: "Arm window length?" Answer: **OPEN QUESTION (producer)** — proposed default: one full night (22:00 → 06:00 local, >= 8 h), Arm A then Arm B on the same weekday type, identical length for both. Delegated to implement time.
- Q: "Write the protocol while the gate is unmet?" Answer (plan): yes — child 2 has no dependency on the busy gate (desk work), so implementation can begin immediately and the gate evidence decides when the arms may run.


## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-25Z (plan session herdr-1792903336-2608898-6919): superseded the placeholder auto-skip verdict (XS/0.00 h) with a genuine estimate (Medium effort/Medium risk); ran full /skill:plan decomposition. Created 7 children (LP-0MVNCMDK7003BWCG gate, LP-0MVNCMDW50043RSP protocol+reporter, LP-0MVNCME7Y009KC9K Arm A, LP-0MVNCMEJ6004A2QY Arm B, LP-0MVNCMEV1007R6YY comparison+decision, LP-0MVNCMF6U006D2H7 docs propagation, LP-0MVNCMFIF007TBFP suite green) in test-first order with dependency edges C3<-C1,C2 / C4<-C3 / C5<-C4 / C6<-C5 / C7<-C6. Ran the six automated review stages (trace bullets added; Key Files validated), AC coverage review proceeded (7/7), stage advanced to plan_complete. Effort/risk re-estimated (Medium, WBS from children).

## CURRENT MEASUREMENT WINDOW — re-arm #2 (applied 2026-10-28T10:39Z, producer decision A)

The window pinned on 2026-10-26 (`2026-10-26T21:02:00Z → 2026-10-27T21:02:00Z`)
was **invalidated by two proxy restarts inside it**: `2026-10-27T09:33:12Z`
(pid 3775724) and `2026-10-27T10:16:12Z` (pid 3791954), both
`source=manual actor=unknown`. Producer decision (2026-10-28, option **A**):
re-arm to latest restart + 24 h. Children re-pinned to the new window (Q2 = yes).

- **Pinned window (authoritative): `2026-10-27T10:17:00Z → 2026-10-28T10:17:00Z`**
  (exactly 24 h). Start is the first whole minute after the 10:16:12 restart
  (same convention as the superseded 21:01:43 → 21:02:00 pin), so the restart
  line is outside the window.
- **Run instant:** `2026-10-28T10:17:00Z` (window close). Run started
  `2026-10-28T10:39Z`.
- **Restart-freedom attested:** only restart marker in the window files is the
  10:16:12 anchor (before start); `ps -o lstart -p 3791954` = `Tue Oct 27
  10:16:11 2026`, continuous uptime `1-00:23:07` at run time; **no**
  `Logging initialised` / `Rotated previous proxy log aside` between start and
  end. Window is valid.
- **Log files covering the window (disjoint, verified first/last timestamps):**
  `proxy.log.2026-10-27_10` (10:16:12→16:16:11), `proxy.log.2026-10-27_16`
  (16:16:13→22:16:12), `proxy.log-2026-10-28_00` (22:16:13→23:59:59),
  `proxy.log.2026-10-27_22` (00:00:02→04:16:11), `proxy.log.2026-10-28_04`
  (04:16:13→10:16:12), `proxy.log` (10:16:13→live).
- **Config at measurement:** `local_resident_prefix_min_ratio: 0.5`,
  `local_cold_prefill_budget_tokens: 25000`, `local_prefill_deadline_seconds:
  120`, `local_admission_guard_budget_safety_fraction: 0.95`.
- **Code identity (shared checkout; tip moves without restart):** read at run
  time and recorded in the result comment.
- **Superseded history:** the `## Pinned measurement window (Q1 ...)` section
  below (2026-10-25T21:19 → 2026-10-26T21:19) and the 2026-10-26 re-arm
  (21:02 → 21:02) are retained as history only.

## Objective

Execute the **24 h post-deploy verification of AC4** for `LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG`
(resident-prefix admission + session tenancy) on a restart-free production
window and record whether **scheduling-attributed** `prefill_deadline_exceeded`
cancellations fell by **≥ 90 %** against that same window's own re-anchored
baseline — plus the AC5 observability and AC6 lease-watchdog checks.

This item only measures and reports; it changes no scheduling logic.

## Problem statement

The epic's AC4 cannot be verified inside the implementing session: it needs a
full 24 h production soak on code that is actually running. Verification also
silently invalidates itself — the proxy restarted **six times on 2026-10-25**
(log rotations at 11:01:54, 11:21:20, 11:46:48, 18:57:27, 20:16:58 and
21:18:04 UTC), and each restart resets the in-memory residency/lease state, so
a window that contains a restart measures nothing. Without a pinned window,
attested uptime, and a window-scoped baseline, the ≥ 90 % claim is
unfalsifiable.

## Users

- **Proxy operator** — needs a defensible verdict on the thrash change before
  the epic closes, and needs to know whether to roll back.
  - *As the proxy operator, I want the 24 h result stated with its window,
    counts and baseline, so I can accept the change or roll it back.*
- **Implementing agents of the epic** — need AC4 satisfied by an independent
  measurement, not by their own in-session numbers.
  - *As the epic's implementing agent, I want the verdict recorded on the epic,
    so I can close AC4 without self-certifying.*
- **Future thrash investigations** — need the measured window, the corrected
  commands and the classifier rule as precedent.
  - *As a future investigator, I want the procedure and its numbers in
    `findings.md`, so I do not re-derive the methodology.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Preconditions attested before measuring.** The result records: the
  proxy PID and its start instant (`ps -o lstart -p <pid>`), continuous uptime
  covering the entire window, the code identity read **from the checkout the
  running proxy was started from** (`git log -1 --format=%H` — the checkout is
  shared, so the tip moves without a restart), and explicit confirmation that
  both target changes are in that tree (`LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG` ladder;
  `LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D` 25k cold budget / 120 s deadline).
- **AC2 — Window pinned and restart-free.** The window is
  `2026-10-27T10:17:00Z → 2026-10-28T10:17:00Z` (ISO-8601 UTC, exactly 24 h,
  start ≥ the latest proxy restart; re-arm #2 after the 2026-10-27T09:33:12Z and
  10:16:12Z restarts invalidated the previous window).
  Restart-freedom is evidenced by `ps -o lstart` plus the absence of
  `Logging initialised … pid=` / `Rotated previous proxy log aside` lines
  between start and end. A restart inside the window re-arms the run (new
  window, both windows recorded) and never yields a PASS.
- **AC3 — Absolute counts recorded.** `prefill_deadline_exceeded` events and
  total wasted prefill tokens for the window, with the
  `LP-0MVODJ3P6000AIUM` caveat stated (event fields are recomputed post-hoc, so
  `wasted_prefill_tokens` is overstated; the figure is either re-derived from
  admission-side data or reported with that caveat).
- **AC4 — Scheduling-attributed split, reproducible.** Every deadline event is
  classified as scheduling-attributed when either (a) the `reuse_ratio` logged
  at admission was below `server.local_resident_prefix_min_ratio`
  (0.5 in `proxy/config.yaml`), or (b) `slot_owner_session` at admission
  differs from the owner at the deadline event. Per-class counts are recorded;
  the remainder is reported as genuine GPU-speed misses and declared out of
  scope. Because the event line logs only `session` and `deadline`
  (`proxy/proxy/router.py` ~line 1616), the classifier joins each event to the
  session's most recent `routing_resident_prefix` line and any `local_eviction*`
  line before it — the join rule is stated in the result, and events whose
  join is ambiguous are counted separately and **not** as scheduling-attributed
  (conservative).
- **AC5 — Baseline re-anchored to the same window.** Baseline is computed by
  capturing the window with `capture_prefill_thrash_window.py` and replaying it
  through the residency ladder with `replay_prefill_occupancy.py
  --window-fixture`, and the reduction percentage against the
  scheduling-attributed count is stated explicitly. The 2026-10-24 figures
  (160 events / 5.4 h ≈ 780k wasted prefill tokens) are historical reference
  only and are never the baseline.
- **AC6 — Verdict recorded with both gates.** **PASS** requires (i) ≥ 90 %
  reduction in scheduling-attributed cancellations and (ii) no
  `local_lease_active` refusal window longer than the 180 s watchdog bound. On
  FAIL the measured numbers are recorded, a `discovered-from` item is created
  with the offending log extract, and this item is not marked complete.
- **AC7 — Staged-rollout observability check.** The window's
  `analyze_proxy_usage.py` report contains `## Residency-aware admission` with
  the `residency_decisions` / `residency_resident_admits` /
  `residency_evicted_denials` / `residency_tenant_limit_denials` /
  `local_evictions` counters and the per-session slot-owner churn table. An
  absent section, or decisions logged but all unmeasured, is a finding (ladder
  not emitting), never a pass.
- **AC8 — Result recorded and propagated.** One structured result comment on
  this item (window bounds, precondition attestation, counts, classified split,
  baseline, reduction %, verdict), cross-referenced from
  `LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG` and from
  `Post-deploy 24 h prefill regression verification (LP-0MVN4LD2F006B76I)`,
  which consumes the same report set (Q2 decision A) rather than running its
  own window.
- **AC9 — Documentation updated.** `docs/dev/slot-thrashing-investigation/findings.md`
  gains the measured window and verdict (and the corrected capture invocation
  with `--log`), so the 2026-10-24 numbers are labelled historical; all related
  documentation (code comments, README, docs site entries) is updated to
  reflect the changes.
- **AC10 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes** (executed
  via the test skill / dev-push gate; no ad-hoc full-suite runs).

## Constraints

- **No restart inside the window.** Evidence that this is the dominant risk:
  six restarts on 2026-10-25 alone; the 21:18:10 restart was
  `source=manual actor=unknown`. A restart resets residency/lease state and
  invalidates the run.
- **Do not run before the pinned instant, and do not peek early** in a way that
  biases the decision.
- **Read-only measurement:** no `start-proxy.sh --restart`, no config reload, no
  log truncation during the window. Rotated logs (`.gz`) are part of the
  window and must be passed to the capture tool.
- **Counters come from the analysis tool**, not ad-hoc `grep`
  (`LP-0MVOAQDB4002D56G` exposes first-class `--json` keys); `grep` is only used
  for the classification join and for spot evidence.
- **Baseline is window-scoped**, per AC5.
- Analysis window is given with explicit `--start`/`--end` (the
  `05:00 UTC`-boundary convention is a convenience, not a requirement of the
  tool — see Decisions (Q1).

## Existing state (evidence gathered 2026-10-25T23:20–23:35Z)

- **Latest proxy restart: 2026-10-25T21:18:10Z**, PID **3057415**
  (`ps -o lstart -p 3057415` → `Sun Oct 25 21:18:08 2026`; log head:
  `Logging initialised at /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log pid=3057415`
  followed by `Proxy restart attribution: source=manual actor=unknown`).
  ⇒ earliest legal run instant is **2026-10-27T21:02Z**; the item's previous
  instant (11:22Z) is stale.
- **Ladder is emitting:** 871 `routing_resident_prefix` decisions since the
  21:18:10 restart; corrected form present
  (`n_past_actual=none … reuse_ratio=none … residency_source=non_resident`).
- **23 `prefill_deadline_exceeded` events** since the restart (~2 h), all
  `deadline=120s`, e.g. `session=audit-SA-0MVO7XZAB0095R6F-phase2_deep-…` —
  audit sessions visibly dominate the sample, so the user/audit split matters.
- **Report section verified live** for 22:18–23:18: `## Residency-aware
  admission` renders — 446 residency decisions (0 measured / 446 unmeasured),
  9 `tenant_limit` denials, 16 `local_eviction` (8 `local_eviction_after_acceptance`,
  all `prefill_deadline`), 4 of 23 sessions with slot-owner churn.
- **Pipeline smoke-tested end to end** (22:30–23:00): capture → 430 attempts,
  1 deadline-cancelled, ~2152 wasted tokens modelled; replay → 421 over budget,
  9 admitted, **0 over-budget cold admissions**.
- **Gap found — the documented capture command is incomplete:** the item's
  re-anchoring snippet omits `--log`, which is required
  (`capture_prefill_thrash_window.py: error: the following arguments are
  required: --log`). Corrected form is used in this brief.
- **Gap found — classification needs a join:** `prefill_deadline_exceeded`
  logs only `session` + `deadline`, so rule (b) cannot be read off the event
  line itself; it must be joined per session (see AC4).
- **`local_lease_active` is observable**: 37 occurrences since the restart
  (e.g. `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue … queued_duration=60.00s
  reason=local_lease_active`), so the AC6 watchdog check is measurable.
- **Overlapping verification item exists:** `LP-0MVN4LD2F006B76I` (Post-deploy
  24 h prefill regression verification, `plan_complete`, promoted to top level
  on 2026-10-25T22:23Z) measures the same change set with a different window
  (2026-10-25T20:17Z → 2026-10-26T20:17Z, code `fc3c6e2e`) and the historical
  fixture-restated baseline rather than a window-scoped re-anchoring. **That
  window is now invalid:** the 21:18:10 restart falls inside it. Two
  independent runs would produce two contradictory verdicts — see Open
  Question 2.
- **Armed origin:** this item was created and retitled by
  `LP-0MVN4LC7N005XH7P` (`completed`), whose AC4 (deliverable) requires this
  item to carry the deploy-derived instant, the pinned window, the
  re-anchoring query and the classifier.

## Desired change

Nothing in the scheduling path. This item produces:

1. A pinned, restart-free 24 h window recorded on the item **before** the run.
2. One measurement run of the usage analysis plus the re-anchored baseline
   replay, with the scheduling-attributed split applied.
3. A structured result comment with the PASS/FAIL verdict, propagated to the
   epic (and to `LP-0MVN4LD2F006B76I` if it shares this run).
4. The corresponding `findings.md` entry, so the methodology and the numbers
   are reusable.

## Measurement commands (verified working 2026-10-25)

```bash
# 0. Preconditions (attest before measuring, AC1/AC2)
ps -o pid,lstart -p $(pgrep -f "uvicorn proxy.server:app" | head -1)
cd /home/rgardler/projects/llm && git log -1 --format='%H %ci'

# 1. Window report (AC3, AC6, AC7) — explicit window, first-class counters
python3 .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py \
  --start "2026-10-27 10:17:00" --end "2026-10-28 10:17:00" \
  --output-dir ~/proxy-usage-reports/ac4 --json

# 2. Window-scoped baseline (AC5) — every log file overlapping the window,
#    incl. in-process rotations (proxy.log.YYYY-MM-DD_HHMMSS) and .gz
python3 proxy/scripts/capture_prefill_thrash_window.py \
  --start "2026-10-27 10:17:00" --end "2026-10-28 10:17:00" \
  --log /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log \
  --log /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log.2026-10-26_* \
  --log /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log-2026-10-26_00 \
  --out /tmp/ac4_window.jsonl
python3 proxy/scripts/replay_prefill_occupancy.py x \
  --window-fixture /tmp/ac4_window.jsonl    # expects 0 over-budget cold admissions

# 3. Classifier join (AC4) — per-session decision before each deadline event
grep -E "prefill_deadline_exceeded|routing_resident_prefix|local_eviction" \
  /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log
```

## Pinned measurement window (Q1 — operator decision A, 2026-10-25)

- **Start:** `2026-10-25T21:19:00Z` (**already elapsed** — the binding
  restart-anchored freeze is therefore in effect immediately).
- **End / run instant:** `2026-10-26T21:19:00Z` — the analysis runs at/after
  this instant and covers the full 24 h.
- No cron/05:00 alignment (dropped by decision; `analyze_proxy_usage.py`

- **Re-arm rule (binding, unchanged):** any proxy restart between now and
  `2026-10-27T21:02Z` invalidates this window; retitle this item to
  `latest_restart + 24 h` and re-pin before running. A restart **after**

## Shared measurement (Q2 — operator decision A, 2026-10-25)

`Post-deploy 24 h prefill regression verification
(LP-0MVN4LD2F006B76I)` (**re-based by comment 2026-10-25**) consumes this
run's report for its waste/503/eviction-reason/rollback checks instead of
running a separate window. This item owns the scheduling-attributed

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the parent item's gating precondition verified from
measured evidence, so that prefill tuning only starts once local actually
carries sustained work.

## What the gate is

Parent **LP-0MVMHNUAR006SRZT** AC0 requires a comment recording a measured
**>60 % local (GPU) busy** night before any change is made. Busy is the
`## Local model utilization` upper bound (dispatch -> finish: prefill +
decode) from the deterministic `proxy-usage-analysis` CLI, over a complete
night window (22:00-07:00 local).

## Evidence at planning time (2026-10-25)

- Night **2026-10-23 22:00 -> 2026-10-24 07:00**: busy **2.2 %** (719 s of
  32 400 s; 27 local streams; prefill 336 slot-s; decode 383 slot-s;
  idle 97.8 %).
  Command:
  `python3 .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py --log-dir /var/log/llama-proxy --start "2026-10-23 22:00:00" --end "2026-10-24 07:00:00" --output-dir /tmp/wl-gate-check --json`
- Same night in the 24 h daily report (`~/proxy-usage-reports/report.md`,
  window 2026-10-23 10:52 -> 2026-10-24 10:52): busy 10.2 %.

**The gate is NOT met.** The parent is left `blocked` at stage
`plan_complete`, and every other child of this plan depends on this item, so
none of them is dispatchable until the gate passes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC0: The gate AC is satisfied - a comment on this item records the measured >60% GPU utilisation for a full night, from the usage-analysis report, before any change is made.
- AC1: A comment on the parent records local busy % for a **complete** night
  window (22:00-07:00), with the exact CLI invocation, the window bounds and
  the artifact directory used.
- AC2: The gate is declared met **only** when `busy_pct >= 60` for the whole
  night (`definition: dispatch_to_finish` in the CLI `--json` summary).
- AC3: When the gate is not met this item stays **open and incomplete** with
  the evidence comment (recorded `blocked` status is derived from dependency
  edges in `wl` and cannot be pinned, so this item is the lock: keeping it
  incomplete keeps every dependent child dependency-blocked), and no other
  child of the plan is started.
- AC6: This item must never be marked `completed` while the gate is unmet. If a
  run cannot leave it open, it records the evidence and files the deferral on
  the parent rather than completing the gate.
- AC4: When the gate is met this item completes with the evidence comment and
  the parent plus its dependent siblings are unblocked in the same update
  sequence.
- AC5: Measurement only - no configuration, flag or code change.

**Key Files:**
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py` - deterministic report CLI
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/REFERENCE.md` - report section definitions

## Dependencies

None. All other children of this plan depend on this item.

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the A/B benchmark harness to produce valid measurements
in the **40-80k-token** band, because that is the band that produces the
multi-minute local first-byte tail and the only band in which a micro-batch
change can still help.

## Why

`docs/dev/ubatch-ab-2026-10-22.md` (LP-0MVIQ0FSX006HQOS) measured 8.9k / 17.9k
/ 26.8k prompts, found the ubatch 1024->2048 win confined to ~18k (memory
bandwidth bound above), and closed with: *"If this is revisited: measure at
40k-80k tokens"*. The parent item is that revisit, so the harness must be
trustworthy at that size first. Today `build_prompt()` targets ~4 chars/token
without reporting llama-server's real `prompt_tokens`, `--sizes` is free-form,
and a single 80k prefill can take minutes under GPU contention.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The harness records llama-server's reported `prompt_tokens` per sample
  and fails loudly when the delivered size deviates from the requested size by
  more than 10 %, so a mis-sized prompt cannot silently invalidate a bin.
- AC2: An end-to-end run at `--sizes 40960,61440,81920 --reps 3` produces a
  JSON result with per-size p50/p90 and the 20k+ headline aggregate within a
  documented time budget and timeout.
- AC3: Offline unit tests cover prompt sizing/token accounting, percentile
  aggregation, size-deviation rejection and argument validation - no live
  server required.
- AC4: `docs/dev/` records the band methodology and validity guards: unique
  prompt text per repetition, `cache_prompt: false`, the TTS/GPU-contention
  noise rule, and minimum reps.
- AC5: Full suite green via the test skill.

**Key Files:**
- `scripts/ubatch_ab_benchmark.py` - the A/B harness
- `tests/test_ubatch_ab_benchmark.py` - offline harness tests
- `docs/dev/ubatch-ab-2026-10-22.md` - prior experiment record to extend

## Implementation sketch (test-first)

1. Extend the offline tests for the new validations.
2. Report and validate actual `prompt_tokens`; fail fast on a mis-sized bin.
3. Add a documented default band (`40960,61440,81920`) and a per-size timeout
   policy.
4. Record the methodology in `docs/dev/`.

## Dependencies

- Verify sustained local utilisation gate.
- Experiment: 1 slot at 262K ctx vs 2 slots at 131K ctx (LP-0MVMHNUXW0061FGN) -
  a 40-80k prompt must fit the per-slot context.

## Out of scope

Changing llama-server flags, routing or admission policy.

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want `--ubatch-size` and `--batch-size` re-measured in the
40-80k band against a pre-registered win threshold, so the values shipped in
`models.ini` are justified by measurement rather than inherited.

## Context

- Current `[Qwen3]` launch flags: `--ctx-size 262144 --parallel 2
  --batch-size 8192 --ubatch-size 1024 --cache-ram 40960 --cache-type-k q8_0
  --cache-type-v q8_0 --swa-checkpoints 32 --no-mmap -ngl 80 --threads 8`,
  plus `flash-attn`.
- Prior A/B (LP-0MVIQ0FSX006HQOS, `docs/dev/ubatch-ab-2026-10-22.md`): 1.04x
  at p90 over 20k+ batches, reverted. Its close-out rule is that a retry must
  be measured at 40-80k.
- Geometry interacts: per-slot context (`--ctx-size / --parallel`) bounds the
  largest prompt the harness can send, so this item starts only after the
  geometry experiment has recorded its decision.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC2: Prefill throughput is improved by tuning the llama-server launch configuration, each changed value justified by measurement rather than guesswork, or reverted and recorded.
- AC1: A hypothesis and numeric decision gate are written on this item BEFORE
  the first measurement (for example: adopt when p90 prompt-eval tok/s improves
  by >= 1.3x in the 60-80k bins with decode regression <= 2 %).
- AC2: Candidate values (`--ubatch-size` 2048 and 4096; `--batch-size` 8192 vs
  16384) are measured one variable at a time on arm-identical workloads with
  >= 3 reps using the 40-80k band harness; raw JSON is archived under
  `benchmark-results/`.
- AC3: Each knob gets an explicit adopt/revert decision with measured numbers;
  an adopted value is written to `models.ini` `[Qwen3]` with the measurement
  and rollback value in the comment, a rejected value is recorded as reverted
  to 1024 / 8192.
- AC4: VRAM and stability are checked per arm (clean llama-server start, no
  OOM, `rocm-smi` within budget); the restart that empties the 40 GiB prompt
  cache is recorded so proxy first-byte stats are not compared across it.
- AC5: Any test or script asserting the flags is updated in the same change and
  the full suite is green via the test skill.
- AC6: If no value wins, the item completes with a recorded NO-GO and the
  parent's tuning scope narrows to the proxy-knob/ETA-guard half.

**Key Files:**
- `./models.ini` - `[Qwen3]` launch flags
- `./start-llama.sh` - flag defaults passed to llama-server
- `scripts/ubatch_ab_benchmark.py` - measurement harness
- `tests/test_models_ini_centralized_config.sh` - flag assertions
- `docs/dev/ubatch-ab-2026-10-22.md` - prior record to extend
- `benchmark-results/ubatch-ab-2026-10-22-candidate-2048.json` - prior raw arm data

## Dependencies

- Verify sustained local utilisation gate.
- Baseline prefill measurement capture.
- 40-80k prefill benchmark capability.
- Experiment: 1 slot at 262K ctx vs 2 slots at 131K ctx (LP-0MVMHNUXW0061FGN).

## Out of scope

`--cache-ram`, KV-cache quantisation, ctx-size/slot geometry, `--threads`,
`--mlock` and `--swa-checkpoints` (see the sibling launch-flag item).

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the prefill-ETA admission guard and the prefill
deadline re-checked against the post-change prefill rates and the interaction
documented, so a faster GPU cannot silently make the budget/deadline wrong.

## Context

- Live knobs - deployed by LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D, do **not** re-tune without new
  evidence: `local_cold_prefill_budget_tokens: 25000`,
  `local_prefill_deadline_seconds: 120`,
  `local_admission_guard_eta_percentile_min_tokens: 20000`,
  `local_admission_guard_budget_safety_fraction: 0.95`,
  `local_admission_guard_eta_percentile: 75`,
  `local_prefill_thrash_cooldown_seconds: 600`.
- The guard calibrates itself from a rolling window of per-dispatch samples
  `(coded_tokens, new_tokens, dispatch_to_first_byte_ms)` keyed by
  `(model, context bucket)`, so it re-calibrates automatically. But the budget
  (25k) and deadline (120 s) were derived from the OLD band rates (249 t/s at
  20-30k, 114 t/s at 63k). If prefill becomes materially faster, both may be
  re-derivable - a decision for measurement, not guesswork.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC2: Prefill throughput is improved by tuning the configuration (llama-server launch flags and the prefill-related proxy knobs) where measurement justifies each change, otherwise left unchanged and recorded.
- AC4: If a knob change affects the prefill-ETA guard's behaviour, the guard's configuration and documentation are updated together, and the local_prefill_deadline_seconds / ETA interactions are documented.
- AC1: Matched before/after windows compare guard behaviour: admit vs reject
  counts by reason (`prefill_budget_exceeded`, `eta_exceeds_budget`,
  `prefill_deadline_exceeded`), thrash-cooldown events and cancelled prefills.
- AC2: The measured band rates (10-20k, 20-30k, 30-40k, 40-60k, 60-80k) are
  re-derived from the post-change window and compared numerically with the
  rates the budget and deadline were derived from.
- AC3: A decision is recorded on whether 25 000 tokens / 120 s remain optimal;
  any change is justified by AC1/AC2 numbers, shipped in one change with its
  config comment, and carries a documented rollback.
- AC4: The `local_prefill_deadline_seconds` <-> ETA-guard <->
  contention-queue interaction (the ordering invariant
  `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds < local_prefill_deadline_seconds <
  local_dispatch_first_byte_timeout_seconds < local_dispatch_max_prefill_seconds`)
  is documented in one authoritative place (config comments plus a `docs/dev/`
  note) and the tests asserting the ordering still pass.
- AC5: Guard/calibration code is unchanged unless a measured defect is found;
  if changed, unit tests cover the new behaviour.
- AC6: Full suite green via the test skill.

**Key Files:**
- `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py` - calibration and admission guard
- `proxy/config.yaml` - guard, budget and deadline configuration
- `proxy/tests/test_prefill_eta.py` - calibration tests
- `proxy/tests/test_prefill_eta_conservative.py` - conservative pricing tests
- `proxy/tests/test_prefill_eta_deadline.py` - deadline interaction tests
- `docs/dev/prefill-eta-deadline-interaction.md` - authoritative interaction note

## Dependencies

- Verify sustained local utilisation gate.
- Baseline prefill measurement capture.
- Launch-flag A/B: ubatch and batch size (the rates it changes).
- Launch-flag A/B: threads and SWA checkpoints.

## Out of scope

Re-litigating the values shipped by LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D without new
post-change evidence.

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want Arm B (1 slot at 262,144 ctx) measured over a window of
identical length to Arm A, with the slot-count and context-dependent settings
adjusted consistently, so the geometry trade-off is measurable without a
threshold confound.

## Context

- Per-slot ctx is `--ctx-size / --parallel`: `--parallel 1 --ctx-size 262144` -> 262,144 per slot. `--parallel` and `session_slot_pool_size` MUST match or sessions map to nonexistent slots.
- The warm ceiling is `min(clamp, economic)` with economic = `round(local_large_context_economic_ceiling_ratio x local_model_ctx_size)` (0.4578 x 262,144 ~= 120,049) and clamp = 258,048 at 1 slot. Leaving the ratio unchanged keeps the warm cap at ~120K, so the extra slot context would never be routed to - the ratio/threshold must be raised so the ceiling matches the new clamp (parent AC2: "adjusted consistently").
- The cold/warm band must keep non-zero width or the cached_ratio routing check stays unreachable (LP-0MSAZXXDY005AWA1 / LP-0MSI2M5BT004BCDP).
- `local_max_concurrent_prefills: 1` becomes moot with one slot (prefill serialisation is inherent); record whether it is left as-is.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: Geometry changes are applied together and verified after restart: llama-server reports 1 slot with n_ctx 262,144, `session_slot_pool_size: 1`, warm ceiling raised to the 258,048 clamp (or an explicit recorded justification for keeping ~120K), cold threshold unchanged at 38,000. Band width and cached_ratio-check reachability are demonstrated from the routing code / unit tests, not assumed.
- AC2: Arm B is measured over a window of the same length as Arm A inside a >= 60 % busy night; raw data archived under `benchmark-results/`; reporter output recorded on this item and on the parent.

- AC4: Any serving errors introduced (slot_save failed, HTTP 400/503, slot-mismatch warnings) are captured in the arm's metric table.

- Parent AC2 trace: Arm A (2 x 131K, current) and Arm B (1 x 262K) are each run for a comparable period at the gate, with llama-server --parallel / --ctx-size changed together and session_slot_pool_size plus the warm/cold thresholds adjusted consistently.

# Pin start-proxy.sh shell-level `--restart` preserve-vs-restart decision with a pytest test

## Problem statement

`start-proxy.sh --restart` decides whether to preserve a warm llama-server by
comparing the `config_sha256` recorded in `.llama_server_signature.json` with a
freshly computed `merged_config_sha256` of `proxy/config.yaml`; on a match it
preserves ("Preserving running llama-server (unchanged local backend config)."),
otherwise it kills and restarts llama-server. That shell branch is currently
the **only** untested consumer of the merged-config signature: the sole
coverage lives in `tests/test_start_proxy_mode.sh`, which
LP-0MVK6JQW9003KY29 deletes (mode-era harness). The Python tests cover the hash
helper and the signature writer (`proxy/tests/test_config_merge.py`,
`proxy/tests/test_restart_lifecycle.py`), not the shell decision that acts on
them — so a regression there (e.g. comparing the wrong path, ignoring the flag)
would go unnoticed and would either kill a warm llama-server on every restart
or silently preserve a stale one.

## Users

- **Proxy operator** — the warm KV/prompt cache must survive a proxy-only
  restart, and a genuine local-backend change must restart llama-server.
- **Future implementation agents** — need the shell branch pinned so changes to
  `start-proxy.sh` restart handling fail loudly in the default suite.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Unchanged config preserves llama-server.** A pytest test runs a
  sandboxed copy of `start-proxy.sh --foreground --restart` whose signature
  file matches `merged_config_sha256(proxy/config.yaml, proxy/config.yaml)` and
  asserts the "Preserving running llama-server" line is emitted and the fake
  `pkill` log contains **no** `llama-server` kill.
- **AC2 — Changed config restarts llama-server.** With the sandbox config
  edited after the signature was written (merged hash changes), the preserving
  line is absent and the fake `pkill` log shows a `llama-server` kill.
- **AC3 — Fail-safe signatures.** Missing, empty or corrupt signature /
  unreadable hash → conservative restart (never an unearned preserve), asserted
  behaviourally.
- **AC4 — Explicit override still wins.** `--keep-llama-server` forces
  preservation even when the signature mismatches (flag beats hash).
- **AC5 — Sandbox isolation.** The test copies the script into a temp dir with
  stubbed `pkill`/`fuser`/`ss`/`netstat`, an isolated `$HOME`, an ephemeral port
  and a fake interpreter intercepting the final `exec uvicorn`; it never
  touches the live proxy, llama-server, TTS or ports 8000/8080/8081, and never
  issues a blanket kill. It is collected by the default pytest suite (unlike
  the bare `tests/*.sh` harnesses).
- **AC6 — Documentation reflects the new coverage.** The new module carries a
  module docstring stating what it pins (the shell preserve-vs-restart
  decision) and its sandbox guarantees, and `docs/INTEGRATION.md`
  ("On-demand live-server tests" section) gains a cross-reference note
  distinguishing this always-collected pytest module from the opt-in
  `tests/*.sh` harnesses. No README change is required (the README does not
  list individual test modules).
- **AC7 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- No behaviour change to `start-proxy.sh`: this is coverage for the existing
  contract. A defect found while writing it becomes a separate work item.
- Reuse the established sandbox pattern in
  `tests/test_start_proxy_launch_modes.py` (fake `python3` recording argv,
  stubbed process/port probes) rather than inventing a new harness.
- The signature schema is written by `proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py`
  (`_write_llama_server_signature`: `mode`, `model`, `parallel`, `router_mode`,
  `config_sha256`); fixtures must match it.
- UK English.

## Existing state

- `tests/test_start_proxy_mode.sh` (being deleted by LP-0MVK6JQW9003KY29) holds
  the only behavioural assertions for this branch; after deletion the branch has
  none.
- `grep -rln "Preserving running llama-server"` matches only that harness and
  `proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh`.
- `proxy/tests/test_restart_lifecycle.py` asserts the flag is *documented*
  (`test_start_proxy_help_documents_keep_llama_server`) and pins the Python hash
  helper — not the shell preserve/restart decision.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `tests/test_start_proxy_restart_signature.py` — new pytest test (name
  indicative).
- `tests/test_start_proxy_launch_modes.py` — sandbox pattern to reuse.
- `proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh` — script under test (read-only).
- `proxy/proxy/config_merge.py` — `merged_config_sha256` fixture hash.
- `proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py` — signature schema reference.
- `docs/INTEGRATION.md` — "On-demand live-server tests" section (AC6
  cross-reference note).

## Implementation sketch

1. **Harness (reuse, don't reinvent).** Lift the `_sandbox` / `_run` /
   `FAKE_PY` pattern from `tests/test_start_proxy_launch_modes.py` into the new
   module: copy `proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh` plus `proxy/` (including
   `proxy/proxy/config_merge.py`) into `tmp_path`, isolate `$HOME`, bind an
   ephemeral port, and put stubbed `pkill` / `fuser` / `ss` / `netstat` on
   `PATH`. The one delta from the launch-modes stubs: the fake `pkill` must
   **append its argv to a log file** so AC1/AC2/AC4 can assert on
   llama-server kills (the launch-modes stub exits silently).
2. **Fixture hash.** Compute the recorded `config_sha256` in-test with the same
   helper the shell calls: `merged_config_sha256(REPO_ROOT/config.yaml,
   REPO_ROOT/config.yaml)` (base merged with itself — the mode axis is gone),
   imported from `proxy.proxy.config_merge`. Write it into
   `tmp_path/.llama_server_signature.json` using the
   `_write_llama_server_signature` schema (`mode`, `model`, `parallel`,
   `router_mode`, `config_sha256`).
3. **Cases.** One sandbox run per case, all with
   `--foreground --restart`: (a) matching signature → preserve line present, no
   `llama-server` in the fake `pkill` log (AC1); (b) signature written, then the
   sandbox `config.yaml` edited → no preserve line, `llama-server` kill logged
   (AC2); (c) missing / empty / corrupt signature and an unreadable hash
   (omit `config_merge.py` from the sandbox so the inline helper import fails →
   empty `_restart_sha`) → conservative restart (AC3); (d) mismatching
   signature plus `--keep-llama-server` → preserve line present (AC4).
4. **Cost control.** Each `--restart` run pays the script's `sleep 3` (and
   `sleep 2` in the kill phase), so keep the case count minimal — one run per
   AC, no parameterised permutations beyond the three fail-safe variants
   (missing / empty / corrupt) — to avoid slowing the default suite.
5. **Docs (AC6).** Module docstring + `docs/INTEGRATION.md` note.

### Risky assumptions

- The shell branch's `_restart_sha` computation silently degrades to empty when
  `config_merge.py` is absent (`2>/dev/null || true`); AC3's "unreadable hash"
  case depends on that, so the test asserts behaviour, not the mechanism.
- Sandbox `REPO_ROOT` isolation — **verified at plan time**:
  `start-proxy.sh:91` derives `REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"`, so
  copying the script to `tmp_path/proxy/scripts/` makes `REPO_ROOT`
  `tmp_path/proxy` and both the signature file and the hashed `config.yaml`
  are sandbox-local. Keep an explicit assertion on this (e.g. the sandbox
  writes the fixture signature, never reads `$PWD/.llama_server_signature.json`)
  so a future refactor to a hard-coded path fails loudly instead of silently
  testing the live repo.
- Two kill phases, not one: the script runs a graceful `pkill -f 'llama-server'`
  and, when `KEEP_LLAMA=0`, a `pkill -9 -f 'llama-server'`; a preserve
  assertion must therefore cover **both** phases (log has no `llama-server`
  line at all), and a restart assertion may match either.

## Related work

- **LP-0MVK6JQW9003KY29** — deletes the stale mode-era harness; this item
  replaces the one piece of live coverage that deletion removes.
- **LP-0MVFJQAID007YB0H**, **LP-0MVKD0P7R002D5L8** — duplicate items closed
  in favour of LP-0MVK6JQW9003KY29 (producer decision B).
- **LP-0MUJRVYQH002IEHW** — restart signature hashes the merged config.
- **LP-0MUCEFCL6001ZXYN** — preserve-the-warm-llama-server design.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-29 (plan skill, auto-complete path; effort Extra Small / risk Low):
  pre-check returned `skip`, so no decomposition was created. Applied
  conservative review fixes only: tightened AC6 to name `docs/INTEGRATION.md`
  (the doc target already identified at intake) instead of a generic
  "update all docs"; added `docs/INTEGRATION.md` to Key Files; added an
  **Implementation sketch** section and **Risky assumptions** so the item is
  directly implementable. No scope change, no AC added or removed.
