## Problem

`proxy/proxy/handlers.py:489` carries a `# noqa` comment whose text is prose
rather than a comma-separated code list, so ruff cannot parse it as a
suppression. Every `ruff check` run in this repo — repo-wide or file-scoped —
prints a warning to stderr:

```
$ ruff check --select I001 proxy/proxy/handlers.py
warning: Invalid `# noqa` directive on proxy/proxy/handlers.py:489: expected a
comma-separated list of codes (e.g. `# noqa: F401, F841`).
All checks passed!
```

Current source:

```python
    import os  # noqa: local import for config access
```

## Why it matters

- The comment gives no suppression at all: whatever it was intended to silence
  (`F401`? a local-import / `PLC0415` style rule?) is either already allowed by
  `.ruff.toml` or silently expressed as prose — so the intent is unrecoverable
  from the code.
- It makes every lint invocation in this repository noisy, which trains readers
  and agents to ignore ruff's warning channel — the exact channel that would
  surface a genuinely broken suppression.
- It was noted as a known-but-out-of-scope side observation while clearing the
  `I001` findings of epic `LP-0MVLK5H04003FZJS` (see
  `LP-0MVKE61H9001WPAQ` for the earlier sighting).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — warning cleared:** `python3 -m ruff check proxy/proxy/handlers.py`
      produces no `Invalid \`noqa\` directive` warning and still reports
      `All checks passed!` (command + output captured on the work item).
- [ ] **AC2 — intent preserved:** the reason for the directive is expressed
      either as a valid code list (e.g. `# noqa: PLC0415`) that matches the
      rule actually triggered, or as a plain explanatory comment with no
      `noqa` prefix. Determined by removing the directive and re-running ruff
      on the file to see which rule (if any) fires; recorded in the closure
      comment.
- [ ] **AC3 — no blanket suppression:** `.ruff.toml` gains no new
      `per-file-ignores`/global `ignore` entry for `proxy/proxy/handlers.py`,
      so genuine future findings remain detectable (`git diff --stat` on
      `.ruff.toml` empty for this item).
- [ ] **AC4 — no behaviour change:** the change is comment-only; the
      `import os` statement itself is untouched, so runtime behaviour is
      identical.
- [ ] **AC5 — full suite green:** validation runs through the test skill
      (`/skill:test`, changed scope at the implement gate, full suite at the
      dev-push gate) — no ad-hoc `pytest`.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py` — line 489 holds the invalid directive
  (`import os  # noqa: local import for config access`).
- `.ruff.toml` — **must remain unchanged**; no suppression may be added.

## Provenance

Discovered from: `LP-0MVLK5H04003FZJS` (Quality Improvement - Refactoring epic) while
closing child `LP-0MVMLII27004JVII` — that item verified
`ruff check --select I001 .` clean at HEAD `9db15857` and this stray `# noqa`
warning was the only remaining lint-channel noise observed. Earlier sighting
recorded in `LP-0MVKE61H9001WPAQ`. Not blocking that epic: the epic tracks
`I001` findings, and this is a distinct (pre-existing) hygiene defect.

## Goal

Track the parent AC4 residual found by the post-deploy measurement (LP-0MVN4LD2F006B76I): within-budget warm prompts that are admitted, then cancelled by the 120 s prefill deadline with **zero prefill progress** — second-slot head-of-line blocking, not the admission budget.

> **Plan note (2026-10-28) — hypothesis superseded.** The scheduler epic LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG and LP-0MVOFVCA2008DQVE are completed, yet the residual survived; a later window (LP-0MVQIT9QY007QU27) shows 68 % of these evictions overlap no other prefill, so the cause is predicted-not-measured warmth, not second-slot head-of-line blocking. The live fix owner is LP-0MVQIT9QY007QU27 (with F5 LP-0MVR7IXAI002QXXD). The *Ownership* and *Key Files* sections below are stale on this point; the AC text is unchanged and the closure verdict is owned by child LP-0MVRMOV8K0007NFO.

## Evidence (2026-10-25 11:46:50 → 19:11, post-deploy window of LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D)

- 22 `local_eviction_after_acceptance reason=prefill_deadline` events over 7.4 h (2.97/h vs the 24.3/h baseline → −88 %), all with `new_tokens ≤ 25 000` (so all within the shipped budget) and ETA ≤ 68 s for the small ones (e.g. `eta_prefill_s=7.1 elapsed_s=120.1`, `eta_prefill_s=20.4 elapsed_s=120.1`, `eta_prefill_s=24.8 elapsed_s=120.2`).
- The common signature is `lease_extended_during_prefill … progress=None alive=False in_flight=True` repeated for the whole lease plus `prefill_wait_exceeds_threshold waited=30s progress=0` — the llama task makes **no progress at all** for 120 s while the other slot serves a prefill. E.g. a 13.3k-token cold prompt sat behind an audit session's huge prefill for the full lease.
- 10 of the 22 events are sibling-epic audit loads (`audit-LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG-*`, `audit-AH-*`, drive session `01a172f6…`); user-traffic residual = 12 events / 7.4 h = 1.6/h.
- Every over-budget (>25 k new-token) prompt was refused at admission in the window (zero over-budget admissions, `prefill_budget_exceeded` refusals 1 089) — the budget half of the parent is working; only the *warm, small-ETA* residual survives, and it is a scheduler/occupancy problem.

## Ownership

The scheduler epic **LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG** (session-level tenancy / resident-prefix admission, serialised prefills LP-0MVGDUUV3001XFRJ) covers exactly this class: per-request scheduling against the 2-slot pool with no occupancy-aware admission. This item is a **tracking/evidence item** for the parent's AC4; it is deliberately not implemented here (out of this parent's scope).

## Scope

**In:** evidence, link to the scheduler epic, closure criteria, and the parent-AC4 re-scope note. The eventual fix (occupancy-aware admission: refuse a local dispatch when the other slot is mid-prefill and the projected total exceeds the deadline) is scheduled on LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG.

**Out:** changes to this parent's budget/deadline maths; any work already owned by the scheduler epic.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Evidence recorded.** The 22-event/7.4 h measurement (12 user-traffic) with the `progress=0` signature and the audit-load split is referenced from the parent AC4 comment.
- **AC2 — Link established.** A related edge points to LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG so the producer can fold this into the scheduler scope (or explicitly re-scope parent AC4 to exclude audit traffic / warm-HOL).
- **AC3 — Closure.** Closed only when either (a) the scheduler epic lands and a post-landing window shows zero user-traffic `prefill_deadline` evictions after acceptance, or (b) the producer explicitly re-scopes parent AC4 with an agreed threshold and the re-scoped criterion is met.
- **AC4 — Rollback note.** No rollback recommended: the budget change is working (−88 % deadline rate, 0 over-budget admissions, −83 % wasted tokens); rolling back restores the thrash without touching this residual.

## Key Files

- `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log*` (window evidence)
- `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py` (occupancy-aware `ProjectedWait` exists; the scheduler epic consumes it)
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` (`_try_acquire_local_dispatch` prefill gate)
## Relationships

- **discovered-from: LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D** (cold-prefill admission budget epic) — found by its post-deploy measurement (LP-0MVN4LD2F006B76I).
- **depends-on: LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG** (local slot scheduling epic) — the fix is occupancy-aware admission / prefill scheduling, owned there.
- **Detached from LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D's children (2026-10-25).** It was filed as a child of that epic, but it depends on the scheduler epic's multi-day horizon, and a parent cannot advance to `in_review` while any child is still open — keeping it as a child would have made the admission-budget epic unable to close after its own 24 h window. It is therefore a standalone tracking item: the budget epic closes on its re-scoped AC4; this item closes on its own AC3.
## Implementation and measurement vehicles (added at intake, 2026-10-25)

The fix and the closing measurement are separate items; this item owns only the evidence, the link and the closure verdict.

- **`LP-0MVOFVCA2008DQVE` — `[impl] Occupancy-aware deadline admission (second-slot head-of-line residual)`** (child of the scheduler epic `LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG`, `intake_complete`, implementation started 2026-10-25T23:08Z). It prices the projected time-to-first-byte from the **occupant's** own admission evidence (`eta_prefill_s` − elapsed) and refuses with `reason=prefill_eta_exceeds_deadline` when the projection exceeds `local_prefill_deadline_seconds`. Its "Out of scope" section names this item's AC3 as the owner of the ≥24 h post-landing measurement — i.e. the fix lands there, the verdict is recorded here.
- **`LP-0MVN4LD2F006B76I` — `Post-deploy 24 h prefill regression verification`** (top level, implementable from `2026-10-26 20:17:00 UTC`) reports the post-acceptance eviction counter and its per-reason breakdown for the **budget** window. It is a different window and a different baseline from this item's closure window (which starts when the occupancy-aware admission lands), so its verdict must not be reused as AC3 evidence.

### AC3 closure conditions, made concrete

- **(a)** `LP-0MVOFVCA2008DQVE` lands, and a ≥24 h window starting **after** its deploy shows **zero user-traffic** `local_eviction_after_acceptance reason=prefill_deadline` events (audit sessions reported separately, as in the parent AC4 re-scope). A residual that is shown to be GPU incapacity rather than occupancy — measured, with the same evidence standard as the 22-event baseline — also satisfies (a).
- **(b)** The producer explicitly re-scopes parent AC4 with an agreed threshold and that re-scoped criterion is met.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption — the residual is occupancy, not capacity.** The `progress=None alive=False in_flight=True` signature (no prefill progress for the whole lease while the other slot serves) is the diagnostic; the occupant-evidence pricing in `LP-0MVOFVCA2008DQVE` is the matching fix. If the post-landing window still shows zero-progress evictions, the measurement must separate occupant starvation from GPU saturation before AC3 can be closed.
- **Risk — window contamination.** A restart, config reload or slot-count change inside the closure window re-bases it; record the deploy timestamp of `LP-0MVOFVCA2008DQVE` on this item before the window opens.
- **Risk — attribution.** 10 of the 22 baseline events were sibling-epic audit loads; the user-traffic / audit split must use the same classifier as the parent AC4 measurement so the two reports stay comparable.
- **Scope-creep risk — further admission-maths tuning.** Any additional change to budgets, deadlines, queue bounds or slot counts discovered while measuring is filed as a linked work item on `LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG`, not folded into this tracking item.

## Intake notes (auto-complete)

- **Evaluation:** intake interview not required — the item already carries a measured evidence window, four testable acceptance criteria, key files, dependency edges and a producer-decided scope. Advanced via `intake.py auto-complete` (no clarifying questions asked; no Appendix required because no interview took place).
- **Duplicate check (2026-10-25):** searched `prefill_deadline`, `head-of-line`, `occupancy-aware`, `resident-prefix` and `prefill deadline`. No completed or open item fully satisfies this item's ACs: `LP-0MVOFVCA2008DQVE` implements the fix and explicitly out-scopes the measurement here; `LP-0MVO7IDTP005S92D` (completed) excluded the 22 genuine `prefill_deadline` events from its scope; `LP-0MVN3KPEC007WWL5` evaluates the snapshot-pool size. Partial overlap only — no rewrite required.
- **Issue type corrected** `feature` → `task`: the deliverable is evidence, a link and a closure verdict, not new capability (the capability is `LP-0MVOFVCA2008DQVE`).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items

- **LP-0MVKUKEU80022C3U** – Deadline-aware local admission bound (completed)

## Goal

As an operator I need `llama_process_rss_bytes` / `llama_model_rss_bytes` to
report real memory figures, so memory pressure on the llama-server process can be
alerted on instead of being permanently invisible.

## Context

Discovered while resolving the dead alert groups in LP-0MVO8DOHP008FL48. The
proxy publishes both RSS gauges as **0** on every scrape:

```
llama_process_rss_bytes 0.0
llama_model_rss_bytes{model="Qwen3"} 0.0        # and every other model label
```

Original diagnosis: `proxy/proxy/handlers.py` (`/admin/metrics`) only reads RSS
when it holds a live host process handle:

```python
if 'psutil' in dir(srv) and srv.psutil and srv.llama_process is not None:
    pid = getattr(srv.llama_process, 'pid', None)
    ...
    process_rss = getattr(mem, 'rss', None)
```

llama-server can run inside a **podman container**
(`scripts/podman_start_llama.sh`, container `${PODMAN_LC_CONTAINER:-llama}`), so
`srv.llama_process` is the host-side `podman exec` wrapper (or `None`),
`process_rss` stays `None`, and `metrics.update_metrics(None, models)` sets
`llama_process_rss_bytes = 0` and zeroes every `llama_model_rss_bytes` label. The
status/`/admin/metrics` endpoint likewise reports `process_rss_bytes: null`.

### Root-cause correction (verified live, 2026-10-26)

The container is **not** the only failure mode. On this host llama-server runs
host-direct (no podman containers were running) and the gauges are still 0:

- `ps -eo pid,rss,cmd` showed a host `llama-server` router (`rss` ≈ 0.34 GB) with
  a model child process holding ≈ 45 GB — **router-mode model memory lives in
  child processes, not in the top-level process**. Reading only
  `llama_process.pid` therefore under-reports by ~99% even when a pid is
  available.
- `curl localhost:8000/admin/metrics` returned `process_rss_bytes: null` although
  `llama_server_running: true`: the proxy had restarted ~2 h earlier and
  **adopted** the 3-day-old server via `_AdoptedLlamaProcess`, whose sentinel
  carries `pid = 0` (`proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py`), so `if pid:` is false.
- `/metrics` is served from the already-set gauges
  (`metrics.generate_metrics_payload()`), while `metrics.update_metrics()` has a
  single caller — the `/admin/metrics` handler. Prometheus scrapes `/metrics`
  every 15 s (`monitoring/prometheus.yml`), so the series are only refreshed when
  something separately polls `/admin/metrics`; otherwise they stay at their
  registered 0.
- llama.cpp's own `/metrics` exposes **no** RSS/memory series (checked against a
  live server), so the container/proc/cgroup view is the only source of truth.
- Both runtime paths must keep working: `proxy/config.yaml` sets
  `llama_start_script: start-llama.sh` with `llama_allow_host_fallback: true`, and
  the container path (`scripts/podman_start_llama.sh`) is the documented default
  for container-managed deployments. The fix is **additive**: keep the existing
  host-pid path.

Consequence: the `LlamaMemoryHighWarning` / `LlamaMemoryHighCritical` rules
(75% / 90% of 90 GB on `llama_process_rss_bytes`) could never fire, so they were
deleted in LP-0MVO8DOHP008FL48 and GPU memory pressure is now alerted on
`gpu_gtt_used_bytes` instead. That covers the GPU-visible pool, but the proxy's
own RSS (and the per-model attribution) is still unmeasured, and the existing
`monitoring/llama_memory_alerts.yaml` documentation references disappeared with
the rules.

**Key Files:**

- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py` — `/admin/metrics` RSS read (host-pid only) and `/metrics` handler
- `proxy/proxy/metrics.py` — `update_metrics()` gauges and the zero-on-`None` behaviour
- `proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py` — `_AdoptedLlamaProcess` sentinel (`pid = 0`) and `start_llama_server()`
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — existing router child-port discovery (reusable for per-model attribution)
- `scripts/podman_start_llama.sh` — container name and `podman exec` wrapper
- `proxy/tests/test_metrics.py` — metric unit tests
- `proxy/tests/test_observability_regression.py` — `/metrics` payload regression guard
- `proxy/tests/test_monitoring_deployment.py` — `FORBIDDEN_RULE_SERIES` / `REQUIRED_RULE_FILES` guards
- `monitoring/prometheus.yml` — scrape path (`/metrics`) and `rule_files`
- `monitoring/gpu_memory_alerts.yaml` — existing GTT memory-pressure coverage
- `monitoring/llama_memory_alerts.yaml` — removed file, to be restored if AC5 restores the alert

## Acceptance criteria

1. `llama_process_rss_bytes` returns a non-zero value within 5% of the
   llama-server's actual resident memory — `podman stats --no-stream` /
   cgroup `memory.current` for the container, or the summed RSS of the
   llama-server process tree on the host — while a model is loaded, and it stays
   fresh when only `/metrics` is scraped (Prometheus does not call
   `/admin/metrics`).
2. `llama_model_rss_bytes{model=...}` attributes memory per loaded model with the
   documented heuristic (equal split or a better measure), and the labelled
   values sum to within ~10% of `llama_process_rss_bytes`.
3. The value is obtained without requiring a host-side process handle when
   llama-server runs in podman (e.g. resolve the container via
   `podman inspect -f '{{.State.Pid}}'` plus its cgroup `memory.current`, or
   `podman inspect`/`podman stats`), and the resolution chain covers the
   adopted-server case (`_AdoptedLlamaProcess` has `pid = 0`) and the router-child
   case (model memory held by child processes). It degrades safely when the
   runtime is unavailable: the scrape still succeeds and the failure is logged
   once, not per scrape.
4. A test asserts a non-zero RSS is published for a mocked container-backed
   backend, and that the RSS path fails soft (still serves `/metrics`) when the
   container runtime lookup raises.
5. A memory-pressure alert on the now-working series is restored (or a decision
   is recorded that GTT coverage in `gpu_memory_alerts.yaml` is sufficient). If
   the alert is restored, `llama_process_rss_bytes` is removed from
   `FORBIDDEN_RULE_SERIES` in `proxy/tests/test_monitoring_deployment.py`, the
   rule file is registered in `monitoring/prometheus.yml` `rule_files` (and in
   `REQUIRED_RULE_FILES`), and the "removed because the series is 0" comment in
   `prometheus.yml` is updated.

## Verification

- `curl -s localhost:8000/metrics | grep llama_process_rss_bytes` — non-zero,
  refreshed between two consecutive 15 s scrapes with no `/admin/metrics` poll.
- `curl -s localhost:8000/admin/metrics | jq .process_rss_bytes` — non-null and
  matching the gauge.
- Host-direct: compare with `ps -o rss= -p <router pid>` plus its model children.
- Container: compare with `podman stats --no-stream llama` and
  `cat /sys/fs/cgroup/.../libpod-*.scope/memory.current`.
- Runtime absent/erroring: `/metrics` still returns 200 and the warning appears
  once in the proxy log.

## Notes

- Not blocking LP-0MVO8DOHP008FL48; the dead rules were removed and GTT coverage
  added there, so no alert is silently dead in the meantime.
- Related: LP-0MVO8CLCL00086NT (monitoring tree), LP-0MQR554O60033BGF (Grafana,
  which would consume these series).
- Implement test-first: extend `proxy/tests/test_metrics.py` /
  `test_observability_regression.py` before touching the handler.
- Observed-but-out-of-scope: `loaded_models` on `/health` and `/admin/metrics`
  currently lists every alias in the preset (~15 labels) rather than only the
  loaded models, so equal-split attribution is arithmetically correct but
  semantically coarse. Narrowing the loaded-model set is a separate decision.

# Skill-suite tests are invisible to the repo full-suite gate

## Goal (headline)

The dev-push full-suite gate must execute the project-local skill tests under
`.pi/skills/*/tests` (529 tests today), so a regression in the observability the
audit and the 05:00 cron depend on can no longer pass the gate silently.

> **Status: DECIDED — blocked-by SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB.** Decision: option 3
> (upstream fix in the test skill, SorraAgents), coverage breadth **all**
> `.pi/skills/*/tests` directories. The llm repo is intentionally **not**
> configured with a local pin (see Constraints); enforcement arrives when the
> upstream item ships. Work on this item starts only after that.

**Headline for the report:** the repo's dev-push full-suite gate only ever
collects `tests/` and `proxy/` (5 264 tests), because pytest's default
`norecursedirs` includes `.*` and therefore prunes `.pi/`; the 529 real, ~6 s
`proxy-usage-analysis` skill tests were enforced by nothing. The fix is now owned
upstream (SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB); this item proves the enforcement, publishes the
split counts, keeps the convention path active, and guards against drift.

## Producer decision (AC1)

Decision recorded 2026-10-27 (intake round 1 answers):

| Question | Answer | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Enforcement option | **Option 3 — upstream generic fix in the test skill (`run_tests.py` `full_suite_commands`), tracked as SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB** | One resolution rule serves every project; no repo-local pin to maintain. Producer constraint: projects can supply local test-skill configuration, so a pinned `.pi/test-config.json` `suiteCommands` must stay authoritative (returned verbatim, gap surfaced as a notice) — captured as D3/AC3 on the upstream item. |
| Coverage breadth (Q2) | **All** `.pi/skills/*/tests` directories | Identical cost today (only one skill ships tests) and future skill suites are covered without another change. |

Rejected alternatives, for the record:

- **Option 1 — `.pi/test-config.json` `suiteCommands` with a second pytest
  command.** Would give the same coverage, but setting `suiteCommands` makes
  `changed_scope_commands()` return `None` (`run_tests.py:645`), so every
  `implement.py finish` falls back to the **full** suite (~302 s instead of a
  changed subset) — a silent local-loop regression (AC4).
- **Option 2 — root `pytest.ini` with `testpaths = . .pi/skills/*/tests`.**
  Works (testpaths entries are pytest initial paths and bypass `norecursedirs`)
  and keeps the finish loop fast, but it is a per-repo workaround that every
  project with local skills would have to repeat.
- **Option 4 — document the gap.** Leaves 529 tests unenforced.

## Problem statement

`run_tests.py --scope full` resolves the suite to a single canonical command,
`pytest -q -r a --disable-warnings`, executed from the repo root. pytest's
default `norecursedirs` (`*.egg .* _darcs build CVS dist node_modules venv`)
prunes every dot-directory, so `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/` is never
collected. Adding 10 tests there left the published full-suite count unchanged at
**5 264 passed**, while running that directory explicitly collects **529 passed**
in roughly 6 s. Those 529 tests are the only automated guard on
`.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py` — the report the
`audit` skill and the daily 05:00 cron read.

## Users and user stories

- **Implementing agent** — "As an agent changing the usage-analysis parser, I want
  the push gate to refuse my change when a skill test breaks, so I do not ship a
  silently wrong report."
- **Producer / audit** — "As the audit, I want the published full-suite number to
  provably include the skill tests, so 'green' means the same thing in every
  consumer."
- **Operator** — "As the operator, I want the gate cost to stay predictable
  (about +6 s cold) and the local `implement.py finish` loop to stay fast."

## Measured evidence

Recorded 2026-10-25 by LP-0MVOAQDB4002D56G, re-verified for this brief on the
current tree:

| Observation | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Gate command | `pytest -q -r a --disable-warnings` (scope `full`) | `.worklog/cache/*/metadata.json` |
| Full-suite total before/after adding 10 skill tests | **5 264 passed / 5 264 passed** (unchanged) | item comment, LP-0MVOAQDB4002D56G |
| `pytest .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests` | **529 passed**, ~6 s | item comment, LP-0MVOAQDB4002D56G |
| Skill test modules | 6 `test_*.py` + `conftest.py` + `fixtures.py` + `__init__.py`, all git-tracked | `git ls-files .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests` |
| Cold full suite on this host | ~302 s | `docs/dev/git-hooks.md` |
| Per-command timeout | 1800 s | `.pi/test-config.json` |
| pytest version | 9.0.3 | host interpreter |

Mechanism, confirmed against the installed pytest source
(`_pytest/main.py:425` `pytest_ignore_collect`, `Dir.collect` at :552): the
`norecursedirs` check is skipped for *initial paths* (paths given on the command
line or via `testpaths`), which is exactly why the explicit run collects the 529
tests while the recursive run cannot see them. The upstream fix exploits this by
emitting the skill directories as an explicit pytest initial path.

## Existing state

- `.pi/test-config.json` contains only `{"timeoutPerCommand": 1800}` — no
  `suiteCommands`, no `groups`. This is deliberate: it keeps the convention
  detection path active so the upstream rule applies here.
- There is **no** root `pytest.ini` / `pyproject.toml` / `setup.cfg` / `tox.ini`,
  so the gate runs with rootdir = repo root and no ini file; recursion from the
  root picks up `tests/` and all of `proxy/` (including
  `proxy/proxy/test_home_page.py`) → 5 264 tests.
- `proxy/pytest.ini` registers the proxy markers (`slow`, `live`,
  `live_port_kill`, …); it is only loaded when pytest is invoked from `proxy/`,
  not by the root gate run.
- Only one of the three project-local skills ships tests
  (`proxy-usage-analysis`); `proxy-log-debug` and `start-proxy` have none. Its
  `tests/conftest.py` puts `../scripts` on `sys.path`, so collection works from
  any cwd inside the repo.
- `.githooks/pre-push` delegates suite resolution to `run_tests.py` (repo-local
  first, then the global install) and runs `--scope full`; the audit skill's F3
  check resolves the same commands through `full_suite_commands()`.
- Upstream work item **SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB** (SorraAgents) carries the resolution
  change, its precedence rules (pinned `suiteCommands` verbatim + notice,
  `testpaths`/`addopts` de-duplication, groups/types untouched) and its own tests
  and docs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Decision recorded.** ✅ Recorded above (option 3 + all skill test
  dirs), with the rejected alternatives and their runtime-cost rationale, and
  mirrored to the upstream item.
- **AC2 — Enforcement proven end-to-end.** After SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB ships and
  its runner is installed, add a deliberately failing test under
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests` on a scratch branch, observe the push
  to `dev` being **refused** by the gate, then remove the test and confirm green.
  Record the gate output excerpt (naming the skill-test command) in a comment.
- **AC3 — Counts published separately.** Publish the repo-test count, the
  skill-test count and the combined total as three distinct numbers in a
  work-item comment and in `docs/dev/git-hooks.md`, so the surfaces can never be
  conflated again.
- **AC4 — No finish-gate regression.** `implement.py finish`'s change-scope
  selection still returns a subset command (not a full-suite fallback) for a
  representative change, and the measured cold-gate runtime after the change is
  documented (expected ~302 s + ~6 s).
- **AC5 — Drift guard.** An automated test in `tests/` asserts that the resolved
  full-suite command set includes a command targeting
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests` (importing the installed
  `run_tests.py` through its resolved path and calling `full_suite_commands()` —
  no nested suite execution), so a future configuration or resolution change
  cannot silently re-blind the gate.
- **AC6 — Documentation.** `docs/dev/git-hooks.md` documents that the gate covers
  repo tests *and* project-local skill tests, the split counts, the measured
  runtime, and the rule that this repo must not pin `suiteCommands` (doing so
  would drop the skill tests until they are listed explicitly). Affected code
  comments updated.
- **AC7 — Full suite green.** The full project test suite passes with the change
  applied — repo tests plus the skill tests, no regressions, no collection
  errors, and no duplicate collection.

## Constraints

- **Blocked-by SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB.** Do not implement a repo-local workaround
  (no `suiteCommands`, no root `pytest.ini` `testpaths`) — the decision is
  explicitly the upstream route.
- **Project-local test-skill configuration stays authoritative.** llm's
  `.pi/test-config.json` keeps only `timeoutPerCommand`. Adding `suiteCommands`
  here would make the skill tests silently drop out again (the pinned list wins
  by design) and would also disable changed-scope selection.
- **Repository boundary.** No edits to the global skill install
  (`~/.pi/agent/skills`) or to `skill/` from this repo; the code change belongs
  to SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB.
- **Single source of truth.** Suite-command resolution stays in `run_tests.py`;
  do not fork it inside `.githooks/pre-push`.
- **Cost budget.** Skill tests add ~6 s to a ~302 s cold gate; `timeoutPerCommand`
  stays 1800.
- UK English in all written output.

## Desired change

No product-code change in this repo. After the upstream item ships: verify
enforcement (AC2), publish the three counts (AC3), confirm the finish loop is
unchanged (AC4), add the drift-guard test (AC5), update
`docs/dev/git-hooks.md` (AC6), and run the full suite (AC7).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `tests/test_git_hooks.py` (or a new `tests/test_skill_suite_gate.py`) — AC5
  drift guard calling the resolved `run_tests.py` `full_suite_commands()`.

# Goal

Run the verified tool over the post-fix night window (2026-10-24 20:00 → 2026-10-25 07:00 IST) and produce the measured numbers required by the parent item's AC1–AC3, including attribution of any residual stale polls.

## Context

The capacity-signal fix (commits 56a3a28a, 2d2b6b51 of LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM) was live in the proxy from ~10:35 IST on 2026-10-24. The fixed window is 2026-10-24 20:00 → 2026-10-25 07:00 IST (Europe/Dublin), matching the 2026-10-22 pre-fix evidence window. Log coverage for the window is confirmed present: `proxy.log.2026-10-24_17.gz` (20:00→23:37), `proxy.log-2026-10-25_00` (23:37→23:59), `proxy.log.2026-10-24_22` (00:00→04:37), `proxy.log.2026-10-25_04` (04:37→07:00). Pre-fix baseline: `slots_stale` 79.5%, `capacity_hint=saturated` 82.3% while zero local streams ran, herdr dispatched 1 item in ~9 h; Oct 20/21 baseline ≥10 dispatches/night.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: Over the post-fix night window 2026-10-24 20:00 → 07:00 IST (comparable to 2026-10-22 20:00-07:00 local), `slots_stale` is <5% of status polls (was 79.5%), and `capacity_hint=saturated` is only observed while the proxy has live local work. If the target is not met, report the measured value and why.
- AC2: `capacity_hint` distribution for the window, with every `saturated` observation shown to coincide with live local work (zero violations, or a timestamped list of violations with the proxy's concurrent activity at each).
- AC3: herdr downtime dispatches on a genuinely idle GPU night reach the Oct 20/21 baseline (≥10 dispatches/night) with the same work-item queue (was 1 in ~9 h) — report the dispatch count for this window with queue/state evidence and the exact log lines/derivation used.
- AC4: Any residual stale polls are attributable (documented cause, e.g. transient /slots 500 vs idle-model unload) in the nightly usage report — every residual `slots_stale=true` poll attributed (including proxy-restart cases), or explicitly stated as unattributable with the evidence limits.
- AC5: Raw measurement artifacts (tool `--json` output, coverage verdict, per-metric derivations) saved under a named directory in `~/proxy-usage-reports/` and referenced by the report.

## Key Files

- `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log.2026-10-24_17.gz`, `proxy.log-2026-10-25_00`, `proxy.log.2026-10-24_22`, `proxy.log.2026-10-25_04` — window evidence.
- `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py` — the measurement tool (from the sibling verification child).
- `~/proxy-usage-reports/` — artifact + nightly-report surface.
- `proxy/docs/per-slot-status-verification.md` — status semantics reference for attribution.

## Constraints

- Read-only measurement: never kill/restart the proxy; use logs only (parent constraint).
- Window is fixed: 2026-10-24 20:00 → 2026-10-25 07:00 IST.
- Use the verified tool from the sibling child; no ad-hoc regex archaeology for the headline numbers (spot-checks to confirm are fine).

## Definition of Done / Verification

- All parent ACs AC1–AC3 numbers produced with the tool and artifacts saved (AC5 here).
- Attribution list present (AC4 here) — completing parent AC3.

# Grafana dashboard GPU panel queries a memory pool that exists

**Headline:** the only GPU memory panel on the dashboard charts a pool nothing
publishes; repoint it at the GTT/VRAM series the host does export, relabel it
honestly, and replace the test that currently protects the broken expression
with one that fails for any unpublished series.

## Problem statement

The "GPU VRAM Usage (bytes)" panel in
`monitoring/grafana_llama_memory_dashboard.json` queries `rocm_vram_total_bytes`
and `rocm_vram_used_bytes`, series that no process on this host publishes
(`amd/rocm-exporter` has no release artefacts, so the scrape job is commented out
in `monitoring/prometheus.yml`). The panel is therefore permanently empty, the
README documents it as a known gap, and
`TestGrafanaDashboardVramPanel::test_vram_panel_has_rocm_expr` asserts the broken
expression — the test protects the defect rather than the behaviour.

## Users

Primary user: the operator of this host, monitoring local model memory pressure
through Grafana once it is deployed (it is not deployed today, so the dashboard
is currently a reviewable artefact rather than a live screen).

User stories:

- As the host operator, I want a GPU memory panel whose series actually exist, so
  that opening the dashboard shows current memory use instead of "No data".
- As the host operator, I want the panel labelled so I can tell that models live
  in GTT (system RAM mapped for the GPU) and that the VRAM carve-out is a ~1 GiB
  BIOS reservation, so the panel does not imply the carve-out is the model pool.
- As a reviewer, I want a test that fails when a panel selects a series no
  exporter publishes, so this class of defect cannot be reintroduced silently.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Every GPU memory panel target selects a series this host publishes.** Each
   expression in the panel resolves to one of the node_exporter textfile series
   produced by `gpu-metrics.service` — `gpu_gtt_used_bytes`,
   `gpu_vram_used_bytes`, `gpu_vram_total_bytes` — and no `rocm_` series remains
   in either dashboard copy (verify: `grep -c 'rocm_' monitoring/grafana_llama_memory_dashboard.json monitoring/grafana/dashboards/grafana_llama_memory_dashboard.json`
   reports `0` for both).
2. **Title and legends reflect what is shown.** The panel title names both pools
   (GTT and the VRAM carve-out) without implying VRAM is the model pool; each
   target's `legendFormat` names its series and the VRAM legends mark the ~1 GiB
   carve-out. The dashboard's `version` field is bumped.
3. **The test asserts published series, not `rocm_*`.** `TestGrafanaDashboardVramPanel`
   derives the set of GPU series the documented sampler actually emits (running
   the documented `gpu-metrics-textfile.sh` against fixture sysfs, reusing the
   existing `TestGpuMetricsSamplerAndUnit` helpers) and asserts every expression
   in the panel selects a member of that set. A panel selecting a series the
   sampler does not publish fails. The obsolete `test_vram_panel_has_rocm_expr`
   is removed, `test_dashboard_has_vram_panel` still passes, and a test asserts
   the two dashboard copies stay byte-identical (verify: temporarily reintroducing
   `rocm_vram_used_bytes` in the panel makes the class fail).
4. **Documentation matches reality.** The "Known gap" paragraph in
   `monitoring/README.md` § 4 is replaced by a short statement of which series
   the panel now uses; `proxy/README.md`'s dashboard panel list mentions the GPU
   memory panel; all related documentation (README sections, code comments,
   docstrings) reflects the change, including that GTT is the pool models map
   into and the VRAM carve-out is not.
5. **Full project test suite passes** with the change (`/skill:test`), with no
   regressions elsewhere.

## Constraints

- **Dashboard, tests and docs only.** No new exporter, daemon, scrape job or
  systemd unit: the required series are already served by
  `gpu-metrics.service` → `node_exporter` textfile collector
  (`127.0.0.1:9100`).
- **Never reintroduce the dead route.** No `rocm-exporter` scrape job and no
  `rocm_vram_*` expression anywhere; existing guards
  (`FORBIDDEN_RULE_SERIES`, `test_no_scrape_job_for_unpublished_exporter`) must
  keep passing.
- **Follow the established GTT reasoning** from `monitoring/gpu_memory_alerts.yaml`:
  GTT is the pool models map into (~36 GiB of a 128 GiB pool in normal
  operation); the VRAM carve-out is 1 GiB with ~0.3 GiB used.
- **One Y-axis, bytes only.** The panel shows bytes; a GTT fraction
  (`gpu_gtt_used_bytes / 137438953472`) stays in the README query cookbook rather
  than being mixed into a bytes panel.
- **Two dashboard copies must stay identical.**
  `monitoring/grafana_llama_memory_dashboard.json` and
  `monitoring/grafana/dashboards/grafana_llama_memory_dashboard.json` are
  byte-identical today; both are edited together.
- **No visual verification is possible**: Grafana is not deployed on this host
  (`monitoring/README.md` § 4), so correctness is established by the tests and by
  matching the documented series list.
- UK English in all written output; **CHANGELOG.md is out of scope** (ship
  pipeline manages it).

## Existing state

Panel 4 of `monitoring/grafana_llama_memory_dashboard.json`:

```json
{
  "type": "graph",
  "title": "GPU VRAM Usage (bytes)",
  "id": 4,
  "targets": [
    {"expr": "rocm_vram_total_bytes", "legendFormat": "total"},
    {"expr": "rocm_vram_used_bytes", "legendFormat": "used"}
  ],
  "datasource": "Prometheus",
  "gridPos": {"h": 8, "w": 24, "x": 0, "y": 18}
}
```

- `proxy/tests/test_monitoring_deployment.py` (lines 855–891) contains
  `TestGrafanaDashboardVramPanel` with `test_dashboard_has_vram_panel` (title must
  contain "vram") and `test_vram_panel_has_rocm_expr` (asserts one of
  `EXPECTED_ROCM_EXPORTER_METRICS` appears in the expression).
- `EXPECTED_ROCM_EXPORTER_METRICS` (line 65) lists the three `rocm_vram_*`
  names; `FORBIDDEN_RULE_SERIES` (line 59) already bans `rocm_vram_` in **rule**
  expressions — the dashboard is not covered by it.
- `TestGpuMetricsSamplerAndUnit` (lines 1138–1215) already extracts the
  documented sampler from `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service`, runs it against a
  fixture sysfs directory via `GPU_SYSFS`, and asserts the emitted series are
  exactly `gpu_busy_percent`, `gpu_vram_used_bytes`, `gpu_vram_total_bytes`,
  `gpu_gtt_used_bytes`.
- `monitoring/README.md` § 4 ends with the "Known gap" paragraph (line 296) naming
  this panel; § 3 ("Resulting GPU series: …") and the query cookbook above it
  already document `gpu_gtt_used_bytes` as the pool that matters.
- `proxy/README.md` (line 2901) lists the dashboard panels without the GPU panel.
- `grep -c 'rocm_'` currently reports `2` for each dashboard copy, so the AC 1
  verification command is a real regression guard (`0` after the change).

## Desired change

Replace the two `rocm_vram_*` targets with the published textfile series and
label them honestly. Keep the panel's `id`, `type`, `datasource`, `gridPos` and
the dashboard's `title`/`schemaVersion` untouched — only targets, title, legends
and `version` change. Sketch:

```json
{
  "type": "graph",
  "title": "GPU memory: GTT (models) and VRAM carve-out (bytes)",
  "id": 4,
  "targets": [
    {"expr": "gpu_gtt_used_bytes", "legendFormat": "GTT used (models live here)"},
    {"expr": "gpu_vram_used_bytes", "legendFormat": "VRAM used (1 GiB carve-out)"},
    {"expr": "gpu_vram_total_bytes", "legendFormat": "VRAM total (1 GiB carve-out)"}
  ]
}
```

Rewrite the test class to assert *published* series (derived from the sampler run,
so the test tracks the real exporter rather than a hand-maintained list), and
update the two README references. Title keeps the word "VRAM" so
`test_dashboard_has_vram_panel` remains a meaningful guard.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `monitoring/grafana_llama_memory_dashboard.json` — replace panel 4 targets/title/legends; bump `version`.
- `monitoring/grafana/dashboards/grafana_llama_memory_dashboard.json` — identical copy, edited in the same commit.
- `proxy/tests/test_monitoring_deployment.py` — rewrite `TestGrafanaDashboardVramPanel` (lines 855–891), reuse/lift the sampler helpers from `TestGpuMetricsSamplerAndUnit` (lines 1138–1215), retire `EXPECTED_ROCM_EXPORTER_METRICS`.
- `monitoring/README.md` — § 4: delete the "Known gap" paragraph (line 296), state the series the panel uses.
- `proxy/README.md` — line 2901: add the GPU memory panel to the panel list.

## Related work

- **LP-0MQMH11AO002IIID** — Add GPU VRAM/ROCm metrics to Prometheus and Grafana
  dashboards (completed): introduced this panel and its `rocm_vram_*` expression,
  i.e. the origin of the defect.
- **LP-0MVO8DOHP008FL48** — GPU utilisation must come from power, and two alert
  groups are dead (completed): same root cause fixed for **rule files**
  (`gpu_memory_alerts.yaml` now uses `gpu_gtt_used_bytes`); the dashboard panel
  was left behind, which is why it needs its own item.
- **LP-0MVO8DORX004P05G** — Docs: record the deployed monitoring stack (completed):
  documented the gap in `monitoring/README.md` § 4.
- **LP-0MQR554O60033BGF** — Deploy Prometheus and Grafana instances (completed):
  deployment context; Grafana is still not running on this host.
- **LP-0MQ53C4HU003FCZ3** — Grafana panel for 5xx counter (completed): precedent
  for panel + test changes in this dashboard.
- `monitoring/gpu_memory_alerts.yaml`, `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service` — the
  authoritative list of published GPU memory series.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk: a permissive test.** Asserting only "the expression mentions `gpu_`"
  would pass for an unpublished `gpu_*` name. Mitigation: derive the published
  set by executing the documented sampler (single source of truth), and include
  the negative check in AC 1.
- **Risk: only one copy edited.** Two identical dashboard files exist and only
  `monitoring/grafana_llama_memory_dashboard.json` is read by the current test, so
  the provisioning copy could silently drift. Mitigation: AC 3's equality test.
- **Risk: legend/title churn breaks the title guard.** Renaming the panel away
  from "VRAM" would defeat `test_dashboard_has_vram_panel`. Mitigation: keep
  "VRAM" in the title.
- **Assumption:** panel stays a bytes gauge with no derived fraction — mixing
  units on one axis is what the README query cookbook exists to avoid.
- **Assumption:** Grafana remains undeployed, so no live datasource/panel
  screenshot validation is expected in this item.
- **Risk: dashboard churn.** Editing `id`, `datasource`, `gridPos` or the
  dashboard `title` would break panel identity for anyone with a saved Grafana
  instance. Mitigation: the change is limited to targets, panel title, legends
  and `version`.
- **Risk: rule-file drift.** Nothing in `monitoring/*.yaml` or
  `prometheus.yml` should change; if the implementation finds itself editing a
  rule file or scrape job, the change has left this item's scope.
- **Scope-creep watch:** the following are real defects but **out of scope**
  (recorded, not fixed here): (a) the "llama-server RSS (bytes)" panel charts
  `llama_process_rss_bytes`, which the proxy publishes as `0`
  (LP-0MVO8DOHP008FL48 territory); (b) `proxy/README.md` § Alerting Rules still
  references the deleted `monitoring/llama_memory_alerts.yaml` and its 90 GB
  threshold; (c) `docs/gpu-offload-verification.md` § 6 tells readers to watch
  `rocm_vram_usage_bytes` / `rocm_device_temperature_celsius`, which nothing
  publishes. (b) and (c) are tracked separately as **LP-0MVQ6NQU9009LY2Y**
  (Stale monitoring references).
- **Open question (non-blocking):** whether a second panel should chart GTT as a
  fraction of the 128 GiB pool. Recorded as a possible follow-up, not part of
  this item, because the pool size is a hard-coded constant that changes only
  with the BIOS carve-out.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

Interview round 1 (intake, 2026-10-27) — no blocking questions asked: the seed
context, `monitoring/README.md` § 4, `monitoring/gpu_memory_alerts.yaml` and the
sampler documentation already answer the "why GTT" and "which series exist"
questions. Decisions taken and recorded for audit:

- Q: Which series should replace `rocm_vram_*`? — Answer (agent, evidence
  `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service` metric table and
  `TestGpuMetricsSamplerAndUnit::test_sampler_publishes_the_documented_series`):
  `gpu_gtt_used_bytes` as the primary series, plus `gpu_vram_used_bytes` /
  `gpu_vram_total_bytes` for carve-out context. **Recommended:** all three — GTT
  is where models live, VRAM names the pool the old panel claimed to show.
- Q: Should both dashboard JSON copies be updated and guarded? — Answer (agent,
  evidence: `diff` of the two files is empty, both are 66 lines): yes, both, with
  an equality test. **Recommended:** update both plus the test.
- Q: Should the published-series guard cover all dashboard panels? — Answer
  (agent, evidence `FORBIDDEN_RULE_SERIES` and AC 3): no, only the GPU memory
  panel. `llama_process_rss_bytes` *is* published (as `0`), so a
  published-series check would not catch it; that is a separate pinned-series
  problem recorded in the scope-creep watch list. **Recommended:** scope the
  guard to the panel this item fixes.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MVQ6NQU9009LY2Y** – Stale monitoring references: deleted llama_memory_alerts.yaml and unpublished rocm_vram_usage_bytes in docs (open)
- **LP-0MQMH11AO002IIID** – Add GPU VRAM/ROCm metrics to Prometheus and Grafana dashboards (completed)
- **LP-0MVO8DOHP008FL48** – GPU utilisation must come from power, and two alert groups are dead (rocm_vram_*, llama_process_rss_bytes=0) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts.txt` — matched: acceptance, actually, add, agent, already (+333 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_nothink.txt` — matched: acceptance, actually, add, agent, already (+333 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_think.txt` — matched: acceptance, actually, add, agent, already (+333 more)

# Intake Brief — Lease fairness: cap consecutive prefill-lease renewals so one session cannot monopolise the local gate

## Problem statement

One session can hold the local gate for many minutes by chaining
`lease_extended_during_prefill` renewals (with or without a first byte), while
concurrent sessions queue up to the contention budget (60–120 s) and fall back
to paid remote providers. Observed 2026-10-23: session `herdr-1792789684-1790656-13656`
held the local lease ~19 min with continuous renewal while three other sessions
queued 60 s and fell back (`contention_queue_fallback_after_queue
reason=local_lease_active`). The lease must be fairly shared: a bounded hold per
session while others are queued, without regressing warm-slot affinity for
successful turns.

## Users

- **Operator** (primary) — wants the local gate shared fairly across sessions so
  no single session monopolises capacity while others pay remote fallback costs.
  - *User story*: "As an operator, I want a session that has held the local gate
    for an unbounded chain of `progress=None` renewals to be cut off near the
    prefill deadline, so queued sessions get served instead of falling back."
  - *User story*: "As an operator, I want a session that already delivered a
    first byte but keeps renewing across turn boundaries to give queued sessions
    a bounded window, while still keeping its warm slot priority."
- **Concurrent sessions** (secondary) — experience queue-then-fallback latency and
  cost when a monopoliser holds the gate.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. [impl] A bounded hold bound exists for `lease_extended_during_prefill ...
   progress=None` chains: total prefill-hold without a first byte is capped
   near `local_prefill_deadline_seconds` (e.g. deadline + overhead), with a
   regression test. The bound applies regardless of extension signal
   (including `in_flight=True`), and releases the gate so a queued session is
   admitted.
2. A session that has already delivered a first byte may not extend its lease
   indefinitely while other sessions queue: a bounded-max hold (or yielding)
   with a regression test — **mechanism pending producer decision (Appendix Q1)**
   — release at request boundary / between-turn yield is the recommended shape;
   no mid-stream kill of a producing stream (Appendix Q2).
3. Warm-slot affinity for successful turns is preserved: a session that recently
   completed a local turn still re-acquires the same slot/warm KV (no regression
   against `prefill_extended_streams` behaviour). With the recommended
   between-turn yield this is preserved via the contention-queue retention
   mechanism (`contention_queue.retained` waiters ahead of newcomers).
4. The 24 h post-fix window measurement re-run after the change shows the
   productive-holder denial class materially reduced (target: -50 % vs the
   classification baseline) while `ac1.wedge_denials` stays 0. Re-run via
   `scripts/prefill_recovery_verification.py --measure`; baseline/window
   confirmed in Appendix Q3.
5. [test] Validation: hermetic regression tests plus the full project test suite
   pass with the new changes (continuous-renewal monopoliser bounded; first-byte
   session bounded without mid-stream truncation; warm-slot affinity preserved;
   `0`-valued knobs restore pre-change behaviour).
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes —
   `proxy/config.yaml` knob comments, `proxy/README.md` / `proxy/docs/routing.md`
   lease section, and `docs/dev/prefill-recovery-verification.md` for the AC4
   re-run procedure and results.

## Constraints

- **No mid-stream kill of a producing stream** (recommended; pending Q2): a
  stream that has delivered a first byte and is actively generating occupies a
  physical slot in a single-slot pool — pre-empting it would truncate the
  holder's turn and would not free the slot for real work anyway.
- **Warm-slot affinity is intentional** (epic assumption, LP-0MVLHMCN6003GAMD):
  lease retention for explicit sessions with cache history must survive the
  fairness change.
- Extension signals that are **not** progress must not count as progress: an
  open in-flight request already does not refresh `last_progress_ts`
  (LP-0MVKUKFSO008GI6O AC4); the fairness cap must not reintroduce a wedge-shape
  that defeats the 180 s no-progress watchdog.
- The wedge defect shape is tracked separately (LP-0MVPUBQLQ008GJOV, in-request
  re-dispatch after prefill-deadline cancellation re-arming the lease); the
  fairness cap here must not mask or duplicate that defect.
- Config-consistent: any new knob is documented in `proxy/config.yaml` (and the
  cheap/fast profiles if changes are needed) with a rollback default.

## Existing state

- `_extend_lease_during_prefill` (router_helpers.py) pushes `expires_at` out by
  `local_dispatch_lease_prefill_buffer_seconds` (30 s) on numeric progress
  advance, observed slot liveness, or the caller's own in-flight marker —
  every 10 s poll. There is **no per-session hold counter** and no
  cap on consecutive `progress=None` renewals.
- `local_prefill_deadline_seconds: 120` cancels a no-first-byte dispatch in the
  router and releases the lease (`lease_released reason=prefill_deadline`); its
  `_watchdog_no_progress` bound is 180 s. These are per-request backstops and do
  not bound a session's *chain* of renewals across requests/turns.
- 24 h post-fix window (LP-0MVM83F6X0005V8S, commit 458c7fc6):
  `local_dispatch_denied` = 306 short-hold / 141 stale-owner / 2
  productive-holder / 0 wedge; max productive hold 190 s, max unproductive
  164 s; `prefill_extended_streams` = 1975.
- Later window (2026-10-26, comment LP-C0MVPUC5E2003ZVF5): 3 wedge-attributed
  denials separated out to LP-0MVPUBQLQ008GJOV (blocking-edge input).

## Desired change

- **AC1 (recommended, no open decision):** track per-dispatch
  no-first-byte hold start; refuse extension (all signals) once
  `now − first_acquisition >= bound`, where bound defaults to
  `local_prefill_deadline_seconds + buffer` (150 s at defaults) behind a new
  config knob `local_dispatch_no_first_byte_hold_seconds`. Release the gate at
  the bound so a queued session is admitted; regression test.
- **AC2 (mechanism pending producer decision, Appendix Q1/Q2):** recommended
  shape is a request-boundary yield — cap same-session re-acquisition while the
  contention queue holds other-session waiters (with retention priority
  preserving warm-slot affinity), rather than a mid-stream kill. Alternative
  considered: hard-abort the holder's stream at the bound (rejected: destructive,
  oversubscribes the physical slot).
- **AC4:** re-run `scripts/prefill_recovery_verification.py --measure` on the 24 h
  window after deploy; gate on productive-holder denials −50 % vs the
  2/306/141 baseline with `ac1.wedge_denials == 0`.

**Key Files:**

- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — `_extend_lease_during_prefill` (~line 1491),
  `_get_prefill_lease_config` (~line 1015), `mark_local_first_byte`,
  `_try_acquire_local_dispatch` (~line 2679), `_dispatch_lease_key` (~line 50):
  hold tracking, extension cap, re-acquisition gating.
- `proxy/proxy/contention_queue.py` — queued-waiter visibility for the
  yield/deny decision (`retained` waiters, `contention_queue_retention`).
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `local_lease_active` deny/fallback paths
  (~lines 6890–11490).
- `proxy/config.yaml` — `local_prefill_*` section (deadline 120 s, thrash
  cooldown 600 s), new fairness knobs.
- `scripts/prefill_recovery_verification.py` — `ac1` attribution for AC4
  (`productive_holder_denials`, `wedge_denials`).
- Tests: `proxy/tests/test_prefill_lease_extension.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_lease_truthfulness.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_contention_queue_retention.py`.

## Related work

- LP-0MVLHMCN6003GAMD (completed, in_review) — "Post-fix local gate still
  denies queued sessions"; its 2026-10-25 producer decision on AC1 (option A
  restated the wedge AC) routed option B's fairness work to this item. No open
  dependency edge (that item is terminal); recorded as provenance only.
- LP-0MVPUBQLQ008GJOV (open, intake_complete) — in-request local re-dispatch
  after deadline cancellation re-arms the lease (the wedge narrow defect);
  fairness cap alone does not fix that re-dispatch — linked, not duplicated.
- LP-0MVKUKFSO008GI6O (completed) — in-flight signal no longer refreshes
  `last_progress_ts`; `proxy/tests/test_lease_truthfulness.py` pins the
  contract the fairness cap must preserve.
- LP-0MVKUKFHH005UDWL (completed) — post-deadline prefill-thrash cooldown
  (per-session), the per-session precedent for fairness knobs.
- LP-0MVK35HBI003SB3Z (open) — lease-gate shape attribution in idle-admit
  measurement (feeds AC4 classification).
- Docs: `docs/dev/in-flight-lease-hold-characterisation.md` (superseded),
  `docs/dev/contention-queue-lease-retention.md`,
  `docs/dev/prefill-recovery-verification.md`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep:** the in-request re-dispatch wedge (LP-0MVPUBQLQ008GJOV) is a
  separate defect; verify the fairness change does not paper over it. New
  observation opportunities (e.g. per-hold-content time series) go to new work
  items, not this one.
- **False kill of a legitimate long prefill:** the no-first-byte cap must sit at
  or above the deadline so it cannot fire before the deadline's own cancellation;
  genuine long prefills (>180 s observed) still need the in-flight/liveness
  extension, so the cap targets *chains spanning multiple requests*, not one
  long prefill.
- **Warm-slot regression from AC2:** the between-turn yield must route the
  holder's next request back to the same slot/warm KV via retention; a naive
  lease-drop between turns would evict KV and reintroduce re-prefill thrash.
- **AC4 measurement variance:** 24 h windows are noisy; the −50 % target is
  directional, and `ac1.wedge_denials == 0` is the hard gate.
- **Interaction with the thrash cooldown (600 s):** a refused extension plus the
  per-session `local_prefill_thrash_cooldown_seconds` could compound into a long
  local skip for the affected session; the cap must not stack multiplicatively
  with the cooldown into a self-inflicted local outage.
- **Assumption:** defaults for new knobs preserve current behaviour except the
  bounded hold, so a misconfig is rollback-safe (`0` disables a knob).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Which mechanism should AC2 use to bound a first-byte session's hold while
  others queue?" — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION (producer)** — recommended: (a)
  request-boundary yield — cap same-session re-acquisition while the contention
  queue holds other sessions, holder re-queues with retention priority; vs (b)
  hard max session hold that aborts the next extension; vs (c) per-request lease
  cycle only (extensions never outlive the request). Research: single-slot pool
  physically cannot share a slot mid-generation; observed max productive hold
  190 s < 300 s wedge bound; `_try_acquire_local_dispatch` allows same-session
  re-acquisition unconditionally, which is the AC2 gap.
- Q2: "May the fairness bound ever pre-empt (kill) a stream that has already
  delivered a first byte and is still producing?" — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION
  (producer)** — recommended: No — never kill a producing stream for fairness;
  AC2's bound applies at request boundaries / extension refusal, not mid-stream.
  Evidence: a 19-min monopoliser *did* serve local streams; killing truncates
  the holder's turn and frees no physical slot.
- Q3: "What is the baseline and verification window for AC4's −50 % target?"
  — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION (producer)** — recommended: reuse the
  LP-0MVM83F6X0005V8S 24 h post-fix classification baseline
  (2 productive-holder / 306 short-hold / 141 stale-owner) and the same
  `scripts/prefill_recovery_verification.py --measure` window shape (24 h
  post-deploy), with the implementer/operator confirming the window start.
  Research: description baseline is the 2026-10-23 post-fix window; the
  2026-10-25 window added 3 wedge denials attributed to LP-0MVPUBQLQ008GJOV,
  which the AC re-run must exclude.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MR9G183O004SJLO** – Add local_owner_session_id to /llama/local/status endpoint (completed)
- **LP-0MSJ7W7YE003HETO** – Hermetic tests: prefill-progress lease extension (completed)
- **LP-0MV0MM5R60025XZE** – Cap exhaustion retry timer at 60 minutes for clients (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `proxy/README.md` — matched: abort, aborts, ac1, ac2, ac4 (+326 more)
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — matched: 0mvkukfhh005udwl, 0mvkukfso008gi6o, abort, aborts, ac1 (+319 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts.txt` — matched: abort, ac1, ac2, ac4, acceptance (+316 more)

# Router `/slots` HTTP 400s — `?model=` resolution path (86 residual router 400 responses)

**Priority:** medium (as filed) · **Type:** bug (broken behaviour: router answers `HTTP 400` for `/slots`) · **Scope decision:** guard-only (intake answer Q1 = **B**)

## Problem statement

llama.cpp's router answers `GET /slots` with HTTP 400 whenever it cannot resolve a model for the query — either the request omits `?model=` entirely, or `?model=` names a model id/alias the router does not recognise or that is not loaded. The original omission was fixed for the status handler (LP-0MSHW2AXJ009DO3S) and the router-proxied 500 storm was fixed by routing proxy polls to the child port (LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF); a residual, previously un-attributed class of router-responder `GET /slots ... 400` responses (86 in the 2026-10-26 window) was split out into this item.

## Agreed scope (intake answers)

- **Q1 = B (guard-only).** Fix the model-less call sites and the hard-coded model default, add guard tests, and record attribution from existing log/metric evidence. **No new per-query instrumentation** in this item — that work is deferred to **LP-0MVTDMXXH005D5D5**.
- **Q2 = A.** A `?model=<id>` 400 for a legitimately **unloaded/unrecognised** model is *expected truth* (the documented "definitively model absent" signal the proxy already fail-opens on). It is **documented, not eliminated**. Only **model-less / unknown-id** 400s are defects in scope.
- **Q3 = A.** AC4 is verified over a **fresh 24 h window** using the `scripts/slots_500_triage.py` responder split (no instrumentation), after deploy + `/skill:start-proxy --restart`, recorded as a work-item comment.

## Current evidence (measured 2026-10-29, live `/var/log/llama-proxy` + proxy `/metrics`)

- **The 400 class has largely stopped since the parent fix.** In the current `llama-server.log` (router started 2026-10-23 22:04), router-responder `/slots` lines are: **400=102, 500=33, 200=29**, child-responder `200=11779`. The last router 400 sits at position 8087; **zero router `/slots` lines in the final ~18,600 lines** — all recent polling is child-responder. Historical files show the pre-fix rates: `.4.log` (993 400s ≈ 1 day), `.1.log` (172), `.2.log` (115).
- **Proxy-side metric confirms no current 400s:** `llama_slots_query_failures_total{reason="http_400"}` = 0 since proxy start (2026-10-29 00:10); current reasons are `timeout` (663) and `unknown` (2). `llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total` = 0.
- **Live probe (3 read-only requests):** `GET /slots` (no param) → **400**; `GET /slots?model=NOPE` (unknown id) → **400**; `GET /slots?model=Qwen3` (loaded id) → **200** (log lines 31528/31529/31537).
- **llama.cpp logs no query string on the router line** — `srv log_server_r: done request: GET /slots 127.0.0.1 400` is identical whether or not `?model=` was sent (verified empirically). Attribution of *individual historical events* is therefore impossible from `llama-server.log`; the achievable AC1 evidence is a **static call-site audit plus log/metric bounding** (this is precisely why instrumentation is deferred to LP-0MVTDMXXH005D5D5).
- **Router model ids are presets, not one name:** `/models` returns `Qwen3`, `mxbai-embed`, `Qwen2.5-7B`, `Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-Next-GGUF:Q5_K_M`, … with `status.value` per model — confirming that a hard-coded `"Qwen3"` default is not a valid universal resolution.

## Root-cause candidates (code-level, still present today)

1. **Model-less `/slots` call sites** (each 400s if it targets the router):
   - `proxy/proxy/backend_health.py:242` — `_probe_local_endpoint_http` `/health`→`/slots` fallback, no `?model=`.
   - `proxy/proxy/backends/llama.py:212` — `_probe_gpu_wedge` probes `http://{host}:{port}/slots` model-less (targets a child port, so benign today; the rule is unenforced).
   - `proxy/proxy/compaction_summarizer.py:55` — `_probe_slot_capacity_sync(llama_port)` defaults to **8080 (the router port)** — a model-less router 400 per call; reached only via the local summarizer fallback (inert while `models.compact` is configured, `proxy/config.yaml:936`).
2. **Hard-coded default model instead of `/models`-derived id:** `_discover_local_child_port` (`router_helpers.py:5570`) and `_check_slot_availability` (`router_helpers.py:5795`) fall back to the literal `"Qwen3"` when no model is known. If the router preset id differs, that `?model=` is unresolvable → router 400.
3. **Expected (benign) 400 class — out of scope per Q2=A:** `?model=<id>` for an unloaded model returns 400 by design (`slots_failure_is_definitive_model_absent`, `observability.py:603`), e.g. the cold-start probes recorded in LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF AC4 §2. Documented in AC5, not fixed.
4. **Attribution observability gap — deferred to LP-0MVTDMXXH005D5D5:** `_query_slots_detail`/`_query_slots_progress` (`observability.py:695/:773`) swallow non-200s silently (no failure metric, debug log only).

## Users and impact

- **Operators** see phantom 4xx in the llama-server access log and cannot tell a proxy defect from an expected "model not loaded" answer; the F3-era 400s (527/day) were indistinguishable from real failures.
- **Orchestrators** (`/llama/local/status` consumers: herdr downtime worker, web UI) — no functional impact today (status path passes `?model=` and fail-opens), but any future model-less probe on the router port silently degrades to "0/0 slots".

User story: *As an operator, I want no proxy path to send a `?model=` the router cannot resolve, and the expected "model not yet loaded" 400 to be documented as such, so a genuinely missing parameter can never masquerade as a capacity or health problem.*

## Desired change

1. **No model-less `/slots`** from any proxy call site: the three sites above pass the resolved model, or skip the query when no model is loaded (keep the existing fail-open behaviour).
2. **Resolve the model from the router's `/models` ids/presets** (`srv.current_model` → `/models` id match, case-insensitive; alias/preset mismatch tolerated) instead of the hard-coded `"Qwen3"` default at `router_helpers.py:5570` and `:5795`.
3. **Guard tests** that make regressions impossible (see AC3).
4. **A documented model-resolution rule** in the docs, including the expected unloaded-model 400 semantics.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Attribution by audit + evidence.** Every proxy call path that can emit a router-responder `GET /slots ... 400` is enumerated with the exact model string it would send (static audit of `/slots` construction sites + the responder-split/metric evidence above), and the finding is recorded as a work-item comment — including an explicit statement that individual historical events cannot be attributed from `llama-server.log` (query string not logged; instrumentation deferred to LP-0MVTDMXXH005D5D5) and a re-check that no non-proxy client (config/monitoring/cron/scripts) polls the router `/slots` directly.
- [ ] **AC2 — No model-less proxy `/slots`.** None of `backend_health.py:242`, `backends/llama.py:212`, `compaction_summarizer.py:55` issues `/slots` without `?model=`; each passes the resolved model or skips the query when no model is loaded. The hard-coded `"Qwen3"` defaults at `router_helpers.py:5570`/`:5795` are replaced by `/models`-derived resolution (default retained only as a documented last resort).
- [ ] **AC3 — Tests.** New tests assert: (a) no constructed proxy `/slots` URL omits `?model=`; (b) an unknown/alias-mismatched model cannot silently produce a 400-retry loop (fail-open once, never a loop); (c) the model-less call sites pass the model or skip against a router-mode responder stub.
- [ ] **AC4 — Verification window.** Router-responder `GET /slots ... 400` count is **0** over a fresh 24 h window after deploy + restart, measured with `scripts/slots_500_triage.py`'s responder split and recorded as a comment; any non-zero event must be attributed to the expected unloaded-model class (Q2=A) or an AC1-listed call site — an unexplained event reopens the item.
- [ ] **AC5 — Tests + docs.** Changed-scope and full project test suite pass (via the test skill); `proxy/README.md` and `docs/dev/slots-500-triage.md` document the model-resolution rule (`?model=` from `/models` ids/presets; router 400 semantics for *missing* vs *unknown* vs *unloaded* model).

## Out of scope (linked, not this item)

- **Per-query instrumentation** (caller tag + `http_400` metric on the detail/progress paths) — **LP-0MVTDMXXH005D5D5**.
- **Eliminating expected unloaded-model 400s** (e.g. a `/models` status pre-check) — rejected at intake (Q2=A); documented as expected behaviour.
- Upstream llama.cpp router semantics (F3 option 3) — out of scope per LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF Q1.
- The 24 h `router:500 == 0` verification — LP-0MVP7HX2S008IU57 (separate item/window).

## Constraints

- No llama.cpp changes; a 400 for a missing/unknown/unloaded model is upstream semantics to work within.
- No new per-request log-scanning cost, and **no new required instrumentation** in this item (deferred, LP-0MVTDMXXH005D5D5).
- Must not weaken fail-open / "definitively model absent" behaviour (LP-0MSI06HPB0043MV1, `slots_failure_is_definitive_model_absent`).
- Worktree-isolated implementation only (implement skill); restart only via `/skill:start-proxy --restart` after deploy; the AC4 window starts after that restart.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the residual 400 events were emitted by the proxy's own polls in the pre-fix window (router fallback) plus acknowledged cold-start probes; no non-proxy client polls the router `/slots` directly (no such poller found in `proxy/config.yaml`, `monitoring/`, `crontab`, or `scripts/`). AC1 explicitly re-checks this.
- **Risk (medium):** "skip the query when no model is loaded" could hide a genuine capacity regression behind fail-open; mitigation: AC3 loop-guard test plus the AC4 window.
- **Risk (low):** replacing the `"Qwen3"` default could change which child port resolves for other models; mitigation: resolve from `srv.current_model`/`/models` ids, keep the default only as a documented last resort, and cover with a test.
- **Risk (low):** without instrumentation (Q1=B) the AC4 window can only bound the class, not attribute it per event; the residual risk is explicitly accepted by the producer and covered by the deferred item.
- **Scope-creep risk:** instrumentation, `/models` pre-checks, and alert rules are adjacent ideas — recorded as LP-0MVTDMXXH005D5D5 and rejected options, not folded in.

## Existing state

- `_query_slots` (`observability.py:556`) passes `?model=` when *model* is known and **records** `http_400` failures; the status handler (LP-0MSHW2AXJ009DO3S) and SSE broadcast resolve to the child port (LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF AC2).
- `_query_slots_detail`/`_query_slots_progress` (`observability.py:695/:773`) pass `?model=` when *model* is known but record **no** failure metric on non-200.
- `_discover_local_child_port` / `_check_slot_availability` (`router_helpers.py:5570/:5795`) hard-code the `"Qwen3"` default model.
- Parent evidence (LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF AC4 §2): 3× router 400 at cold start, "the known residual 400 class tracked by this item".
- Verification tooling: `scripts/slots_500_triage.py` (responder split), `proxy/tests/test_slots_500_triage.py`.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/backend_health.py:242`, `proxy/proxy/backends/llama.py:212`, `proxy/proxy/compaction_summarizer.py:55` — model-less `/slots` call sites to fix
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — `_discover_local_child_port` (`:5570`) / `_check_slot_availability` (`:5795`) hard-coded `"Qwen3"` default → `/models`-derived id
- `proxy/proxy/observability.py` — `_query_slots` (`:556`, `?model=` + metric precedent), `slots_failure_is_definitive_model_absent` (`:603`, semantics to preserve)
- `scripts/slots_500_triage.py` + `proxy/tests/test_slots_500_triage.py` — responder-split AC4 measurement
- `proxy/README.md`, `docs/dev/slots-500-triage.md` — model-resolution rule + expected-400 documentation
- `proxy/tests/` — new guard tests (AC3)

## Related work

- LP-0MSHW2AXJ009DO3S — original `/slots` `?model=` omission (status path; completed) — partial overlap only; this item covers the residual call sites, not a redo
- LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF — parent: rotation-proof child-port discovery, every call site through it (completed; this item split from its answer Q3)
- LP-0MVTDMXXH005D5D5 — **follow-up (new):** caller tag + `http_400` metric on the detail/progress query paths (deferred instrumentation, Q1=B)
- LP-0MVP7HX2S008IU57 — verify `router:500 == 0` over 24 h (separate acceptance window)
- LP-0MTCMEV1G0022A35 — F3: `/slots` 500-storm triage (background: "527 HTTP 400s are router responses when it cannot answer /slots with a resolvable model")
- LP-0MSI06HPB0043MV1 — fail-open status when no model is loaded
- LP-0MTP1FQXH004JYEF — child-port discovery model filtering (embed vs Qwen3)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Scope (full / guard-only / forensics-first)?** — Answer (producer, 2026-10-29, interactive reply): **B — guard-only.** Fix the model-less call sites and add the "no proxy `/slots` without `?model=`" test; record attribution from existing logs; do not add instrumentation. Research basis: live 2026-10-29 responder split (zero router `/slots` lines in the final ~18,600 log lines), `llama_slots_query_failures_total{reason="http_400"}=0` since proxy start, and three direct probes (no param → 400, unknown id → 400, loaded id → 200).
- **Q2 — Are expected 400s (`?model=<id>` for an unloaded model) in scope for elimination?** — Answer (producer, 2026-10-29): **A — no.** Eliminate only model-less/unknown-id 400s; unloaded-model 400s are expected truth and are documented as such (AC5). Research: `?model=<unloaded id>` → 400 is upstream router semantics; the proxy already treats it as the definitive "model absent" signal (`slots_failure_is_definitive_model_absent`).
- **Q3 — AC4 acceptance signal?** — Answer (producer, 2026-10-29): **A — fresh 24 h window with router-responder 400 == 0**, measured via `scripts/slots_500_triage.py` after deploy + restart and recorded as a comment (mirrors LP-0MVP7HX2S008IU57); any event must be attributed to the expected class or an AC1 call site.
- **Q4 — Where does the deferred attribution instrumentation go?** — Derived action (producer answers Q1=B, Q3=A imply attribution stays log-based in this item): created **LP-0MVTDMXXH005D5D5** (discovered-from this item) for the caller tag + `http_400` metric on the detail/progress paths. Source: intake agent, recorded for traceability.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MSHW2AXJ009DO3S** – Fix /slots endpoint query: llama-server returns HTTP 400 without ?model=, so /llama/local/status always reports 0/0 slots (completed)
- **LP-0MNA7FYH4001ZUR4** – Router-mode llama-server integration (completed)
