## Goal

As an operator I need the proxy to publish **slot occupancy** (total slots, busy
slots, per-slot 0/1 state, in-flight tasks and the age of the last successful
sample) on its existing `/metrics` endpoint, so that "GPU power was high" can be
attributed to llama-server work and gaps in the sample stream stay visible.

## Context

Parent: LP-0MVNWUEY8008XM6W. This child is the **workload half** of the parent:
Power/VRAM/GTT already arrive via node_exporter (`gpu-metrics.service` +
`gpu_compute_rules.yaml`), but nothing publishes slot state — verified
2026-10-29: `curl localhost:8000/metrics | grep llama_slots_` returns only the
existing `llama_slots_query_failures_total` / `llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total`
counters, and `curl localhost:8000/slots` is 404.

Reuse, do not rebuild:

- `proxy/proxy/observability.py::_fetch_slots_payload` — TTL caching (1 s),
  single-flight coalescing, bounded follower wait, failure backoff (5 s).
- `proxy/proxy/observability.py::_query_slots_detail` — per-slot
  `slot_id` / `is_processing` extraction (returns `[]` on failure, so the
  sampler must not treat that as "zero slots").
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py::_resolve_local_slots_target` — child-port
  discovery plus the throttled fallback counter, so the sampler does not traverse
  the router and re-introduce the cancel-500 behaviour (LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF).
- `proxy/proxy/metrics.py` — the existing optional-`prometheus_client` pattern
  (module-level `None` gauges, guarded registration, no-op when the library is
  absent).

Known trap: a failed query must produce **no gauge write at all** (absent/stale),
never `llama_slots_busy 0`. The heartbeat
`llama_slots_sample_timestamp_seconds` is what makes staleness queryable.

## Minimal implementation

- New gauges in `proxy/proxy/metrics.py`: `llama_slots_total`,
  `llama_slots_busy`, `llama_slot_busy{slot="<id>"}`, `llama_slots_in_flight_tasks`,
  `llama_slots_sample_timestamp_seconds`; register under the same `if _enabled:` guard.
- New `record_slot_occupancy(snapshot | None)` helper plus a
  `_slot_metrics_loop()` task in `observability.py` (or `backends/llama.py`),
  started from the proxy lifespan only when metrics are enabled; interval from
  `server.llama_slot_metrics_interval_seconds` (default 10 s, documented in
  `proxy/config.yaml` next to the wedge-detector keys).
- Remove per-slot labels for slots no longer present in the payload, so a
  restarted llama-server does not leave ghost `slot=` series.
- `llama_slots_in_flight_tasks` = slots that report an assigned task: count
  `id_task >= 0` when the build publishes it, else count `is_processing: true`
  (this build publishes no `id_task` — verify live and document the fallback in
  the metric docstring).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Parent AC1 (restated in full):** The proxy publishes slot occupancy series on `/metrics` — total slots, busy-slot count, per-slot 0/1 busy state, in-flight task count and a last-successful-sample timestamp — refreshed by a sampler loop with a configurable interval (default 10 s); a failed `/slots` query leaves the metrics absent/stale rather than reporting zero busy slots, and the failure remains visible through the existing failure counter.
- [ ] The proxy publishes slot occupancy series on `/metrics` — total slots, busy-slot count, per-slot 0/1 busy state, in-flight task count and a last-successful-sample timestamp — refreshed by a sampler loop with a configurable interval (default 10 s); a failed `/slots` query leaves the metrics absent/stale rather than reporting zero busy slots, and the failure remains visible through the existing failure counter.
- [ ] The series are registered only when `prometheus_client` is importable, and a test proves the proxy still serves `/metrics` (and the sampler does not raise) when the library is absent.
- [ ] The sampler loop reuses the coalesced `/slots` path and child-port discovery (`_fetch_slots_payload` + `_resolve_local_slots_target`); no second HTTP client and no new listening port are introduced, and the /slots timeout budget stays ≤ the existing 2 s default.
- [ ] `llama_slots_sample_timestamp_seconds` advances only on a successful sample, so the age of the last successful slot sample is queryable and a stalled sampler is distinguishable from idle slots.
- [ ] Per-slot `slot=` labels are cleaned up when a slot disappears from the payload (asserted by a test that shrinks the slot count).
- [ ] Unit tests cover sampler interval configurability (config default and override), healthy publication of every gauge, failure → no write plus incremented `llama_slots_query_failures_total{reason=...}`, heartbeat non-advance on failure, and the optional-client no-op path; each asserts observable values.
- [ ] On a live host `curl -s localhost:8000/metrics | grep '^llama_slots'` shows the new series with plausible values (recorded in the completion comment).
- [ ] Changed-scope tests pass via `/skill:test`.

**Key Files:**

- `proxy/proxy/metrics.py`
- `proxy/proxy/observability.py` (coalesced `/slots` path; loop lives here or in `proxy/proxy/backends/llama.py`)
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` (see `_resolve_local_slots_target`, no change expected)
- `proxy/config.yaml` (`server.llama_slot_metrics_interval_seconds`)
- `proxy/tests/test_gpu_telemetry_sampler.py` (new)
- `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service` (must stay accurate — expected to need no change)

## Notes

Risk carried from the parent brief: a 10 s sampler adds load to an endpoint that
has produced 1 392 timeout failures on this host. Mitigation is reuse of the
coalesced path, the short timeout, and the configurable interval — do not add a
dedicated poller that bypasses coalescing.

data.description:
## Goal

As an operator (or an agent writing PromQL) I need **one shared definition** of
"the GPU is doing our local model's work" — power at compute level *and* at least
one llama-server slot busy — expressed as a Prometheus recording rule, so the new
CLI, alerts and ad-hoc queries cannot drift into three different definitions.

## Context

Parent: LP-0MVNWUEY8008XM6W (AC3). `monitoring/gpu_compute_rules.yaml` already
records the power-only `gpu:computing:bool` (`gpu:power_watts:amdgpu >= bool 90`)
with `promtool` behavioural tests in `monitoring/tests/gpu_rules_test.yml`. That
series is kept unchanged for comparison; this child adds the combined rule on top
of it and on `llama_slots_busy` published by the sibling sampler child.

**Label-matching trap (found while planning):** the two inputs come from
*different scrape jobs* — the power series carries `instance="localhost:9100"`
(node_exporter) and `llama_slots_busy` carries `instance="localhost:8000"`
(llama-proxy). A naive `and` / `on(instance)` join matches nothing and the rule
silently yields **no series at all** (which would look like "unknown" forever, or
in a dashboard like "never computing"). Use label-agnostic vector matching —
e.g. `gpu:computing:bool * on() group_left() (llama_slots_busy >= bool 1)`, or an
equivalent form — and prove it with a `promtool test rules` case whose input
series carry those distinct `instance` labels.

Keep the missing-data semantics: when `llama_slots_busy` is absent (sampler down,
proxy down) the rule must produce **no series**, not `0`. Absence is `unknown`,
and 0 is "idle" — conflating them is exactly what the parent forbids.

## Minimal implementation

- Add `gpu:computing_workload:bool` to `monitoring/gpu_compute_rules.yaml` plus a
  header paragraph on the join semantics and the gap behaviour.
- Extend `monitoring/tests/gpu_rules_test.yml` with the cases below.
- No change to `monitoring/prometheus.yml` is expected (the rule file is already
  loaded); confirm with `promtool check config`.
- Do **not** add `gpu_busy_percent` anywhere (guard already enforces this).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Parent AC3 (restated in full):** Computing time is defined as `power >= 90 W AND at least one slot busy`, expressed once as a Prometheus recording rule that the CLI, alerts and ad-hoc PromQL all share (asserted by a `promtool test rules` case in `monitoring/tests/gpu_rules_test.yml`); the output also shows the power-only fraction so the two definitions can be compared, and `gpu_busy_percent` contributes to no computation (a regression test asserts no rule file or CLI expression uses it as a utilisation input).
- [ ] Computing time is defined as `power >= 90 W AND at least one slot busy`, expressed once as a Prometheus recording rule (`gpu:computing_workload:bool`) that the CLI, alerts and ad-hoc PromQL all share, with the existing power-only `gpu:computing:bool` preserved unchanged for comparison.
- [ ] A `promtool test rules` case in `monitoring/tests/gpu_rules_test.yml` asserts the recording rule's 0/1 values, including a case whose input series carry the two different `instance` labels (`localhost:9100` power, `localhost:8000` slots) so a label-matching regression fails the test.
- [ ] Rule cases cover: power ≥ 90 W with 1+ busy slots → 1; power ≥ 90 W with 0 busy slots → 0; power < 90 W with busy slots → 0; power exactly at 90 W → 1 (boundary); missing `llama_slots_busy` → the recorded series is absent (not 0); missing power → absent.
- [ ] `gpu_busy_percent` contributes to no computation: the rule file contains no reference to it, and the existing `FORBIDDEN_RULE_SERIES` regression test in `proxy/tests/test_monitoring_deployment.py` still passes.
- [ ] `promtool check rules monitoring/gpu_compute_rules.yaml` and `promtool test rules monitoring/tests/gpu_rules_test.yml` pass, and the rule-file header documents why absence must stay absent (no series rather than 0).
- [ ] Changed-scope tests pass via `/skill:test`.

**Key Files:**

- `monitoring/gpu_compute_rules.yaml`
- `monitoring/tests/gpu_rules_test.yml`
- `monitoring/prometheus.yml` (verify only; no change expected)
- `proxy/tests/test_monitoring_deployment.py` (guard must keep passing)

## Notes

Deployed rules only start producing `gpu:computing_workload:bool` after Prometheus
reloads the file; the completion comment should state the reload step
(`systemctl --user reload prometheus`) and verify the series appears with an
instant query.

data.description:
## Goal

As an operator I can run one command — `python3 scripts/gpu_utilisation.py
--window 2h` — and read `computing 32.4% / idle 61.1% / unknown 6.5%, mean 61 W,
max 118 W, peak 3 busy slots`, with `--json` giving an agent the same numbers,
so "how busy was the GPU between 17:00 and 19:00?" is a direct measurement that
does not depend on `proxy.log`.

## Context

Parent: LP-0MVNWUEY8008XM6W (AC2, AC4, AC5, AC6, and the output half of AC3).
The store is the deployed Prometheus (`127.0.0.1:9090`, 90 d retention, 15 s
scrape). A very similar (smaller) reader already exists at
`.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/gpu_busy.py` — reuse its *approach*
(urllib + `/api/v1/query_range`, best-effort JSON, dataclass result) but do not
import from `.pi/` (agent infrastructure, out of bounds); put the code in
`scripts/` and keep the new module self-contained.

**The honesty requirement is the hard part.** `avg_over_time` renormalises over
present samples only, so a 2 h window where the sampler was down for 30 min
reports a *higher* computing fraction than reality and cannot distinguish "idle"
from "nobody was looking". Compute coverage explicitly and report the remainder
as `unknown`:

- expected samples = window length ÷ step (the step actually queried, reported in
  the output next to the 15 s scrape floor);
- present samples = union of the sentinels that prove the pipeline was alive at
  that instant: `up{job="llama-proxy"}`, `up{job="node-exporter"}` and the
  `llama_slots_sample_timestamp_seconds` heartbeat (a sample counts as *observed*
  only when it is fresh within one scrape interval of the evaluation instant);
- `computing` = observed samples where `gpu:computing_workload:bool == 1`;
  `idle` = observed samples where it is `0`; `unknown` = expected − observed.
  The three shares must sum to 100 % by construction (assert it).

Guard: `gpu_busy_percent` must never appear in any expression (the sibling
test-first child adds the guard that scans this file).

## Minimal implementation

- `scripts/gpu_utilisation.py`: `argparse` (`--since`, `--until`, `--window`,
  `--step`, `--prometheus-url`, `--json`), window/step resolution, one place
  holding the query expressions (`QUERIES` dict), arithmetic, human + JSON output.
- Reuse the recorded payloads from `monitoring/tests/fixtures/` in tests rather
  than hitting a live Prometheus; inject the HTTP getter so tests need no network.
- Report both definitions: `computing_pct` (workload rule) and
  `power_only_computing_pct` (`gpu:computing:bool`), plus `peak_busy_slots`
  (`max_over_time(llama_slots_busy[window])`) and `mean`/`max` power.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Parent AC2 (restated in full):** `scripts/gpu_utilisation.py` reports, for an arbitrary window (`--since/--until` or `--window`, `--step`), the computing-time percentage, idle percentage, unknown percentage, mean and max power in watts, and peak concurrent busy slots; `--json` emits the same figures machine-readably.
- [ ] **Parent AC4 (restated in full):** Windows containing missing samples report the missing share as `unknown` (never as idle, never renormalised away); an integration/unit test drives a fixture sample stream with a deliberate gap and asserts the exact computing/idle/unknown split.
- [ ] **Parent AC5 (restated in full):** The CLI produces correct output with `proxy.log` absent — an integration test runs the query path against recorded Prometheus API payloads with no proxy log present, proving the figure is a direct measurement.
- [ ] **Parent AC6 (restated in full):** Unit tests cover window/step selection, threshold and percentage arithmetic (including boundary power exactly at 90 W), Prometheus response parsing/timestamp alignment, gap and partial-coverage handling, and sampler interval configurability; each test asserts observable behaviour rather than non-`None`.
- [ ] `scripts/gpu_utilisation.py` reports, for an arbitrary window (`--since/--until` or `--window`, `--step`, `--prometheus-url` default `http://127.0.0.1:9090`), the computing-time percentage, idle percentage, unknown percentage, mean and max power in watts, and peak concurrent busy slots; `--json` emits the same figures machine-readably as a stable, documented schema.
- [ ] Windows containing missing samples report the missing share as `unknown` (never as idle, never renormalised away); a test drives a fixture sample stream with a deliberate gap and asserts the exact computing/idle/unknown split, and asserts the three shares sum to 100 %.
- [ ] The CLI produces correct output with `proxy.log` absent — an integration test runs the query path against recorded Prometheus API payloads with no proxy log present, proving the figure is a direct measurement.
- [ ] The output also shows the power-only fraction (`gpu:computing:bool`) so the two definitions can be compared, and `gpu_busy_percent` contributes to no computation (the guard test covering this file passes).
- [ ] Unit tests cover window/step selection (including a step larger than the scrape interval and a window shorter than one step), threshold and percentage arithmetic including boundary power exactly at 90 W, Prometheus response parsing/timestamp alignment, gap and partial-coverage handling, and empty/all-unknown windows (explicit exit code and message); each test asserts observable behaviour rather than non-`None`.
- [ ] Invalid input is rejected with a clear non-zero exit: `--until` before `--since`, both `--window` and `--since/--until` given, unparseable duration, and a `--prometheus-url` that does not answer.
- [ ] The reported resolution states the step actually queried and the 15 s scrape floor, so the output never implies second-level fidelity.
- [ ] Changed-scope tests pass via `/skill:test`.

**Key Files:**

- `scripts/gpu_utilisation.py` (new)
- `proxy/tests/test_gpu_utilisation_cli.py` (new)
- `monitoring/tests/fixtures/prometheus_query_range.json` (recorded payloads from the test-first child)
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/gpu_busy.py` (reference only, no edits)

## Notes

Out of scope (parent constraint): feeding these figures into the daily usage
report's "Local model utilization" section — that stays a follow-up item.

data.description:
## Goal

As an operator reading `monitoring/README.md` I can find the new slot series, run
the utilisation CLI from a copy-pasteable example, understand the retention and
resolution limits of the store, and re-measure the power calibration myself after
a hardware, driver or kernel change.

## Context

Parent: LP-0MVNWUEY8008XM6W (AC7, AC8). The README already documents deployment,
the exposure boundary, the PromQL query cookbook and the "why not `amd-smi`"
evidence (LP-0MVSQQO910077LYL). This child adds the workload series, the CLI, the
retention/resolution statements and the calibration procedure, and closes the
documentation gap between the hardware figure (`gpu:computing:bool`) and the
usage report's proxy-inferred `local_busy.busy_pct`.

Two figures must not be conflated (see LP-0MVSPWLLP008AQXZ, which measured a ~27
point divergence): the log-derived figure measures slot occupancy from proxy
events, the hardware+slot figure measures "GPU drew compute power while at least
one slot was busy". The docs must state what each answers and why neither
replaces the other.

## Minimal implementation

  cookbook with `llama_slots_busy`, `llama_slot_busy`, `llama_slots_total`,

  `gpu:computing_workload:bool`; add a CLI section with a real example run.
- New calibration subsection: idle ≈ 40–54 W, computing ≈ 115 W, threshold 90 W,
  and the re-measure recipe (`cat /sys/class/drm/card0/device/hwmon/hwmon*/power1_average`
  while idle and during a known-long generation; update the rule threshold and
  `server.llama_gpu_wedge_power_low_threshold_watts` together).
- Retention/resolution statement: 90 d, history starts when the TSDB was created
  (2026-10-25 19:22 on this host), observed resolution is the 15 s scrape interval
  even though the sysfs sampler writes at 10 s.
- Keep `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service` accurate; update it only if the
  cadence/responsibilities actually change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Parent AC7 (restated in full):** Documentation is updated: `monitoring/README.md` gains the slot series, the CLI usage, the retention statement (90 d, and that history starts when the TSDB was created) and a calibration/re-measure section, plus an explicit note on how computing-time % differs from the usage report's proxy-inferred `local_busy.busy_pct`; code comments and `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service` stay accurate.

- [ ] `gpu_busy_percent` appears in the README only in the "not a utilisation signal" context; a grep assertion in the existing docs test suite (or a new assertion) enforces it.
- [ ] `monitoring/README.md` states the resolution floor (15 s scrape, 10 s sysfs write) and that the CLI reports the step it queried, so no figure implies finer fidelity than the store holds.

This is the last slice: it documents what actually shipped, not the plan. If a
sibling child had to deviate (metric names, flag names, exit codes), the docs
follow the code and the deviation is recorded in the parent's plan changelog.

# Drift guard: resolved full-suite command set must include hidden skill tests

## Goal

An automated test in `tests/` asserts that the resolved full-suite command set
includes a command targeting `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests`, so a
future configuration or resolution change cannot silently re-blind the
dev-push gate (parent AC5).

## Context

Parent: **LP-0MVOBJGB4001TQ8X** — repo full-suite gate never runs
`.pi/skills/*/tests` (529 unenforced tests).

**Blocked by SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB** (cross-store, SorraAgents): upstream
`run_tests.py` `full_suite_commands()` must emit an extra explicit-path pytest
command for project-local skill test directories. This child lands the guard
that would have caught the original gap; it must not start before the upstream
rule is installed, because the assertion is red until then.

## Minimal implementation

- New `tests/test_skill_suite_gate.py`; resolve the runner exactly like
  `.githooks/pre-push`: repo-local `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` first,
  then `~/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py`.
- Import the resolved module with `importlib.util.spec_from_file_location` and
  call `full_suite_commands(REPO_ROOT)` — no nested suite execution.
- Assert exactly one command whose pytest initial path targets
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests`; assert the canonical repo command
  (`pytest -q -r a --disable-warnings`) is still present; assert
  `.pi/test-config.json` has no `suiteCommands` key.
- Failure messages name SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB and `docs/dev/git-hooks.md` so a
  future reader knows what regressed and where the rule is documented.

**Key Files:**

- `tests/test_skill_suite_gate.py`
- `.pi/test-config.json`
- `docs/dev/git-hooks.md`
- `scripts/install_git_hooks.sh`

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Drift guard.** An automated test in `tests/` asserts that the
  resolved full-suite command set includes a command targeting
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests`, and it passes in the repo full
  suite (run via the test skill) once SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB's rule is installed.
- **AC2 — Additive, not a replacement.** The same test asserts the canonical
  repo pytest command is still present, so the skill command is proven
  additive.
- **AC3 — No-pin guard.** The test asserts `.pi/test-config.json` carries no
  `suiteCommands` key, with a failure message explaining that a pin would
  silently drop the skill tests and would also disable changed-scope
  selection.
- **AC4 — Resolver parity.** Runner resolution mirrors `.githooks/pre-push`
  (repo-local first, then the global install); the test imports `run_tests.py`
  through that resolved path and only calls `full_suite_commands()` — it never
  executes a nested suite and completes in well under a second.
- **AC5 — Explicit skip.** If neither runner exists the test skips with a
  reason naming the expected install path (documented limitation, D-P3), so a
  skip stays visible in the report rather than silently passing.


## Dependencies

- **Blocked by SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB** (cross-store) — the resolution rule this
  test asserts.
- No sibling dependency: this is the test-first item for the parent's
  enforcement work.

## Deliverables

- `tests/test_skill_suite_gate.py` (new module, 3–5 tests).

# Prove the dev-push gate refuses a failing skill test

## Goal

Enforcement is proven end-to-end: a deliberately failing test under
`.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests` makes the dev-push full-suite gate
refuse, and removing it restores green (parent AC2). The repo/skill/combined
counts measured during the proof are published as three distinct numbers
(parent AC3, work-item half).

## Context

Parent: **LP-0MVOBJGB4001TQ8X**. **Blocked by SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB** — the gate
cannot refuse a skill-test failure until the upstream resolution rule emits the
extra explicit-path command.

## Minimal implementation

- On a scratch branch in the implementation worktree, add a deliberately
  failing test under `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests`
  (e.g. `test_gate_proof_tmp.py`).
- Force an **uncached** `--scope full` gate run: the runner caches per git
  state and command, so use a fresh git state or remove the matching
  `.worklog/cache` entry, and record which method was used.
- Capture the verbatim gate output excerpt that names the failing skill test
  and both suite commands, then remove the failing test and re-run uncached to
  confirm green.
- Never push the red tree to `origin/dev` (or `main`): use a scratch branch
  plus the documented stdin push simulation in `docs/dev/git-hooks.md` if a
  hook-level proof is wanted.

**Key Files:**

- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py`
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/conftest.py`
- `docs/dev/git-hooks.md`
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py`

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Enforcement proven end-to-end.** After SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB ships and
  its runner is installed, a deliberately failing test under
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests` on a scratch branch makes the gate
  refuse the `dev` push (uncached run), and removing the test confirms green.
- **AC2 — Skill command named.** The same gate output lists both the canonical
  repo pytest command and the `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests` command,
  proving the skill suite is inside the gate's command set.
- **AC3 — Clean after removal.** After the failing test is removed, the same
  uncached run passes and the combined total is recorded.
- **AC4 — Counts published separately.** The repo-test count, the skill-test
  count and the combined total are published as three distinct numbers in a
  work-item comment together with the gate output excerpt.
- **AC5 — No red push.** No push of the red tree to `origin/dev` or `main` is
  attempted; the proof uses a scratch branch and, if needed, the documented
  stdin simulation.


## Dependencies

- **Blocked by SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB** (cross-store).
- After the drift-guard test (test-first ordering).

## Deliverables

- Verbatim gate output excerpt in a work-item comment.
- Three published counts + the uncached-run method used.
- No committed code (the failing probe test is removed).

# Add cooldown-skip metrics to capacity verification tool

## Summary

Make the cooldown-skip evidence re-derivable by the same tool that produces the
capacity numbers, by adding `routing_skip_local reason=prefill_thrash_cooldown`
metrics to `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py` in a strictly additive way.

Parent: LP-0MVRMI5HK00558TB — the before/after measurement AC2 requires and the
AC4 re-measurement. Today the 916-skip / 336-free-GPU baseline was derived with
ad-hoc log greps, so the fix cannot be verified by the same invocation shape.

## Target outcome

One tool invocation reports, over any window, the abandonment → ghost →
cooldown chain: `saturated` without live work, cooldown skips in total, per
session, for `herdr-*` sessions, and how many of those skips happened while the
proxy's own nearest status poll said the GPU was free.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The report gains a **new** additive block (e.g. `prefill_thrash_cooldown`)
  containing at minimum: total `routing_skip_local … reason=prefill_thrash_cooldown`
  skips, distinct skipped sessions, skips for `herdr-*` sessions and their
  distinct session count, and skips whose nearest preceding status poll within
  120 s has `local_in_flight_requests=0` **and** `slots_detail_stale=false`
  (with the sub-count where that poll reads `capacity_hint=idle`).
- The free-GPU attribution rule is exactly the one recorded in the parent's
  Appendix (nearest fresh poll within 120 s), and the rule is stated in the
  report itself so the number is not a magic constant.
- **Strictly additive**: every existing metric keeps its name, definition and
  JSON shape (`saturated_without_live_work`, the hint histogram, stale rate,
  downtime-dispatch counts, existing CSV artefacts). Existing consumers
  (LP-0MVOG6YRA000T9PK, the nightly report) must parse the new output unchanged.
- The new block is emitted in both the human render and `--json`, and any new
  per-event CSV is written only as an *additional* file.
- Missing/gzipped/rotated log handling and window/coverage-gap semantics for the
  new metric match the existing ones — a coverage gap is reported as a gap, not
  as zero skips.
- If the cooldown release log line from the implementation item is present in
  the window, releases are counted by reason; when it is absent (older logs) the
  metric reads zero rather than failing.
- Unit tests cover the parsing, the attribution rule, the coverage-gap
  behaviour, and that the existing metric shapes are unchanged.
- The full project test suite passes with the change, run through the test
  skill (parent AC6; the dev-push gate enforces the full suite).

## Minimal implementation

- `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py`: a `analyse_prefill_thrash_skips()`
  pass over the same line stream, a `prefill_thrash_cooldown` report block, and
  render support; reuse the existing `_status_fields` / `_in_window` helpers.
- Nearest-poll attribution: index the status polls by timestamp once and bisect,
  rather than rescanning per skip.
- `proxy/tests/test_capacity_signal_verification.py`: extend with the new
  fixtures (skip lines, interleaved status polls, gz rotation) and the
  additive-shape assertions.

## Deliverables

- Additive metric + tests, proven on the existing baseline window shape.
- A short note in the parent item giving the exact invocation used, so the AC4
  re-measurement uses the identical shape.

## Dependencies

None (the metric parses log lines that exist today). It must land **before**
the re-measurement item.

## Key Files

- `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_capacity_signal_verification.py`
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` (read-only reference for the skip log line and its fields)

# Re-measure one comparable night and publish before/after

## Summary

Re-run the capacity measurement over one comparable night with the extended
tool and report whether the ghost saturation and the free-GPU cooldown skips are
gone, plus the herdr downtime-dispatch count against the ≥ 10/night target.

Parent: LP-0MVRMI5HK00558TB — AC4, and the before/after half of AC2.

## Target outcome

A published, reproducible report answering: (a) is `capacity_hint=saturated`
with `local_in_flight_requests=0` and `slots_detail_stale=false` ≈ 0
(baseline 247 polls / 2.12 %), and (b) how many cooldown skips still happen
while the proxy's own snapshot says the GPU is free (baseline 336 of 916), and
(c) how many herdr downtime dispatches the night reached against ≥ 10.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC4 — Re-measurement over one comparable night (same tool, same window
  length)** (parent LP-0MVRMI5HK00558TB AC4, restated as this item's outcome).

- Run over a window of the **same length** as the baseline (11 h overnight,
  20:00 → 07:00 local) and state the exact bounds, the deployed commit and the
  proxy start time, so the window is comparable and any deploy mid-window is
  visible.
- Uses the **same tool invocation shape** as the baseline plus the additive
  cooldown block, and states the invocation verbatim in the report.
- Artifacts persisted under a named directory in `~/proxy-usage-reports/`
  (`measurement.json`, `measurement.txt`, the per-poll CSV, and the new skip
  CSV), with the directory path recorded on the parent item.
- Reports **before vs after side by side** for: `saturated`-without-live-work
  polls and rate; total cooldown skips; distinct sessions; `herdr-*` skips and
  sessions; skips with a free GPU and the `idle`/`available_slots=2` sub-count;
  and herdr downtime dispatches for the night.
- When a number misses its target, the report says precisely why, with the
  evidence limits named (as LP-0MVOG7IP80003MLV AC3 did) — never a bare miss.
  In particular: if the herdr dispatch count is below 10, separate "the fix did
  not help" from "the night had less work / the queue was empty".
- Read-only: the re-measurement never restarts, kills or reconfigures the proxy
  to obtain evidence (no blanket `pkill`/`killall` — see project AGENTS.md).
- Verdict recorded on the parent item as a comment, with the headline numbers.

## Minimal implementation

- Pick the first night after the implementation items are deployed and running
  for a full window; record the deploy commit.
- Run `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py` with the documented bounds and
  `--out-dir`, then write the before/after table from the two
  `measurement.json` files.
- Reuse the window tooling of the re-measurement siblings
  (LP-0MVRZDC3Y005JHQJ / LP-0MVSTQT8V002SPRZ) rather than a parallel path; if
  their window shape differs, note the difference.

## Deliverables

- Measurement artifacts directory + published before/after table.
- Verdict comment on the parent, including any residual defect handed to a
  follow-on item.

## Dependencies

- Depends on **Abandoned-slot registry and upstream cancel on abandonment**
  (AC1 behaviour must be deployed).
- Depends on **Fingerprint-scoped cooldown with free-GPU release** (AC2
  behaviour must be deployed).
- Depends on **Add cooldown-skip metrics to capacity verification tool** (the
  metric must exist).

## Key Files

- `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py`
- `~/proxy-usage-reports/<named-directory>/measurement.json`
- `~/proxy-usage-reports/<named-directory>/prefill_thrash_skips.csv`

## Goal

As the proxy operator, I want a session that owns a local slot to log its
**measured** reusable prefix at admission (AC1), so a cold-prefill admission is
visible in the log before it becomes a 120 s deadline cancellation and AC4 rule
(a) becomes evaluable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Measured prefix at admission.** When a session owns a local slot,
  `routing_resident_prefix` logs a **numeric** `n_past_actual` and the derived
  `reuse_ratio` (`min(n_past_actual, estimated_tokens) / estimated_tokens`),
  sourced from the best available measurement — here the `measured_prefill`
  store's last dispatch `total` for that `(model, session)` pair — and labelled
  `residency_source=measured_last_dispatch` so provenance is auditable against
  the live-snapshot `measured` source.
- **Rung order preserved.** `measured` (live `context_tokens`) still wins;
  `measured_last_dispatch` is consulted before the `session_slot` sentinel rung;
  `non_resident` / `unknown` are unchanged.
- **Provenance is auditable in the log.** The emitted line gains an **additive**
  `measurement=` field immediately after `residency_source=`; this item emits
  `measurement=measured` for both measured sources. All existing keys keep their
  relative order and `reuse_ratio=none` remains the numeric-absent form.
- **The gate uses the measurement.** Admission pricing reads the measured
  `n_past_actual` (`min(n_past_actual, estimated_tokens)` reusable) instead of the
  implicit "all tokens reused" assumption, so `reuse_ratio` is a real number and
  a grown prompt can now be denied with `resident_prefix_insufficient` — this is
  the intended AC4 rule (a) signal, not a regression; `local_resident_prefix_min_ratio: 0`
  remains the documented rollback.
- **Fail-open, no fabrication.** `total` of `None`/`0`/non-finite, a missing store
  entry, an unreadable config, or any exception degrades to the existing
  `session_slot` behaviour; nothing raises into the request path and no
  synchronous `/slots` call is added (LP-0MUXTW4MD003TVIC).
- **Tests.** The xfail markers added by `LP-0MVT2PB6U007PKD1` for AC3(i) are
  removed and pass; `proxy/tests/test_local_resident_prefix_admission.py` stays
  green under the changed-scope gate (AC7).
- **Model plumbed.** `_should_skip_local` passes `model_name` into
  `resolve_resident_prefix` (it is not a parameter today), defaulting to `None`
  for existing call sites so behaviour without a model name is unchanged.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Add `model_name: str | None = None` to `resolve_resident_prefix` and thread it
   from the `_should_skip_local` call site (and the reserve/pricing call site if
   present).
2. Add `RESIDENCY_SOURCE_MEASURED_LAST_DISPATCH = "measured_last_dispatch"` and
   include it in `ResidentPrefixFacts.resident`.
3. Insert the new rung between the `context_tokens` rung and the ownership rung,
   guarded by live ownership and `capture_enabled(server_config)` (read lazily and
   fail-open).
4. Add `measurement` to `ResidentPrefixFacts` (default `measured` for measured
   sources) and emit it from `_log_residency_decision`; keep the numeric-absent
   suppression for `None` `n_past_actual`.
5. Remove the AC3(i) xfail marker.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py`
- `proxy/proxy/measured_prefill.py`
- `proxy/proxy/residency.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_local_resident_prefix_admission.py`

  green regression tests.

## Goal

As the verification agent, I want every decision that *cannot* be measured to
say **why** in a closed vocabulary (AC2), so "the ladder cannot measure" is
distinguishable from "there is no slot to measure" and AC4's unmeasured share is
attributable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC2 — Unmeasured is explicit and distinguishable.** A decision that cannot
  be measured logs an explicit, closed-vocabulary reason — exactly one
  `measurement=` value per line, drawn from module-level constants: `measured`,
  `unavailable:no_slot`, `unavailable:no_prior_measurement`,
  `unavailable:stale_view`, `unavailable:capture_disabled`.
- **Precedence is deterministic.** `capture_disabled` (the
  `local_measured_cache_abort_enabled` rollback is off) wins over
  `no_prior_measurement` for a slot-owning session; `no_slot` applies to the
  fresh-view non-resident rung; `stale_view` applies to the `unknown` source
  where the residency view is absent/stale (extending `LP-0MVN4LANP0069QQM`); a
  measured source always reports `measured`.
- **No fabricated numbers.** A non-measurement never logs a numeric
  `reuse_ratio` — the internal `0.0`/`1.0` gate sentinels are never surfaced, and
  the LP-0MVNPZY22008B536 regression (no `reuse_ratio=0.0000` for a session with
  no measurement) stays pinned by its existing test.
- **Backward compatible.** `reuse_ratio=none` is still emitted for every
  non-measurement, `residency_source` values are unchanged, and existing
  assertions/parsers keep working with no change.
- **Fail-open.** An unreadable config or store is treated as enabled/absent, not
  an error; the reason string never raises into the request path.
- **Tests.** The AC3(ii)/(iii) xfail markers from `LP-0MVT2PB6U007PKD1` are
  removed and pass; a table-driven test covers every vocabulary value's trigger;
  suite green under the changed-scope gate (AC7).

## Minimal Implementation

1. Add the vocabulary constants and a `measurement_reason(...)` helper (or
   equivalent derivation inside `resolve_resident_prefix`) so every return path
   sets exactly one reason.
2. Set `ResidentPrefixFacts.measurement` on all four ladder rungs, using
   `capture_enabled(server_config)` for `capture_disabled`.
3. Emit the field from `_log_residency_decision` (added by the measurement-rung
   child) and keep the numeric suppression rule.
4. Remove the AC3(ii)/(iii) xfail markers and add the table-driven vocabulary
   test.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py`
- `proxy/proxy/measured_prefill.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_local_resident_prefix_admission.py`

## Dependencies

- Blocked by `LP-0MVT2PB6U007PKD1` (failing-first tests).

## Goal

As the operator, I want a captured measurement to be **invalidated** when the
session loses its slot, the slot is reassigned to another session, or the model
changes, so the fix cannot trade one fabricated ratio for another (AC2/AC3(iv),
the parent item's highest risk).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Eviction clears.** Every reclaim chokepoint that emits `local_eviction`
  (`router_helpers._record_local_eviction`) clears the
  `(model, session)` measurement for the evicted session, so its next admission
  logs `unavailable:no_prior_measurement` rather than a stale ratio.
- **Slot release/reassignment clears.** `session._free_slot_assignment`
  (used by the lease reclaim and orphan-cleanup paths) clears the session's
  measurement, so a slot reassigned to another session cannot inherit the
  previous owner's prefix size.
- **Model switch does not reuse.** A measurement recorded under model A is never
  read for a dispatch on model B (the store is keyed by model, and the rung reads
  only the request's model); an explicit clear on the model-switch path is added
  where the switch is observable, with the key-scoped lookup as the backstop.
- **Live-ownership guard.** The rung only fires while `_session_owns_slot`
  returns a slot id; a measurement whose session no longer owns a slot is not
  used even if the clear path was missed.
- **AC3(iv) tests pass.** The invalidation fixtures from `LP-0MVT2PB6U007PKD1`
  (eviction, reassignment, model switch) have their xfail markers removed and
  pass, each asserting no numeric `reuse_ratio` is emitted after invalidation.
- **Fail-open.** Clearing never raises and never changes a non-residency
  decision; no extra `/slots` query and no lock held across a dispatch.
- **AC7 — Suite green.** The full project test suite passes with the change
  (enforced by the dev-push gate; no ad-hoc full-suite runs) — including the
  store-cap behaviour and the existing measured-prefill capture tests.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Give `clear_measured_prefill` its first real callers: in
   `_record_local_eviction`, in `session._free_slot_assignment`, and on the
   model-switch path (whatever `(model, session)` pair is losing its slot/model).
2. Have `clear_measured_prefill` accept a `None` model to clear **all** models for
   a session (single-pass over the dict), so call sites that do not know the
   model do not leave orphans.
3. Keep the rung's live-ownership guard as the backstop for a missed clear.
4. Remove the AC3(iv) xfail markers and extend the store clear tests.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/measured_prefill.py`
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`
- `proxy/proxy/session.py`
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py`

- Blocked by `LP-0MVT2PY3J00077W6` (the rung that reads the store).

## Deliverables

- Measurement invalidation on eviction, slot release and model switch, with
  per-path regression tests.

## Goal

As the proxy operator (and the next agent reading the design), I want the
measurement sources, the closed unmeasured-reason vocabulary and the residual
buffered-dispatch limitation documented (AC5), so the new log field is readable
without re-deriving the ladder from code.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Observability grammar.** `proxy/docs/routing.md` (§ observability grammar,
  ~line 821) shows the `routing_resident_prefix` line **including** the additive
  `measurement=` field, enumerates the closed vocabulary
  (`measured`, `unavailable:no_slot`, `unavailable:no_prior_measurement`,
  `unavailable:stale_view`, `unavailable:capture_disabled`), and adds
  `measured_last_dispatch` to the `residency_source` values — matching the
  constants shipped in `proxy/proxy/provider.py` verbatim.
- **Rollout guidance.** `docs/dev/resident-prefix-rollout.md` gains a "what to
  read" note: grep `measurement=` on resident decisions and expect a numeric
  `reuse_ratio` when a prior measured dispatch exists; it states the residual
  limitation (buffered/non-streaming dispatches emit no `prompt_progress`, so they
  stay `unavailable:no_prior_measurement`) and that
  `local_measured_cache_abort_enabled: 0` turns resident decisions into
  `unavailable:capture_disabled` (intended, not a regression).
- **Design doc.** `docs/dev/slot-management-design.md` (ladder/observability
  section, ~line 837) records the new rung between the live-snapshot rung and the
  ownership rung, its measurement source (`measured_prefill` store, `total` of the
  last dispatch) and the invalidation rule (eviction / slot reassignment / model
  switch).

  (`proxy/tests/test_resident_prefix_config_docs.py`) still pass; if any asserts
  the exact grammar line or rung count, it is updated in the same change.
- **Accuracy.** No fabricated claim: the docs say the value is an upper-bound-ish
  proxy (last dispatch's total, same prompt plus decode) and never promise a
  measurement for buffered dispatches.

## Goal

As a proxy maintainer, I want every admission-guard refusal reason pinned on the **free-slot (direct) dispatch path** end-to-end, so a regression cannot relabel a non-ETA refusal as `eta_exceeds_budget_direct` when a local slot happens to be free (LP-0MVRO3AHN002UM1Q AC1/AC3/AC4).

TDD slice: write the failing/extended rows first, then only fix `provider.py` if a row disproves the mapping that landed in `0466f5db`.

## Scope

- `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py` — `_OCCUPANCY_REFUSAL_CASES` (~1127): add `path="direct"` rows; `_assert_occupancy_refusal_contract` (~1222): assert body `reason` verbatim; `_occupancy_row` (~1430) / `_REFUSAL_CONTRACT_ROWS` (~1442): row identity `(reason, path)`; attempt diagnostics and the `local_admission_guard_direct_fallback` log line asserted from `caplog`, never re-derived in the test body.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — read-only unless a row disproves the mapping (then fix the free-slot branch ~12233 and record the commit).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `_OCCUPANCY_REFUSAL_CASES` gains `path="direct"` rows for `prefill_eta_exceeds_deadline` and `prefill_eta_exceeds_safety_budget`, each driven through `proxy_with_fallback` with a free local slot (`_MutableConcurrency(0, 1)`), and the existing `eta_exceeds_budget_direct` row keeps its identity.
2. `_assert_occupancy_refusal_contract` asserts the body `reason` equals the case reason verbatim, not only `X-Local-Fallback-Reason`, so header and body cannot drift.
3. `_occupancy_row` and `_REFUSAL_CONTRACT_ROWS` identify a row by `(reason, path)`, so the direct rows do not break `test_refusal_contract_table_has_exactly_one_row_per_reason` (~1559) and the pinned reason set stays unchanged.
4. Existing queue-path rows keep their expected `Retry-After` / `retry_at` values, and `test_occupancy_refusal_case_table_matches_the_advertised_formula` (~1263) passes for every row including the new ones.
5. Changed-scope test gate green via the test skill; no production change unless a row disproves the mapping.
6. **Direct-path reason pass-through is table-driven and complete.** `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py` drives every admission-guard reason through the **free-slot** (direct) path end-to-end via `proxy_with_fallback` — `prefill_eta_exceeds_deadline`, `prefill_eta_exceeds_safety_budget`, `prefill_budget_exceeded`, and the ETA/budget case — asserting both `X-Local-Fallback-Reason` and body `reason` equal the governing decision reason, with `eta_exceeds_budget_direct` used only where the free-slot ETA/budget bound itself is the cause.
7. **The governing reason reaches the recorded attempt and the dispatch log.** The `local_admission_reject` attempt diagnostics and the `local_admission_guard_direct_fallback ... reason=<token>` log line name the governing reason (not `eta_exceeds_budget_direct`) for the deadline, safety-budget and cold-budget refusals; the line still carries `free_slot=true`.
8. **Regression guard on the label.** A test fails if `eta_exceeds_budget_direct` is (re)emitted as the refusal reason for any non-ETA-budget decision reason, on either path.

## Summary

Follow-up split out of LP-0MVP7HV7Q001AJF8 intake answer Q1 (scope = guard-only, `B`). Attribution of individual router-responder `GET /slots ... 400` events is currently impossible from `llama-server.log` because llama.cpp's router access line omits the query string (`srv log_server_r: done request: GET /slots 127.0.0.1 400` is identical with and without `?model=`, verified empirically 2026-10-29).

## Problem

`_query_slots_detail` and `_query_slots_progress` (`proxy/proxy/observability.py:695`/`:773`) swallow non-200 responses silently — no failure metric, debug-level logging only — so a 400 on those paths is invisible in `/metrics` and `proxy.log`. Only `_query_slots` records `llama_slots_query_failures_total{reason="http_400"}`.

## Desired change

- Record `llama_slots_query_failures_total{reason="http_400"}` (and other non-200 reasons) from the detail/progress query paths, aligned with the existing `_query_slots` precedent.
- Add a cheap caller/tag label (e.g. `path=status|sse|availability|progress|detail`) so a router 400 can be attributed to a call site without per-request log scanning.
- Optionally emit one throttled WARNING carrying the exact URL + model string on a router-responder 400.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A router-responder `/slots` 400 on any proxy query path increments a metric carrying the call-site tag.
- Tests assert the metric/label is emitted on non-200 for the detail and progress paths.
- Alert rules in `monitoring/slots_query_alerts.yaml` are reviewed so the added series does not create alert noise.
- Documentation (`proxy/README.md` slots-status section) mentions the metric and label.
- Full project test suite passes.

Parent: LP-0MVRBQBDF0037OZ5 (Compact before moving from local to remote). Covers parent AC1 (decision half) and AC6 (unit half).

**Goal:** As a proxy maintainer, I want the local→remote boundary compaction contract written down as failing tests before any production code exists, so that the trigger gates, the slot pin and the release ordering are specified by executable assertions rather than prose.

**Target outcome:** a single new test module, `proxy/tests/test_compaction_boundary_remote.py`, that expresses the whole boundary-compaction contract and currently fails for the right reason (missing symbol / missing behaviour), not because of an unrelated import error.

**Definition of done**

- Pass/fail checks
  - The module collects cleanly and every test fails only because the boundary symbols do not exist yet.
  - Decision tests cover: fires for a session with recorded local provenance routed to a `type: remote` provider; does **not** fire for a session with no prior local service; does **not** fire below the minimum-size guard; does **not** fire when `server.remote_boundary_compaction` is `false`.
  - Decision tests assert the machine-readable reason token for every skip path (`boundary_no_slot`, `boundary_slot_unavailable`, `boundary_summarizer_failed`, `boundary_below_guard`, plus the disabled token).
  - Slot-pin tests assert the summariser request body carries the session's assigned `id_slot`.
  - A release-ordering test asserts the session's local lease release precedes the remote stream start.
- Automated tests: the module is run through the test skill (`/skill:test` changed scope) and its red state is recorded on this item.

**Constraints**

- Test-only change: no production behaviour may change in this item.
- Follow the conventions of the existing compaction tests (`proxy/tests/test_compaction_bypass_wiring.py`, `proxy/tests/test_router_helpers_compaction.py`): `pytest` classes, injected fakes for the summariser and estimator, no live llama-server or GPU dependency.
- Tests must be deterministic and fast; no sleeps or network calls.

**Risky assumptions**

- One module can host both the decision unit tests and the later dispatch integration test without becoming unwieldy; if it grows past ~600 lines, split the integration half into its own module during the integration item.
- The summary marker (`<!-- compaction-summary -->` style) and the retention invariant (system prompt + first user message verbatim) stay exactly as `plan_session_compaction` implements them today, so the tests can assert against them.

**Key Files:**

- `proxy/tests/test_compaction_boundary_remote.py` — new test module holding the full contract.
- `proxy/tests/test_compaction_bypass_wiring.py` — reference for fakes/wiring style.
- `proxy/proxy/compaction.py` — the module whose new helper the tests will target.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `proxy/tests/test_compaction_boundary_remote.py` exists and the boundary compaction decision is covered by unit tests that fire only for a session with recorded local provenance, a remote provider type and an estimate above the minimum-size guard.
2. Unit tests assert each skip reason token for the boundary decision, including below-guard suppression and the disabled-knob case.
3. Unit tests assert the summarisation call is pinned to the session's assigned `id_slot` (the slot pin contract), and an ordering assertion proves the release precedes the remote stream start.
4. The new tests are TDD-red before implementation: they fail only because the boundary symbols are absent, and that red state is recorded on this work item.
5. Tests run deterministically with injected fakes — no live llama-server, GPU or network access.
data.title: Test: boundary compaction decision and slot-pin contracts

data.description:
Parent: LP-0MVRBQBDF0037OZ5 (Compact before moving from local to remote). Covers parent AC2 and the release half of AC3.

**Goal:** As the local model's capacity, I want the boundary summarisation to run on the slot the session already owns and that slot to be free the instant the summary is produced, so a session being served remotely never holds local GPU capacity and never borrows another session's warm slot.

**Target outcome:** a slot-pinned local summariser callable and an immediate-release step, both unit-tested in isolation.

**Minimal implementation**

1. `proxy/proxy/compaction_summarizer.py`: a slot-pinned builder (e.g. `build_slot_pinned_summarizer(config, slot_id, llama_port=...)`) that posts to the **local** llama-server chat-completions endpoint with `id_slot: <slot_id>` and the **session's own local model** — not `summarizer_model.llama_model`, because slot ids are per llama-server instance and the Qwen2.5-7B summariser backend has its own slot space (see Risky assumptions). Reuse the existing prompt/transcript/retry/fail-open machinery (`EmptySummary`) rather than reimplementing it.
2. `id_slot` is threaded into the request body and asserted in tests; a `None` slot returns a summariser that never fires and reports `boundary_no_slot`.
3. `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`: a small async helper that, given `srv` and a session id, returns the session's assigned slot (read-only `_assigned_slot_for_session`) and, after the summariser returns (success, failure or timeout), calls `_release_local_dispatch` immediately — before the remote stream starts.
4. Green the C1 slot-pin tests; add release-ordering tests (release recorded before the remote request is issued) and a no-leak assertion on the lease registry.
5. Docstrings state the KV caveat: prefilling the summariser prompt overwrites that slot's KV, acceptable only because the session is leaving local.

**Definition of done**

- Pass/fail checks
  - The summariser request body carries `id_slot == _assigned_slot_for_session(session_id)` and targets the local endpoint.
  - No assigned slot → no summariser call, `boundary_no_slot` reason, and the release helper is still invoked so no stale lease survives.
  - Release happens on summariser completion (success / failure / timeout), not on remote response completion — proven by an ordering assertion.
  - The lease registry holds no entry for the session after the helper returns.
- Automated tests: unit tests for the pin, the no-slot path and the release ordering; all green.

**Constraints**

- Never pin to another session's slot: only the read-only `_assigned_slot_for_session` lookup, never `_slot_id_for_session` (which assigns).
- Never fall back to `models.compact` or a dedicated summariser model on this path (parent AC4).
- Reuse `SlotLockCoordinator` ordering; do not add a second lock.
- Bounded by `compaction_summarizer_timeout`; no new timeout knob.

**Risky assumptions**

- **Slot ids are per llama-server instance, so "the session's own slot" means the main local model's slot, not the Qwen2.5-7B summariser backend's slot.** The summariser therefore runs with the main local model's name against the local endpoint. This is the reading of parent AC2 ("reuses the session's own disposable slot instead of taking another session's slot or a separate summariser model"); it is recorded here so the follow-on wiring item does not silently reinterpret it.
- The slot is idle at the boundary (the session is leaving), so the summariser prefill does not queue behind a long generation; if it does, the timeout bounds the wait and the request fails open.

**Key Files:**

- `proxy/proxy/compaction_summarizer.py` — slot-pinned builder reusing the existing prompt/retry/fail-open machinery.
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — slot lookup + immediate `_release_local_dispatch` helper.
- `proxy/proxy/session.py` — read-only `_assigned_slot_for_session` (reuse, no change expected).
- `proxy/tests/test_compaction_summarizer.py` — reference for summariser test style.
- `proxy/tests/test_compaction_boundary_remote.py` — slot-pin and release-ordering tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The summarisation call is pinned to the local llama-server slot currently assigned to that session (`id_slot` from the session→slot registry), so it reuses the session's own disposable slot instead of taking another session's slot or a separate summariser model; verified by asserting the summariser request carries the assigned `id_slot`.
2. When the session has no assigned slot the summariser is not called and the skip is reported with the `boundary_no_slot` machine-readable reason token.
3. The session's local dispatch lease / slot ownership is released immediately after the summariser returns (success, failure, or timeout) and before the remote response is streamed, verified by an ordering assertion plus a no-leaked-lease assertion on the lease registry.
4. Unit tests cover the slot pin, the no-slot path and the release ordering with injected fakes; no live server or GPU required.
5. Docstrings record the KV-overwrite caveat and the per-instance slot-id reasoning that makes the session's own local model — not the dedicated summariser model — the summarisation target.
data.title: Slot-pinned boundary summariser and immediate lease release

data.description:
Parent: LP-0MVRBQBDF0037OZ5 (Compact before moving from local to remote). Covers parent AC1 (dispatch half), AC3, AC4.

**Goal:** As an agent operator, when a session that has been served locally falls back to a remote provider, I want the compacted history actually dispatched upstream — and when compaction cannot run, I want the untouched history sent with a WARNING that names why.

**Target outcome:** one gated, idempotent, fail-open hook at the remote dispatch point(s), reusing `evaluate_and_apply_compaction` where its semantics fit.

**Minimal implementation**

1. `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`: `async def evaluate_boundary_compaction(srv, config, body_json, session_id, provider_cfg, ...) -> dict` — resolves the knob, reads provenance and the estimate, calls `decide_boundary_compaction`, builds the slot-pinned summariser, runs the summarisation in a worker thread (`asyncio.to_thread`, matching `evaluate_and_apply_compaction`), releases the lease immediately, and rewrites `body_json["messages"]` on success (setting `cache_prompt` and `result`-style metadata keys so the existing `X-Compaction-*` bridge headers can mirror them).
2. `proxy/proxy/provider.py`: call the hook immediately before the remote POST in **both** remote dispatch points — the remote-only cycle (`ptr(...)` near ~:10798) and the mixed local+remote cycle (`ptr_remote(...)` near ~:12430) — after the priority/chain resolution and before `_maybe_record_provider_affinity`.
3. Never double-summarise within one request cycle: reuse the `compaction_evaluated`-style per-request flag (a boundary-specific flag if the assembly flag would mask it) and prove it with a test.
4. Fail-open: any exception, timeout, blank/`EmptySummary` return or absent slot leaves the body byte-identical and dispatches remote; log at **WARNING** with a stable token from `boundary_no_slot`, `boundary_slot_unavailable`, `boundary_summarizer_failed`, `boundary_below_guard`, `boundary_disabled`. No remote summariser fallback.
5. Emit a structured boundary compaction event (`boundary_compaction` / `compaction_event`-style) recording session, slot, est_before/est_after, turns summarised, duration_ms and outcome — reuse `log_compaction_event` rather than a new log format where it fits.

**Definition of done**

- Pass/fail checks
  - Fires once per request when the gates pass, and the compacted list is the body sent upstream (asserted on the object handed to the remote dispatcher).
  - Summariser failure / timeout / empty / exception → identical outgoing body, remote dispatch still happens, one WARNING with the correct token.
  - Knob disabled → hook returns immediately, no provenance read cost worth logging, no summariser call.
  - Second invocation in the same cycle is a no-op.
- Automated tests: unit tests for fire-once, fail-open per failure mode, token correctness, and no-double-evaluation.

**Constraints**

- No client-protocol change: behaviour stays inside the proxy; response headers may mirror the existing `X-Compaction-*` bridge (LP-0MU44KSMS002DBWA / LP-0MTYGZ1DI0004QP8).
- Do not re-enable or call the assembly-time path; if `evaluate_and_apply_compaction`'s trigger semantics do not fit, call `decide_boundary_compaction` directly and record why.
- Latency is charged before remote TTFT: keep the guard and timeout bounds from the earlier items; do not add unbounded waits.
- Fail-open in every branch — the hook must never raise into the dispatch loop.

**Risky assumptions**

- Both remote dispatch points are reachable through a shared helper without a third call site (e.g. `proxy/ui.py` embedding routes); if a third site dispatches remote chat traffic, it is added to the same helper and noted here.
- The request body is the authoritative history at the boundary (the session store may lag by the current turn); the hook therefore compacts `body_json["messages"]` and stores the compacted history via `session_manager.update_messages` + `mark_compacted`, inheriting the post-compaction delta heal (LP-0MTXEED8E003EDM8).

**Key Files:**

- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — `evaluate_boundary_compaction` hook beside `evaluate_and_apply_compaction`.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — the two remote dispatch call sites (~:10798, ~:12430).
- `proxy/proxy/compaction.py` — reason tokens / event logging reuse.
- `proxy/proxy/session_manager.py` — compacted-history update + anchors.
- `proxy/tests/test_compaction_boundary_remote.py` — hook tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When a request for a session with at least one prior locally-served turn recorded in the session store is about to be dispatched to a `type: remote` provider, the proxy evaluates boundary compaction before the remote request is sent and dispatches the compacted message list upstream when compaction succeeds.
2. Summariser failure, timeout, empty/blank summary, absence of an assigned slot or an exception leaves the outgoing history byte-identical to today and still dispatches remote — an empty summary is never injected and turns are never silently dropped (existing `EmptySummary` / `remote_with_guidance` guarantees preserved).
3. No remote summariser fallback: every skip is logged at WARNING with a stable machine-readable reason token (`boundary_no_slot`, `boundary_slot_unavailable`, `boundary_summarizer_failed`, `boundary_below_guard`) and the request proceeds remote untouched.
4. A structured compaction-event log line records session, slot, est_before/est_after, turns summarised, duration and outcome for every boundary evaluation.
5. Boundary evaluation is idempotent per request cycle (exactly one summarisation, no re-evaluation), and unit tests cover fire-once plus each fail-open failure mode.
data.title: Boundary compaction hook on remote dispatch (fail-open)

Parent: LP-0MVRBQBDF0037OZ5 (Compact before moving from local to remote). Covers parent AC6 (integration half) and the default-off regression half of AC5.

**Goal:** As a proxy maintainer, I want an integration test that drives the real failure-to-remote path — session served locally, then escalated — so the trigger, the summariser call count, the compacted body on the wire and the slot release ordering are proven end-to-end rather than only in unit isolation.

**Target outcome:** one integration test module (or a clearly separated section of `test_compaction_boundary_remote.py`) that exercises the dispatch cycles with stubbed HTTP transports, plus the default-off regression test.

**Minimal implementation**

1. Build a harness that (a) creates a session, (b) runs a local completion through the mixed cycle so the session records local provenance, (c) makes the next request bypass local (size or explicit remote-only chain) so it routes remote, with `httpx` transport stubs for the local summariser POST and the remote POST.
2. Assert exactly one summarisation call, that its body carries the assigned `id_slot`, and that the remote POST body carries the summary marker plus the retained system prompt and first user message verbatim.
3. Assert ordering: release of the local lease is recorded before the remote stream starts, and the lease registry holds no entry afterwards.
4. Regression: with `server.remote_boundary_compaction: false`, assert zero summariser calls and a dispatch body identical to the pre-change behaviour.
5. Cover the two unchanged cases: a session with no prior local service, and a session below the minimum-size guard.

**Definition of done**

- Pass/fail checks
  - Exactly one summarisation call per boundary evaluation (no double evaluation in a cycle).
  - Remote request body contains the summary marker and the verbatim retention set.
  - Release precedes remote stream start; no leaked lease.
  - Knob disabled → identical dispatch body, no summariser call (byte-comparison against the un-compacted body).
- Automated tests: the integration module is green via the test skill; no live backend, GPU or network.

**Constraints**

- Use the repo's existing stubbing patterns for `httpx` and the provider/remote cycles; do not add a live-endpoint test.
- Do not weaken or delete existing compaction tests; this item adds coverage only.
- Keep runtime under a few seconds — no sleeps, no retry waits.

**Risky assumptions**

- The mixed cycle can be made to bypass local deterministically (size threshold or a remote-only chain) without depending on GPU state; if not, the remote-only cycle is used and the local provenance seeded through the session manager plus a prior local-dispatch unit path.

**Key Files:**

- `proxy/tests/test_compaction_boundary_remote.py` — integration + regression tests.
- `proxy/tests/test_compaction_bypass_wiring.py`, `proxy/tests/test_compaction_integration.py` — harness patterns to reuse.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — the cycles under test.
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — the hook under test.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. An integration test drives a session that is served locally and then routed remote, asserting exactly one summarisation call for the boundary compaction.
2. The integration test asserts the compacted body (summary marker plus the verbatim retention set) is what reaches the remote provider on the wire.
3. The integration test asserts the session's local dispatch lease is released and, with an ordering assertion, that the release precedes the remote stream start.
4. The boundary compaction is controlled by its own independent knob `server.remote_boundary_compaction` (default `false`) that does not re-enable assembly-time compaction, ships disabled by default in `proxy/config.yaml`, and leaves request handling unchanged when disabled — the regression test asserts no summariser call and an identical dispatch body.
5. A session with no prior local service, and a session below the agreed minimum-size guard, are asserted to dispatch unchanged.

data.description:
## Goal

Give clients a preference value that encodes a **hard cost ceiling**: never dispatch a non-local provider, for any reason and under any capacity verdict — and refuse truthfully when the request cannot be served locally.

discovered-from:LP-0MVNU2KTK009D4AG (producer decision 2026-10-29).

## Problem

The current vocabulary has no "never leave local" value:

| value | deferrable verdict | too-large verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `prefer-local` (default) | may fall through to remote | may fall through to remote |
| `local-preferred` (and legacy alias `local-only`) | refuses / defers | **promotes to remote** (`_promote_too_large_local_request`, `provider.py:6610-6712`) |
| `remote-ok` | local stripped | local stripped |

`local-preferred` deliberately promotes an oversized prompt so the client is not handed a useless capacity 429 (LP-0MVSM06LB001PRU4 / epic LP-0MVSHWL47000EVJY; the 2026-10-25 retry-storm evidence in LP-0MVNTT4X8009IO2X). That is right for a client that wants the work done, but it leaves a client whose requirement is **zero remote spend** — e.g. a herdr worker pinned to the local GPU — with no way to say so: its only options are a silent paid dispatch (`local-preferred`) or no pin at all (`prefer-local`). The 2026-10-25 incident (session `herdr-1792897705-4039879-16152` billed by OpenCode Go) is exactly that client.

The two needs must not share one value: "do not give me a useless 429" and "never spend my remote budget" are different policies, and overloading `local-preferred` is what produced the LP-0MVNU2KTK009D4AG audit conflict.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (vocabulary)** `X-Local-Preference: local-exclusive` parses to a new canonical constant in `admission_reserve.py` (`VALID_PREFERENCES` + documented in the module docstring); unknown values still fall back to `prefer-local`; the existing `local-only` → `local-preferred` alias is unchanged.
- **AC2 (no remote dispatch, any verdict)** With `local-exclusive`, no non-local provider is ever dispatched: not on a deferrable exit (cooldown, residency, thrash, queue cap/expiry, lease/gate denial, quota) **and not on a too-large verdict** (`context_too_large`, `prefill_budget_exceeded`, per-entry `max_context_tokens`). Asserted by a fake transport that records every upstream call (`calls == []`) across both row families.
- **AC3 (chain never stripped)** Unlike `local-preferred`, a `local-exclusive` request's chain is **not** filtered: the local entry stays so the refusal can report truthful diagnostics, and a remote-less chain behaves exactly as today.
- **AC4 (truthful refusal shape)** Deferrable exits keep the existing retryable refusal (429, `X-Local-Route: refused`, `X-Local-Fallback-Reason: <token>`, `Retry-After`/`retry_at` per LP-0MVNTT4X8009IO2X). Too-large exits return the **same stable shape** (429, `X-Local-Route: refused`, `X-Local-Fallback-Reason: context_too_large`) but with `retryable: false`, **no `Retry-After`**, and body guidance to compact the prompt — a capacity retry hint for a prompt that can never fit is the untruthful-timer defect LP-0MVNTT4X8009IO2X exists to prevent.
- **AC5 (traceability)** Each refusal emits exactly one `local_only_refused reason=<token> preference=local-exclusive verdict=<deferrable|too_large> retryable=<bool>` line; `priority_routing` continues to carry `preference=` and `session=`.
- **AC6 (no regression)** `prefer-local`, `local-preferred` and `remote-ok` behave byte-identically to today on every path, including the too-large promotion for `local-preferred`; the existing matrix rows pass unmodified.
- **AC7 (tests)** Table-driven rows for both verdict families × `local-exclusive` (refusal, token, no upstream call, no `Retry-After` on the too-large row), a parser/vocabulary test, and an assertion that the preference appears on the refusal line. Full suite green via the changed-scope gate first.
- **AC8 (docs)** `proxy/docs/routing.md` documents `local-exclusive` in the `X-Local-Preference` section, the too-large refusal (`retryable: false`, compact guidance) and its contrast with `local-preferred`'s promotion; docs asserted against implementation by the existing docs test.

## Constraints

- Reuse, do not rebuild: `_build_local_only_refusal_response()` (`provider.py:6595`), `_stamp_local_route_headers()` (`:6906`), `_note_local_fallback_reason()`, and `admission_reserve.LOCAL_FALLBACK_REASON_TOKENS` as the single token table. No new refusal builder, no new token vocabulary, no new config knob.
- Keep one stable client-facing refusal shape (429 + `X-Local-Route: refused`), per LP-0MVNTJJGX00375VQ; `retryable: false` carries the "do not retry, compact" signal without introducing a second status code.
- Do not weaken the `local-preferred` promotion: this item adds a value beside it, it does not change that policy.
- Repository boundary: log-grep consumers under `.pi/skills/` are verified read-only; breakage is reported as a work item, not edited.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** clients can act on `retryable: false` + compact guidance (the herdr workers already compact; the 2026-10-25 incident shows they retry blindly on a `Retry-After: 1`, so an explicit non-retryable signal is the right affordance).
- **Risk:** a `local-exclusive` client on a permanently oversized prompt now gets a hard 429 instead of a served answer. That is the requested behaviour (hard cost ceiling), and the refusal names the compaction remedy; document it prominently.
- **Risk:** vocabulary growth (fourth value) complicates reasoning. Mitigation: the value is strictly "pin + never promote"; every existing value keeps its documented behaviour, and unknown values still degrade to `prefer-local`.

## Related work

- LP-0MVNU2KTK009D4AG — audit that surfaced the split and the need for a distinct hard-pin value (parent by discovery).
- LP-0MVSHWL47000EVJY — epic introducing `local-preferred` and the deferrable/too-large split.
- LP-0MVSM06LB001PRU4 — too-large promotion (must stay intact).
- LP-0MVNTT4X8009IO2X — truthful retry timing / non-retryable refusals (contract reused).
- LP-0MVNTJJGX00375VQ — refusal shape contract (reused).

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py` — `PREF_*` constants (`:63-79`), `LEGACY_PREFERENCE_ALIASES` (`:76`), `parse_preference()` (`:649`), `LOCAL_FALLBACK_REASON_TOKENS` (`:107`), `stamp_route_headers()`.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `_local_preference_pins_local()` (`:6554`), `_promote_too_large_local_request()` (`:6610`), choke points (`:10412`, `:11096`), `_build_local_only_refusal_response()` (`:6595`), `_log_local_only_refusal()` (`:6552`).
- `proxy/tests/test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py` — `_DEFERRABLE_ROWS` / `_TOO_LARGE_ROWS` row families.
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` — `X-Local-Preference` (`:1158`), `X-Local-Route` (`:1173`), exit table (`:1245`).
data.title: Feature: local-exclusive — hard cost-ceiling pin that refuses instead of promoting to remote

# Log the resolved snapshot and sidecar paths in `slot_ratio_seed`

## discovered-from: LP-0MVK0E8C40035FG3

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want each `slot_ratio_seed` line to carry the snapshot path it
resolved (or the candidate paths it tried) and whether the sidecar was present,
so the remaining per-session cause of `missing_sidecar` / `missing_snapshot` is
attributable from logs instead of inferred from code inspection.

## Why (evidence)

The verdict on LP-0MVK0E8C40035FG3 (docs/dev/slot-ratio-seed-verdict-LP-0MVK0E8C40035FG3.md)
proved from 4,488 decisions that the seed path always fails at the lookup
(`missing_sidecar` 75.8 %, `missing_snapshot` 24.2 %; `found`, `expired`,
`prefix_mismatch` all 0). It identified two provable writer-side gaps (the
eviction save path writes no sidecar; the request path skips the sidecar when no
usage block was measured) but could not split the 31 affected sessions between
them, because `missing_sidecar` records `stored_messages=0` by design and logs
neither the resolved `slot_<session>.bin` path nor the sidecar path.

## Scope

**In scope:** one extra field on the existing INFO line (behaviour-neutral) plus
tests/docs. **Out of scope:** any change to the credit decision, `prefix_matches`,
the TTL, or the sidecar format (those belong to LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E).

## Proposed change

1. In `proxy/proxy/slot_cache_ratio.py`, extend `log_seed_outcome()` with an
   optional `slot=<basename>` field (basename only — no absolute paths in logs)
   and pass the resolved candidate for `missing_sidecar` / `missing_snapshot`,
   so a later grep can tell which directory/endpoint variant resolved.
2. Cover every outcome branch in `proxy/tests/test_slot_cache_ratio_restore.py`.
3. Document the extra field in `proxy/docs/routing.md`.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every `slot_ratio_seed` line names the resolved snapshot basename (or the
  first candidate tried when none exists), covered by a unit test per branch.
- No behaviour change: the existing outcome vocabulary and credit decision are
  untouched, and the full seed-outcome test suite passes.
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` documents the field.

## Traceability

- discovered-from: LP-0MVK0E8C40035FG3 (verdict could not split the
  `missing_sidecar` sub-causes from logs)
- feeds: the post-fix re-measurement on LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E

# Slot-cache cleanup is non-recursive and never prunes orphan sidecars

## discovered-from: LP-0MVK0E8C40035FG3

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the retention job to prune stale slot snapshots **and**
their `.ratio.json` sidecars in every endpoint subdirectory, so disk usage stays
bounded and an orphaned sidecar can no longer make a session report
`slot_ratio_seed outcome=missing_snapshot` forever.

## Why (evidence)

While producing the seed-failure verdict on LP-0MVK0E8C40035FG3
(docs/dev/slot-ratio-seed-verdict-LP-0MVK0E8C40035FG3.md):

- `scripts/cleanup-slot-cache.sh` globs `"$SLOT_CACHE_DIR"/slot_*.bin` — **root
  only, non-recursive** — while every live snapshot is written to the
  per-endpoint subdirectory (`slot-cache/localhost-8080/`, LP-0MRPILSMW004T4H8).
  The last nightly run therefore logged `No slot files found in
  /home/rgardler/projects/llm/slot-cache` and the last cron summary was
  `0 files deleted`.
- The script does not know about `.ratio.json` at all, so pruning a snapshot
  leaves its sidecar behind. Measured 2026-10-29 10:50: **139 orphaned sidecars
  on disk with 0 `slot_*.bin` snapshots**, and 24.2 % of all seed decisions
  (1,086/4,488 over 155 h) were `missing_snapshot` because of exactly that
  state.

## Scope

**In scope:** retention correctness for the slot-cache directory. **Out of
scope:** the seed path's writer-side sidecar coupling (LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E) and
any credit logic.

## Proposed change

1. Make the snapshot scan recursive over endpoint subdirectories.
2. Delete a snapshot's `.ratio.json` sidecar whenever the snapshot is pruned
   (reuse `proxy.slot_cache_ratio.sidecar_path` semantics).
3. Add an orphan sweep: remove sidecars whose snapshot no longer exists and that
   are older than `--min-age-days`.
4. Extend `tests/test_cleanup_slot_cache.sh` with per-endpoint, sidecar-pairing
   and orphan-sweep cases.

## Acceptance criteria

- A snapshot under an endpoint subdirectory older than `--max-age-days` is
  deleted along with its sidecar, proven by a test.
- A sidecar whose snapshot is missing and which is older than `--min-age-days`
  is deleted, proven by a test; a recent orphan is kept.
- `--dry-run` lists every would-be deletion (snapshots and sidecars) and deletes
  nothing.
- Root-only layout keeps working (existing tests unchanged and green).

## Traceability

- discovered-from: LP-0MVK0E8C40035FG3
- related: LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E (writer-side sidecar coupling)
data.title: Slot-cache cleanup is non-recursive and never prunes orphan sidecars
